title: Switzerland Clears 57 Jurisdictions for 2028 Crypto Data Sharing
summary: Switzerland approved 57 potential partners for automatic crypto tax data sharing, including every European Union member state and the United Kingdom. Exchanges can begin in 2028 with jurisdictions that express interest and meet international standards for confidentiality and data security. Switzerla...
content:
Switzerland approved 57 potential partners for automatic crypto tax data sharing, including every European Union member state and the United Kingdom. Exchanges can begin in 2028 with jurisdictions that express interest and meet international standards for confidentiality and data security.

Key Takeaways

  • Switzerland approved 57 jurisdictions for potential crypto data exchanges.
  • Eligible partners could start exchanging crypto tax data in 2028.
  • Swiss authorities will check confidentiality and data security before sharing.

Switzerland Approves 57 Potential Partners

Switzerland’s Federal Council, the country’s seven-member executive body that oversees the federal administration, approved 57 potential partners on Nov. 25 for automatic exchanges of crypto tax information beginning in 2028. The list covers all European Union member states, the United Kingdom, and several Group of 20 countries. Each partner must express interest and meet international reporting standards.

The move is part of Switzerland’s plan to begin exchanging crypto information alongside other global asset management centers. The proposed crypto partner list won broad support in a 2024 consultation, and the council approved two notifications needed to carry out automatic information exchange.

Before sharing crypto or financial account data, the council will check whether the relevant partners meet standards set by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), an international organization that works with governments to develop policy standards. It will use a review process Parliament approved on Sept. 28 that covers confidentiality and data security.

What Crypto Providers Report

Under the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, covered service providers report identifying details, such as names and taxpayer identification numbers, to their domestic tax authority. The standard calls for aggregated transaction figures by asset, including purchases and sales involving traditional currencies, crypto-to-crypto trades, and qualifying transfers.

In the United Kingdom, crypto user reporting rules require providers to collect information on all users and submit details and transaction summaries for users who are tax residents of the U.K. or another participating jurisdiction. The first reports, covering 2026 activity, are due May 31, 2027.

The reporting framework gives tax authorities a standard way to obtain information on activity that may occur abroad. How crypto transactions are taxed depends on local law, which can treat sales, swaps, and income from activities such as staking differently.

Other Countries Set Their Own Exchange Timelines

Lithuania’s State Tax Inspectorate updated crypto customer reporting procedures to align with EU and OECD standards. The changes clarify which users fall under mandatory reporting and how crypto providers should collect identifying information, transaction records, and details about tax residency.

Germany’s parliament approved international crypto data sharing in October, with the first exchanges outside the EU planned for September 2027. Those exchanges would use records collected by providers in 2026.

Argentina has committed to exchanging crypto data under the same OECD framework by 2029. Before those exchanges begin, the country still has to finish domestic legal and administrative steps and put its international exchange arrangements in place.

Alongside the crypto decision, the Federal Council approved Armenia and Rwanda as partners under Switzerland’s financial account reporting program. A 2025 consultation showed broad support for expanding that program, and Switzerland expects to begin exchanging financial account information with both countries in 2028.

title: Sky proposes emergency vote on $25M transfer amid liquidity stress
summary: Sky’s Core Facilitator invoked the protocol’s emergency response process to expedite a vote rather than wait until the next scheduled vote on Dec. 3.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 26, 2026

Sky’s Core Facilitator invoked the protocol’s emergency response process to expedite a vote rather than wait until the next scheduled vote on Dec. 3.

Decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol Sky has proposed an emergency governance vote to expedite the transfer to 25 million USDS to the Sky Frontier Foundation to pay down debt amid a liquidity crunch that has left stUSDS depositors struggling to withdraw their funds for more than two weeks.

On Wednesday, Sky’s Core Facilitator said it was invoking the protocol’s emergency response process to accelerate debt repayments in a bid to ease liquidity pressure, rather than wait until the next scheduled vote on Dec. 3. Repaying loans funded by the stUSDS lending pool would free up capital for depositors to withdraw.

The liquidity crisis developed as depositors pulled funds from the stUSDS lending pool, which provides USDS loans to borrowers using staked SKY tokens as collateral. Bitquery found that daily withdrawals reached about $14.2 million on Nov. 10, exhausting available liquidity.

At the time of writing, Spark data showed that nearly all of the pool’s $158.48 million in assets had been lent out, leaving just $3,270 available for withdrawals.

On Monday, Sky co-founder Rune Christensen acknowledged that his borrowing had contributed to the withdrawal crunch, saying he still owed about 77 million USDS.

The proposal follows a Sky lender’s call to use up to $50 million in protocol reserves to purchase SKY tokens from borrowers, enabling them to repay loans and free up withdrawal liquidity.

title: 1Password hacker stole customer names and emails, but vaults safe
summary: The password manager, which is used by millions of people to store their login credentials, said customer vaults were unaffected by the breach.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 26, 2026

The password manager, which is used by millions of people to store their login credentials, said customer vaults were unaffected by the breach.

Password manager 1Password disclosed Wednesday that an attacker stole names and email addresses belonging to some customers after breaking into its backend systems.

Customer vaults and their contents were not affected, but 1Password said the breach could lead to phishing attempts in the form of unexpected emails, texts or calls.

The company said it began investigating last Thursday after discovering signs an attacker had gained access to an employee’s GitHub account. The attacker used the account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, allowing them to extract customer data.

“This data included customer names and email addresses, in addition to non-secret internal metadata about the account. At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker,” the company said.

The password manager lets people store passwords for different websites and apps in one encrypted vault. 1Password says millions of people and more than 200,000 businesses use its service.

The company also partnered with crypto wallet provider Phantom in 2022 to let users save their wallet passwords and recovery phrases in 1Password.

Following the attack, 1Password said it has since disabled the affected GitHub account, removed the attackers’ access, rotated all internal credentials potentially exposed, among other measures. It also said it has not found any evidence of user account takeovers or compromises from the attack.

Related: Chainalysis says breach exposed password hashes and live tokens

title: Senate Democrats urge SEC to scrap crypto, tokenized stock exemptions
summary: US Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Van Hollen, among others, have taken aim at two recent SEC efforts to ease regulatory requirements for the crypto industry.
content:
US Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Van Hollen have urged the US Securities and Exchange Commission to drop a proposal that would allow eligible crypto projects to raise funds from US investors without registering their offerings and revoke an exemption for tokenized stock platforms.

In two letters sent to SEC Chair Paul Atkins on Tuesday, the Democratic lawmakers argued that the agency had exceeded its statutory authority in both cases and that the moves will put investors at risk.

“Together, the letters raise concerns about the SEC’s efforts to carve out special treatment for crypto assets and tokenized securities at the expense of investor protections and market integrity,” they said.

Both SEC measures drew crypto industry support, as they came at a time when the CLARITY Act struggled to advance in Congress. The Regulation Crypto Assets was first introduced in August when the landmark crypto legislation was stalled, while the tokenized stock exemption came out in September, two days after the CLARITY Act fell short of the 60 votes needed to advance.

Senators warn of a “shadow stock market”

The letters also come just a day after OKXICE, a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange, launched a round-the-clock trading venue for tokenized US securities under the exemption on Monday.

The tokenized stock exemption allows qualifying platforms to offer blockchain-based trading of tokenized US stocks without registering as exchanges.

SEC lists four other entities that intend to use the exemption, including TSV LLC (which commenced operation in early November), Kephas Corporation d/b/a Perpetuals.com, Formation Securities LLC and Fairmint TSV LLC.

Van Hollen, Warren and two other senators urged the SEC to withdraw the order, warning the order could create a “shadow stock market” that falls outside of regulatory protections.

“We are particularly troubled by the order’s sweeping exemption of TSVs from fundamental registration requirements,” they said.

They also argued the order places an “unreasonable burden” on publicly traded companies by allowing third parties to tokenize their securities unless the issuer objects within 30 days.

“This effectively establishes an opt-out regime in which companies must continuously monitor tokenization activity and respond to potentially numerous requests from different platforms to prevent unauthorized trading of tokenized versions of their shares.”

Related: Trump’s SEC nominee Johnson backs formal rulemaking for tokenized stock trading

The senators also argued venues are exempt from rules requiring them to display their best prices to traders. “These protections are foundational to the fairness and efficiency of our equity markets,” they said.

Atkins previously described the five-year exemption as an interim measure to allow onchain trading of certain US stocks while the agency considers longer-term rules.

Senators target SEC’s proposed fundraising exemption

In a separate letter, Warren, Van Hollen and Senator Tina Smith urged the SEC to withdraw its Regulation Crypto Assets Proposal, arguing that the proposal only serves to help crypto assets “escape” from the SEC’s regulatory regime.

The proposal would allow eligible crypto projects to raise up to $5 million over four years under a startup exemption or up to $75 million in a 12-month period under a separate fundraising exemption, without registering the offerings with the SEC.

The senators argued these exemptions would let crypto issuers raise money without prior SEC review, particularly the $5 million startup exemption, which would allow early-stage projects to raise money without providing financial statements.

“The proposal rationalizes the startup exemption with the idea that these offerings are from startups, and its only limitation is a $5 million offering cap. However, the exemption does nothing to actually protect investors – it simply means that the SEC is willing for investors to be defrauded in $5 million increments,” they said.

The SEC has previously said that the exemptions would require issuers to give investors written disclosures, and federal anti-fraud and anti-manipulation rules would still apply.

Cointelegraph reached out to the SEC for comment.

title: Fidelity Files for Chainlink ETF. What Does It Mean for LINK?
summary: Key takeaways Fidelity has filed to launch a Chainlink ETF (ticker FLNK) that would hold LINK directly and list on Nasdaq, but the filing is preliminary with no launch date or final fee. The fund would not stake its LINK, so shareholders would not receive staking rewards. Fidelity would enter a mark...
content:
Key takeaways

  • Fidelity has filed to launch a Chainlink ETF (ticker FLNK) that would hold LINK directly and list on Nasdaq, but the filing is preliminary with no launch date or final fee.
  • The fund would not stake its LINK, so shareholders would not receive staking rewards.
  • Fidelity would enter a market that already has Grayscale (GLNK) and Bitwise (CLNK) LINK funds, and Charles Schwab offers direct LINK trading.
  • A new listing does not automatically mean new LINK buying: only sustained net creations add to the fund’s holdings.
  • Shares outstanding, LINK held and net creations after launch will show whether demand is genuinely new.

Fidelity’s Chainlink ETF proposal would hold LINK directly and trade on Nasdaq if it clears the remaining steps. The proposed Fidelity Chainlink Fund, described in a November 25 registration statement, would use the ticker FLNK, although the filing is preliminary and no launch date or final annual fee has been provided.

The larger question is not whether Wall Street can package LINK. It already has. The question is whether Fidelity can attract fresh demand for the token rather than divide the existing market among another set of fund shares.

Fidelity’s Filing Is Specific About What Investors Would Own

The proposed fund would hold LINK, not a basket of blockchain companies or derivatives intended to mimic LINK’s price. Its objective is to follow the token’s U.S. dollar performance, less expenses and liabilities. The prospectus identifies Anchorage Digital Bank, BitGo Bank & Trust and Coinbase Custody as custodians, with the trust intending to hold its LINK on Ethereum.

Fidelity also lays out how the price would be measured. Its proposed reference rate uses prices from eligible LINK spot markets, with a volume-weighted median methodology calculated every 15 seconds using rolling 60-minute market data. That is a mechanism for valuing the assets. It is not a guarantee that fund shares will trade at precisely the reported value when markets are thin or volatile.

Nor is this a yield product. The filing states plainly: “The Trust will not stake its LINK.” Shareholders would not receive staking rewards through the fund. They would be buying securities designed to reflect an underlying token’s price, not a wallet balance they can use in Chainlink services.

That distinction matters because the company’s use of Chainlink technology elsewhere is a separate story. NewsBTC has previously reported on Chainlink infrastructure used with Fidelity’s tokenized FILQ fund. An investment vehicle that owns LINK is not evidence of increased demand for Chainlink’s oracle services, and using the network’s technology does not automatically mean buying its token.

Fidelity Would Enter a Market That Already Has LINK Funds

This is not the first attempt to make LINK available through conventional securities accounts. Grayscale’s Chainlink Trust ETF, trading as GLNK, had a share creation and redemption program in place from December 2025, according to its SEC disclosures. The Bitwise Chainlink ETF, CLNK, also appeared in a January 2026 Nasdaq information circular.

And fund shares are not the only conventional route. In November, NewsBTC covered Charles Schwab’s rollout of direct LINK trading to eligible crypto clients. These routes do different things, but they establish a useful baseline: access is no longer the same problem it was when crypto products were confined to specialist exchanges.

Fidelity’s possible advantage is distribution. Its name and brokerage relationships may reach customers who would not open a crypto wallet or buy LINK on a trading platform. That is a credible reason the filing matters. But branding, however recognizable, cannot tell investors how much money will arrive once trading begins.

There is also the price of access. The preliminary prospectus leaves the sponsor’s annual fee blank. Until that figure is settled, it is impossible to make an honest cost comparison with competing LINK products. For investors choosing between wrappers around the same token, fees, trading spreads and the gap between share prices and net asset value deserve more attention than a new ticker.

A New ETF Listing Would Not Automatically Mean New LINK Buying

The mechanics are worth getting right. The proposed trust would issue and redeem large blocks of shares through authorized participants, using cash or LINK under procedures described in the filing. Everyday investors would generally trade the shares on an exchange instead of placing orders with the trust.

Those are two different markets. When one investor sells an existing fund share to another, the trade does not by itself require the trust to acquire more LINK. Sustained net creations can increase a fund’s underlying holdings. Redemptions can do the reverse. A rising share price, meanwhile, may reflect a higher LINK price rather than additional tokens entering custody.

That is why the announcement alone provides no evidence of fresh institutional inflows. The Form S-1 is a plan, not a subscription report. It does not tell us how much outside capital will be committed, what portion might come from rival products, or whether investor interest will survive a difficult crypto market.

There is a fair counterargument. Fidelity could appeal to a materially different pool of investors and grow total demand rather than simply redistribute it. The filing establishes a possible channel for that to happen. It does not establish the outcome.

What Would Actually Change the Assessment?

First, the registration statement must become effective and the proposed Nasdaq listing must move forward. The final prospectus should also resolve the missing fee and other commercial details. Those are immediate milestones, not formalities to be assumed away.

If the product launches, the more revealing evidence will arrive afterward: the number of LINK held, changes in shares outstanding, sustained net creations or redemptions, trading liquidity and discounts or premiums to net asset value. Comparisons with existing LINK funds would help separate fresh demand from investors moving between products.

Until those figures exist, the sensible interpretation is narrow. Fidelity wants to sell investors exposure to Chainlink through a familiar brokerage format. Whether that changes the market for LINK is still an open question, and one that a filing cannot answer.

title: Coinbase CEO Says Investors Swap Bitcoin for Big IPOs, Then Rotate Back
summary: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said investors have historically moved money out of bitcoin to buy into major initial public offerings and returned afterward. He argued that bitcoin remains as important as ever for investors who expect higher inflation and more money printing. Armstrong Describes How I...
content:
Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said investors have historically moved money out of bitcoin to buy into major initial public offerings and returned afterward. He argued that bitcoin remains as important as ever for investors who expect higher inflation and more money printing.

Key Takeaways

  • Armstrong described investors returning to bitcoin after large IPOs.
  • Spot bitcoin ETFs lost $306.42 million before Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut.
  • Coinbase is building accounts, payment tools, and markets for AI agents.

Armstrong Describes How Investors Move Around Big IPOs

Brian Armstrong, chief executive officer of crypto exchange Coinbase (Nasdaq: COIN), described on Nov. 25 how investors have returned to bitcoin after shifting money into large initial public offerings (IPOs). He paired that observation with a conditional case for holding bitcoin during a period of rising inflation.

Armstrong wrote on X:

“If you believe there will be more inflation and printing of money in the future, Bitcoin is as important as it’s ever been. Historically, people rotate out of it to participate in large IPOs, and then rotate back.”

The price history behind bitcoin’s role as an inflation hedge has been mixed. Bitcoin’s supply is capped at 21 million coins, but its price fell during two of three U.S. inflation shocks examined in a comparison of how the asset performed alongside other investments.

Bitcoin and ETF Flows Around Major IPOs

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs recorded $306.42 million in net outflows on Nov. 18, the day before Anthropic began trading, with seven funds posting withdrawals. Blackrock’s Ishares Bitcoin Trust accounted for $148.66 million.

Bitcoin traded near $80,000 in late October, up 26% from its level at Spacex’s debut in June, after falling around that listing. The cryptocurrency has since dropped to about $60,090 as of Nov. 25, below that June starting point.

Anthropic (Nasdaq: ANT) began trading Nov. 19 and closed its public offering the following day. The IPO generated about $93.5 billion in gross proceeds, including shares sold under the underwriters’ fully exercised option for additional shares. Anthropic received about $91.6 billion of that total.

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse attributed part of the crypto sell-off to investors raising cash for Anthropic’s IPO in a Nov. 19 interview. He cited the rebound after Spacex went public and projected that the broader crypto market could recover after Anthropic’s listing.

Coinbase Builds Financial Tools for AI Agents

In a separate X post, Armstrong outlined Coinbase’s plans for AI agents on Nov. 24. He described agents as a way for individuals to access guidance when making financial decisions.

The Coinbase founder proposed using specialized AI models with publicly available weights, the parameters that determine how a model responds. He argued that models tailored to specific tasks could outperform leading general-purpose models on those tasks and be assembled into teams that beat those models overall.

Armstrong drew on economist Friedrich Hayek’s work on how prices convey information across an economy. He applied that idea to marketplaces where people and AI agents could use prices to guide decisions.

Armstrong wrote on X:

“This is what Coinbase is building: financial accounts, payment rails, and marketplaces for people and their agents to coordinate in this new economy.”

title: Bitcoin Could Sink to $48,500 if It Breaks Below $53K, Analyst Warns
summary: Bitcoin could fall to $48,500 if it stays below its roughly $53,000 realized price, a strategist warned. The analyst still expects bitcoin to revisit $72,000 to $80,000 by year-end. Bitcoin’s $53K Cost Basis Marks a Downside Threshold Matt Mena, senior crypto research strategist at crypto exchange-t...
content:
Bitcoin could fall to $48,500 if it stays below its roughly $53,000 realized price, a strategist warned. The analyst still expects bitcoin to revisit $72,000 to $80,000 by year-end.

Key Takeaways

  • A sustained break below $53,000 could put $48,500 in play.
  • A move that holds above $65,000 would support the $55,000 bottom case.
  • A 21shares strategist expects bitcoin to revisit $72,000 to $80,000 in 2026.

Bitcoin’s $53K Cost Basis Marks a Downside Threshold

Matt Mena, senior crypto research strategist at crypto exchange-traded product issuer 21shares, warned on Nov. 25 that a sustained break below $53,000 could send bitcoin back into the $40,000s. He outlined the downside scenario in comments supplied to Bitcoin.com News after the U.S. inflation release.

Mena wrote:

“Bitcoin’s realized price, or the average cost basis of all bitcoin in circulation, is roughly $53K, and that’s our line in the sand for the level we must hold, or the chances of seeing bitcoin in the $40Ks again come into play.”

In its analysis of bitcoin’s sell-off, 21shares put realized price at about $53,250 on Nov. 22. The measure averages the prices at which circulating coins last moved onchain. The firm expected rallies to fade until stablecoin supply and inflows to exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recovered.

The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis reported that the October PCE price index rose 3.8% from a year earlier. Core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation, which excludes food and energy, increased 3.3% year over year and 0.3% from September. The strategist viewed the core reading as higher than expected.

The analyst said bitcoin briefly fell 1% after the release and traded near $58,000, a level he identified as support. He put total crypto market capitalization above $2 trillion and said the core inflation reading complicated the Federal Reserve’s task heading into 2027.

Bitcoin stood at $60,661 at 8:34 p.m. EST on Nov. 25, up 2.22% over 24 hours after rebounding from a low of about $57,320 to a high near $61,100 in that period. The price remained down 4.09% from $63,244.87 over the past week and 24.50% from $80,344.74 over the past month.

Why the Analyst Is Watching $48,500

The analyst explained:

“A sustained break below it could put $48.5K bitcoin in play, marking the August 2024 Yen-Carry Trade unwind and a resistance level bitcoin initially struggled to break on the historical debut of spot BTC ETFs in the US.”

Bitcoin traded below $49,000 during the August 2024 market sell-off, about a week after briefly touching $70,000. Japan’s Nikkei recorded its steepest daily drop since 1987 as the rout spread across stock and cryptocurrency markets.

The Bank for International Settlements found that an unwind of leveraged trades amplified the broader sell-off. Investors had borrowed cheaply in yen, and a stronger yen put pressure on those positions.

The launch of the first U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs provided the other reference point for Mena’s downside level. U.S. regulators approved 11 spot funds in January 2024, giving investors a way to gain bitcoin exposure through brokerage accounts.

21shares Strategist Sees a Year-End Rebound

A bitcoin rally and reversal took the price to $64,505 on Nov. 23 before it slipped below $61,000 that day. The gains faded within hours of Nvidia (Nasdaq: NVDA) announcing the return of Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.

The strategist noted:

“A sustained move above $65K would signal that an uptrend is taking shape and strengthen the case that $55K marked the cycle bottom.”

On Nov. 21, the intraday low for bitcoin was $55,106. Looking ahead to December, the analyst cited an average gain of 7.65% since 2011 and said bitcoin had never recorded three losing Decembers in a row over that period. He also pointed to losses in each of the past two Decembers.

Crude oil hit a three-month low earlier in the week, according to the strategist, who said sustained lower energy prices could ease pressure on headline inflation. He saw a softer November inflation reading as a potential boost for a December rebound.

He concluded:

“We take the stance that we will see a $72K-$80K bitcoin again in 2026.”

title: AI labs likely sitting on cryptography ‘bombshells,’ computer scientist says
summary: AI is driving a massive wave of mathematical breakthroughs which could have implications for cryptography.
content:
Theoretical computer scientist Scott Aaronson says leading AI laboratories are likely sitting on undisclosed breakthroughs in cryptography.

In a blog post on Wednesday, Aaronson, a former OpenAI researcher and professor at The University of Texas at Austin, warned that algorithms emerging from AI-driven mathematical advances will eventually break currently deployed cryptosystems.

“I’m virtually certain, from multiple reliable sources, that the AI labs are now sitting on one or more bombshells in that area,” Aaronson said. “However, until I either see details or hear directly from someone at a lab, I feel much, much less confident about the specific nature of those bombshells.”

The remarks add to concerns that AI’s accelerating mathematical capabilities could eventually undermine the cryptography used to secure crypto wallets and blockchain transactions. Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin and researcher Justin Drake raised those concerns in October.

AI tackles longstanding mathematical problems

Recent weeks have illustrated the pace at which AI has been able to overcome previously unsolvable math problems.

On Friday, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge released an AI-assisted proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics.

Alpöge developed it with an unreleased version of Claude over roughly six weeks, spanning 17 million lines of Lean code. The proof was later verified as correct by Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative.

Days later, both Anthropic and OpenAI released proofs of the VP versus VNP conjecture, described as an algebraic cousin of P versus NP, another major unsolved problem in theoretical computer science.

In October, OpenAI released 722 AI-generated math manuscripts covering 372 problem areas on GitHub, which has since been nicknamed the “mathocalypse.”

“This past week — is very much like I would’ve always imagined the beginning of an AI singularity to look and feel like,” said Aaronson.

Related: AI poses greater threat to Bitcoin than quantum computing, Swan founder says

One of the rumors, according to Aaronson, is that one or both of the AI labs have solved “Factoring in P,” referring to a polynomial-time factoring algorithm — a breakthrough that could threaten RSA cryptography.

AI commentator Andrew Curran and Carnegie Mellon University machine learning researcher Aran Nayebi also said they had heard similar rumors.

Aaronson, however, declined to offer any insight on the idea that ECDSA, a digital signature scheme used by Bitcoin, had been broken.

“Crucially, don’t want the cryptography part of the story to overshadow the intellectual enormity of what’s happening,” said Aaronson.

“If, in these days of long-prophesied revelation and wonders and terrors, your main worry is your Bitcoin wallet, then go somewhere else for rumors about whether or not ECDSA is broken or whatever. I don’t have what you’re looking for here.”

title: Canaan Expands Nordic Bitcoin Mining Heat Network to Nearly 8,000 Homes
summary: Bitcoin mining equipment manufacturer Canaan announced Wednesday that it secured two additional orders for 430 hydro-cooled Avalon mining units in the Nordic region, expanding its district heating portfolio to nearly 12 megawatts (MW), with the potential to heat nearly 8,000 homes. Canaan Secures Tw...
content:
Bitcoin mining equipment manufacturer Canaan announced Wednesday that it secured two additional orders for 430 hydro-cooled Avalon mining units in the Nordic region, expanding its district heating portfolio to nearly 12 megawatts (MW), with the potential to heat nearly 8,000 homes.

Key Takeaways

  • Canaan secured orders for 430 customized Avalon A1566HA-500T miners, representing 215 PH/s of aggregate computing capacity.
  • The new deployments build upon an 8 MW Nordic district heating initiative announced in May 2026.
  • Both orders came from existing customers following competitive vendor selection processes, signaling continued commercial interest in bitcoin mining heat recovery.

Canaan Secures Two More Nordic Hash-to-Heat Contracts

Six months after Canaan announced its initial 8 MW Nordic district heating project, the Nasdaq-listed company (CAN) is expanding its regional presence with two new equipment orders from repeat customers, according to an announcement shared with Bitcoin.com News on Nov. 25, 2026.

The orders comprise 430 customized Avalon A1566HA-500T units, each delivering 500 terahash per second (TH/s) of computing power. Collectively, the machines represent 215 petahash per second (PH/s) and are engineered to produce hot water at approximately 80 degrees Celsius (176 degrees Fahrenheit).

The recovered thermal energy will feed directly into existing district heating networks at two separate locations, replacing heat that would otherwise be generated through fuel combustion.

As Bitcoin.com News reported on May 19, Canaan’s original Nordic initiative encompassed 920 hydro-cooled mining machines. An initial 2 MW installation consisting of 228 units was already operational, prompting a subsequent order for another 692 machines representing 6 MW of additional capacity.

At the time, Canaan estimated the original installation could supply heating to approximately 2,800 homes. With Wednesday’s announcement, the combined equipment count reaches 1,350 units, while the estimated residential heating potential has nearly tripled.

According to the mining machine maker Canaan, the latest business followed more than four months of technical and commercial discussions. One customer reportedly selected the manufacturer based on its experience with equipment already operating at its first site, citing dependable performance, responsive service and technical support.

“Securing two district heating orders from existing customers across the Nordic region is an encouraging validation of our computing and heat-reuse solutions,” Canaan Chairman and CEO Nangeng Zhang said.

The manufacturer did not identify either customer, disclose the financial terms of the agreements or provide a timetable for completing the new installations.

Bitcoin Mining Heat Recovery Gains Commercial Traction

Unlike conventional boilers, which consume energy primarily to generate heat, hydro-cooled bitcoin mining systems produce two economically useful outputs from a single electricity input. Specialized chips perform computational work while circulating coolant captures thermal energy that would otherwise dissipate into the environment.

The Nordic region offers particularly fertile ground for this model. Established district heating infrastructure allows centralized thermal energy producers to distribute hot water across residential and commercial properties without requiring individual buildings to install specialized mining equipment.

Canaan’s system also allows operators to adjust computing loads in response to electricity prices and grid conditions. The modular architecture enables individual machines to undergo maintenance without necessarily interrupting the entire installation’s thermal output, an important consideration for utilities responsible for dependable residential heating.

Recovering heat without burning natural gas or heating oil on-site eliminates associated local combustion emissions. However, the broader environmental benefits depend partly on the electricity generation mix, alongside the type of fuel displaced and the amount of thermal energy ultimately consumed.

Canaan also has pursued heat recovery applications beyond district heating, including residential Avalon solo miners and heaters and a greenhouse heating initiative in Manitoba, Canada. These projects illustrate how specialized mining hardware can serve markets outside conventional cryptocurrency production.

Perhaps the most commercially significant aspect of Wednesday’s announcement is that both orders originated from returning customers rather than first-time buyers. Although Canaan has not disclosed the underlying economics, repeat purchases following real-world deployments suggest hash-to-heat technology is progressing beyond experimental installations. Its enduring commercial test will be whether mining-powered heating can consistently compete with established thermal energy sources.

summary:

title: Top 7 Signs to Watch That Could Signal a Bitcoin Price Reversal
summary: As sentiment around bitcoin turns overwhelmingly negative once again, analysts point to seven signals that could indicate the market is ready to turn higher. However, the likelihood of many of these signals appearing remains low for now. It’s also anyone’s guess when these changes might occur, if at...
content:
As sentiment around bitcoin turns overwhelmingly negative once again, analysts point to seven signals that could indicate the market is ready to turn higher. However, the likelihood of many of these signals appearing remains low for now. It’s also anyone’s guess when these changes might occur, if at all.

Key Takeaways

  • Sustained spot ETF inflows, a positive Coinbase premium, growing spot demand, steady stablecoin supply and stronger derivatives activity would signal that buyers are returning.
  • Falling realized losses, recovering long-term holder SOPR, lighter selling and no new lows despite extreme fear would suggest capitulation is ending.
  • Bitcoin moving back above $60,000 and through the $62,000-$66,000 range, backed by a softer Fed, stronger stocks and a weaker dollar, could confirm a trend reversal.

At the time of writing, BTC is trading near $59,500 after hitting a new cycle low of about $55,100 on Nov. 21. It is down around 26% over 30 days, about 32% from a year ago and about 53% from its all-time high of about $126,000 on Oct. 6, 2025. Previous bear markets saw much deeper drawdowns, and many analysts expect further downside before the trend changes, as the slump is also hitting stock and gold markets. Glassnode, for example, says another drop of about 10%, to the realized price near $53,200, would not be unusual. Bitcoin has increasingly become a prisoner of external factors unrelated to the asset itself or the Bitcoin network. Analysts also point to these external factors as key indicators to watch for a possible trend reversal.

Signal 1: U.S. Buyers Come Back

This is perhaps one of the most straightforward and trivial signals analysts point to: U.S. buyers returning to the market. These buyers would still need a reason to start buying BTC again, but at least two data points could help identify a shift in sentiment: spot BTC exchange-traded fund (ETF) flows and the Coinbase premium. While ETF flows provide a clear indication of whether U.S. institutions and wealth managers are buying or selling bitcoin, the Coinbase premium shows whether buying demand in the U.S. is stronger than on offshore exchanges. When bitcoin trades at a higher price on Coinbase than on offshore exchanges, the positive premium indicates stronger U.S. buying pressure.

So far in November, U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs have recorded net inflows on only two days, while net outflows reached about $4.94 billion through Nov. 24, based on Farside Investors data. That sets a monthly record, surpassing June’s roughly $4.51 billion.

According to 10x Research, this looks like steady de-risking by allocators rather than a single capitulation event, and “there is no sign yet of the selling fading.” These analysts said this is the fourth time since early 2025 that the ETFs have lost $4 billion to $6 billion over 30 days. Each of the previous three episodes coincided with a roughly $20,000 drop in bitcoin’s price.

Meanwhile, bitcoin has traded at a discount on Coinbase compared with offshore exchanges every day for 80 days. Analysts at Cryptoquant concluded that “US investors aren’t buying this dip.”

“Until the ETF outflows stop, every bounce will run into sellers,” on-chain analyst Axel Adler Jr. said, while ecoinometrics concurred that “Without inflows returning, there is little reason to expect the correction to end.”

“Historically, it has taken months for demand to recover from events like this,” added Cryptoquant CEO Ki Young Ju.

Based on these analysts’ comments, the signs to watch include several consecutive days of ETF inflows, a slowdown in weekly outflows (which 10x Research says remain at or above their 30-day average), net buying on Coinbase accompanied by a positive Coinbase premium, and a stabilization in global bitcoin exchange-traded product holdings.

According to analysts, a softer Fed or stabilizing stock markets could help bring U.S. buyers back. However, U.S. investors account for only part of global demand. Buying pressure could also return from other countries for reasons that are currently unknown.

Signal 2: Bitcoin Wins Back Key Levels

If bitcoin’s price moves decisively above $60,000 and then reclaims the 62,000-66,000 range, this could signal a reversal, according to Glassnode. Conversely, a convincing break below $60,000, which we might be seeing this week, could push the price toward $53,200, where conditions might, in theory, become more favorable for a recovery.

This theory relates to the “realized price” metric, which shows the average price at which each bitcoin last moved, roughly representing the market’s average cost basis.

Different analysts currently put the realized price between $53,000 and $54,000. According to Glassnode, every previous bear market saw bitcoin close below this level, but the current one has not yet done so. Glassnode’s data also shows a cluster of leveraged long positions near $51,500, just below the realized price, adding to the downside risks if the price keeps falling. A drop into the low $50,000s would be consistent with how past bear markets ended, but it would not necessarily mark the bottom. Applied to today’s levels, Glassnode says the lows of past bear markets would translate to roughly $37,000 to $45,000.

Additionally, analysts are watching the 200-day moving average, currently around $72,400, and the 365-day moving average, at $75,450. According to Cryptoquant head of research Julio Moreno, trading below these levels puts bitcoin back in a bearish regime.

Signal 3: Sellers Capitulate and Become Exhausted

While the market currently lacks buyers, sellers could eventually reach a similar point of exhaustion, with everyone willing to sell having already done so. However, every newly breached price level could bring another wave of sellers into the market.

Analysts at Glassnode and Cryptoquant agree that capitulation has already started. The main question is how long it will last. So far, long-term holders, defined as those who have held BTC for at least five months, have realized most of the losses on bitcoin between mid-April and mid-November. According to Glassnode, the same happened around the lows of 2015, 2018, and 2022, with each of those bear markets bottoming during or near such a period. Glassnode notes that these periods lasted for months in the past, while Moreno says bottoming periods tend to last at least two months.

However, “Sellers are still capitulating, rather than exhausting,” Rekt Capital said on Nov. 20, a day before bitcoin hit a new low, while K33 Research added on Nov. 24 that the lack of a trading volume surge raises the question of whether the selling climax is still ahead.

Once sellers run out of coins to sell, even a relatively small increase in demand could push bitcoin higher. It could also trigger a short squeeze, potentially accelerating the price move. Still, a squeeze alone does not last: bitcoin’s price jump on the Nvidia news on Nov. 23 faded within hours.

In the meantime, signs to watch include long-term holder SOPR, which compares the price at which coins are sold with the price at which they were bought, recovering above 1. Bitcoin.com News, citing Cryptoquant data, has identified this as the next test. Other signs include Glassnode’s realized-loss measure peaking and falling while the price holds above the June low, and weekly seller volume, which Rekt Capital tracks, peaking and then shrinking.

Signal 4: Fresh Money Arrives via Spot Demand and Stablecoins

Cryptoquant’s total demand growth measure could help identify a reversal. It estimates how much BTC is being bought in the spot market and through perpetual futures. Changes in stablecoin supply, which market data aggregators track, could provide another indication of returning liquidity.

Earlier in November, total bitcoin demand growth, combining spot and perpetual futures, fell below -400,000 BTC on a 30-day basis, marking the fastest contraction since July 1, according to Cryptoquant. Its head of research, Julio Moreno, said the first positive sign would be the 30-day measure moving back toward zero, driven by spot buying rather than new leverage in perpetual futures.

RugaResearch, 21Shares and Grayscale also point to shrinking stablecoin supply. According to 21Shares, total stablecoin supply contracted by $10.7 billion after the Oct. 29 Binance hack, while stablecoin balances held on exchanges fell 15%. Leo Ruga of RugaResearch wants to see this decline slow, followed by the 60-day change moving toward zero and turning positive. However, the analyst said a rally could start even before that happens, as stablecoins represent only one part of market liquidity.

Signal 5: Leverage Is Cleared and Bitcoin Bets Turn More Bullish

Signs worth watching include open interest, which measures the total value of outstanding derivatives positions, rising alongside the price. Ideally, spot buying rather than new leverage would drive the move, a condition Moreno also stresses. In the options market, a declining put-to-call ratio and lower premiums on puts would help. A pickup in CME futures open interest would also be positive, as K33 Research says it has fallen to a yearly low.

For now, the market is sending mixed signals about what might come next. According to Glassnode, an average of 1.7 puts traded for every call in the options market over seven days last week, the highest ratio since June 2022. This indicates that bearish positions dominate this market. Glassnode notes that a similar reading in June 2022 coincided with a price low, although the final bottom of that bear market came five months later. At the same time, Glassnode says that after BTC dropped toward $55,000, nearly 90% of the long positions between the price and the realized price were wiped out. According to the firm, this is a positive sign because little forced selling remains above the realized price. As mentioned above, a cluster of long positions remains near $51,500.

Signal 6: The Fed, Stocks and the Dollar Stop Pushing BTC Down

With the next U.S. Federal Reserve (Fed) rate decision approaching on Dec. 9, incoming economic data, stock market movements, U.S. dollar strength, and comments from Fed governors will continue fueling speculation about what might happen that day. At the time of writing, almost the entire market expects a quarter-point rate hike.

If the Fed softens its stance, for example, by signaling that December’s hike could be the last, this could help risk assets such as stocks and bitcoin. A declining probability of a January hike would be an early sign.

According to 10x Research, investors are currently pricing in a hawkish Fed that could still raise rates three more times. Adler Jr. summarized the situation by noting that there are currently no signs of an imminent rate cut, oil remains expensive, government debt continues to rise, and almost everything except cash looks risky.

At the same time, stocks resumed their downtrend this week, the U.S. Dollar Index rose to levels last seen in April 2025, according to K33 Research, and the 10-year Treasury yield remained near 4.9%. A reversal in these trends could support bitcoin’s price. One sign to watch, according to Glassnode, is bitcoin outperforming the Nasdaq on days when stocks rise.

Signal 7: Changes in Extreme Fear

While market sentiment usually follows the price, metrics such as the Crypto Fear & Greed Index, Cryptoquant’s analyst tracker, and changes in the options market are still worth watching. For example, if fear remains extreme but the price stops making new lows, some investors might interpret this as a buying signal.

Meanwhile, if fear eases only because the price rises on short covering, without confirmation from the other signals, this would provide weaker evidence of a market reversal and a potential buying opportunity.

For now, most prediction market participants still bet that BTC will fall below $55,000 by the end of this year. However, as a recent Bitcoin.com News analysis noted, the prevailing market mood has often been a poor guide to where the price goes next.

As Charles Edwards, founder of Capriole Investments, put it, you only know peak pessimism has passed after it is over.

A Reversal May Still Be Months Away

At the time of writing, most of the signals above have yet to turn positive, apart from the clearing of leverage and the start of capitulation. As reported by Bitcoin.com News, worst-case scenarios still include a drop toward $50,000 or $40,000, while some analysts even see a fall to $10,000 if stocks crash. What’s more, according to Glassnode, every past bear market ended with the price closing below the realized price, which the current one has not done yet.

If this bear market follows the same pattern, bitcoin would fall below roughly $53,200. Glassnode notes that this bear market has so far been shallower than previous ones, lending some support to the “this time is different” argument. However, the firm adds that if the current cycle is not different after all, it expects lower prices.

Analyst and trader Benjamin Cowen also pointed to a bear market checklist: bitcoin usually falls in the fourth quarter of a midterm election year, after the first rate hike of a hiking cycle, and after a September rate hike in a midterm year. It also usually falls below the realized price and reaches the lower “balanced price.” Finally, it bottoms when his on-chain risk metric falls below 0.1. The metric stood at 0.167 when Cowen published his post.

Meanwhile, trader Route 2 FI pointed out that more than 400 days have now passed since BTC’s all-time high last year.

“That makes this the longest $BTC bear market on record, even though the drawdown, around 55% at the June low, is the mildest one yet,” the trader said on Nov. 20, before BTC slightly deepened its year-to-date drawdown again.

The Next Catalyst Will Be Clear in Hindsight

The market also still seems to be struggling to find a catalyst for bitcoin’s next bull run. However, entrepreneur and bitcoin investor Charlie Shrem noted that the reasons behind past bull markets are usually identified only after the fact. Replying to Vinny Lingham, who asked for the bull case, Shrem also said bull markets emerge as the price makes progressively higher lows, which bitcoin is not doing yet.

In the meantime, watch the seven signals described above for possible signs that the next bull market is starting. Maybe this time we can even get a catalyst directly related to bitcoin and its adoption, rather than relying solely on external factors.

title: Switzerland clears 57 jurisdictions for crypto tax data sharing
summary: The move paves the way for Switzerland to exchange crypto tax data with foreign authorities starting in 2028 as part of a global effort to combat tax evasion.
content:
Switzerland’s Federal Council has approved 57 potential partner jurisdictions for the automatic exchange of information on crypto assets starting in 2028, a move that would expand tax authorities’ access to information on taxpayers’ crypto activity across borders.

According to a Wednesday announcement, the approved jurisdictions include all European Union member states, the United Kingdom and several G20 countries. Switzerland will only share information with jurisdictions that express interest and meet international standards for confidentiality and data security.

Switzerland had initially planned to introduce crypto tax reporting requirements in 2026 but delayed implementation by at least a year as lawmakers had yet to determine which jurisdictions the country would exchange information with. Under the revised timeline, crypto service providers could begin collecting data as early as Jan. 1, 2027, with the first exchanges between tax authorities taking place in 2028.

The reporting requirements fall under the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s (OECD) Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), which aims to combat tax evasion by requiring crypto exchanges and other covered service providers to report customer identities, tax residency and transaction data to tax authorities.

The crypto reporting framework is designed to supplement Switzerland’s existing system for exchanging financial account information and close gaps in tax transparency, according to the State Secretariat for International Finance. Switzerland introduced the legal framework for that system in 2017 and exchanged financial account data with 113 jurisdictions in 2026.

Global crypto tax reporting expands

The European Union introduced crypto reporting requirements under the OECD framework in January, with the first international exchanges of information scheduled for 2027. As of March, 76 jurisdictions worldwide had committed to exchanging information under CARF, according to the European Commission.

title: Tether Expands Latin American Push With Investment in Argentine Fintech Lemon
summary: Tether has invested an undisclosed sum in Argentine fintech Lemon to expand the adoption of its dollar-pegged USDT and XAUT across Latin America. From Inflation Hedge to Everyday Payment Tool Stablecoin issuer Tether announced Nov. 25 an investment in Argentine fintech company Lemon as part of effor...
content:
Tether has invested an undisclosed sum in Argentine fintech Lemon to expand the adoption of its dollar-pegged USDT and XAUT across Latin America.

Key Takeaways

  • Tether invested in Argentine fintech Lemon on Nov. 25 to expand USDT and XAUT adoption across Latin America.
  • Argentina ranks second in Latin America with $88.5 billion in crypto activity, rising 15.3% year-over-year.
  • Lemon plans to build lower-cost financial products by 2027 to broaden USDT and XAUT access beyond trading.

From Inflation Hedge to Everyday Payment Tool

Stablecoin issuer Tether announced Nov. 25 an investment in Argentine fintech company Lemon as part of efforts to expand the use of its USDT stablecoin and gold-backed token, XAUT, across Latin America. The financial terms of the investment were not disclosed.

According to a statement, the investment will support Lemon in developing digital asset-based financial products designed to reduce transaction costs and simplify access to alternative financial services across the region.

Lemon already operates a platform that allows users to save, invest in stocks, send and receive international payments. The platform offers a single digital dollar balance powered by USDT, handling currency conversions, exchange rates and blockchain networks in the background.

Users can also acquire fractional ownership of gold through XAUT without the upfront costs typically associated with purchasing physical bullion. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said stablecoin usage across Latin America is increasingly moving beyond wealth preservation.

“In Argentina and across Latin America, USDT is no longer only a way to protect savings. People are using it to get paid, spend, and send money across borders,” Ardoino said. “Our investment in Lemon reflects how quickly digital dollars, and now digital gold through XAUT, are becoming part of everyday financial life in the region.”

Meeting Demand in a Booming Crypto Economy

Lemon founder and CEO Marcelo Cavazzoli said the investment builds on established demand for digital assets in Argentina and elsewhere in Latin America.

“We are seeing that users don’t want to choose between different types of currencies. They want one that works for everything,” Cavazzoli said.

The investment comes as Argentina continues to rank among Latin America’s largest cryptocurrency markets. According to Chainalysis’ 2026 Geography of Cryptocurrency Report, Argentina recorded $88.5 billion in cryptocurrency activity, up 15.3% over the previous year, making it the region’s second-largest crypto economy.

Persistent inflation and currency volatility have driven Argentine households and businesses toward U.S. dollar-linked digital assets to preserve purchasing power, facilitate remittances and conduct commercial transactions.

The Lemon deal builds on Tether’s broader push to anchor digital asset infrastructure across Latin America. In July 2026, the stablecoin issuer invested $20 million in Brazil-based Mercado Bitcoin, a regulated crypto platform serving more than 4.5 million users, to expand tokenization, lending, on-chain capital markets, and stablecoin payments.

Tether has also backed other regional players, including Bolivian fintech Peso and institutional settlement platform EFY Finance, while integrating USDT with Brazil’s Pix instant payment network through portfolio company Oobit.

For Tether, these investments represent an opportunity to expand the distribution of both tokens beyond cryptocurrency trading platforms. Integrating USDT and XAUT into consumer-facing financial applications could help the company capture a larger share of everyday payments, cross-border transfers and savings activity across Latin America.

title: Braiins warns of Bitcoin mining attacks affecting over 1,000 sites
summary: Bitcoin mining pool operator Braiins warned that attackers are exploiting unsecured connections to hijack miners’ computing power and potentially steal rewards.
content:
Bitcoin mining pool operator Braiins has warned of a growing security threat to the Bitcoin mining industry after a series of attacks affected more than 1,000 mining sites.

In a report shared on Wednesday, Braiins said an attacker redirected internet traffic between Bitcoin miners and their mining pools, allowing the attacker to claim credit for work done by someone else’s machines.

The company identified 24 incidents between Nov. 7 and 20, with the amount of computing power affected in a single attack increasing nearly elevenfold over two weeks. “The episodes so far were short, but they grew from under 175 PH/s to 1.9 EH/s in two weeks,” Braiins said.

Bitcoin’s total computing power, known as hashrate, stood at an estimated 1,016 exahashes per second (EH/s) on Nov. 20, according to MineOrNot data. For context, the computing power affected in the largest attack was equivalent to about 0.19% of that total.

Braiins’ report underscores how the widespread use of unsecured connections could leave more Bitcoin miners vulnerable to similar attacks in the future.

Related: Luxor CEO warns of AI ‘dark forest’ following Bitcoin miner hijack

Bitcoin miners could lose money without noticing

The attacks exploited a weakness in Stratum V1, a widely used mining protocol introduced in 2012 that allows mining machines to communicate with mining pools.

However, the unsecured version does not let miners check whether they are connected to the right pool. This allows attackers to basically impersonate mining pools and collect Bitcoin (BTC) rewards at miners’ expense.

The earlier incidents mainly affected mining sites in Brazil and Argentina. But four larger attacks on Nov. 20 each affected between 1,050 and 1,600 mining sites, mostly in Europe.

While Braiins did not specify whether the attacks affected large commercial mining farms or smaller independent miners, it said the vast majority of Bitcoin’s computing power still uses unsecured Stratum V1 connections.

The attacks come as Bitcoin miners are already facing pressure from lower Bitcoin prices and high operating costs, with several major mining companies pivoting to artificial intelligence (AI) and data center services for new avenues of revenue.

Miners may not immediately notice the attacks because their machines continue to run, the report said. This means they could continue paying for electricity while simultaneously losing mining earnings.

Braiins said neither its mining pool nor the affected machines were hacked directly. The company also did not disclose how much money miners may have lost.

Braiins urges miners to secure their connections

On Nov. 23, Braiins reviewed the largest Bitcoin mining pools and found that most still only offered unsecured Stratum V1 connections.

The company urged miners to switch to Stratum V2, a newer version that protects communications and allows miners to check that they are connected to the right pool.

Meanwhile, miners who cannot upgrade can still use Stratum V1 if their pool offers an encrypted connection and their mining software can verify the pool’s identity.

The warning comes after Bitcoin mining services provider Luxor Technology suffered a separate attack earlier this month.

As Cointelegraph reported on Nov. 16, attackers exploited a weakness in Luxor’s mining management software, Commander, to redirect customers’ computing power to the OCEAN mining pool. The attack affected a little over a dozen customer accounts.

Luxor said it fixed the issue within two hours of detecting the unauthorized changes and also promised to fully compensate affected customers.

title: Why ECB collateral eligibility could boost demand for tokenized bonds
summary: Past ECB decisions offer clues to the value of using bonds as collateral, while US derivatives exchanges face a different calculation over their Bitcoin holdings.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 25, 2026

Past ECB decisions offer clues to the value of using bonds as collateral, while US derivatives exchanges face a different calculation over their Bitcoin holdings.

The European Central Bank (ECB) plans to expand the range of tokenized bonds banks can use as collateral to borrow cash, a move that could lower borrowing costs for issuers and give bond funds additional ways to earn securities-lending fees.

For a borrower preparing a bond sale, the choice of where to issue it could affect the interest bill. From June 2027, the ECB plans to accept qualifying bonds issued on platforms licensed under the EU’s distributed ledger technology pilot regime.

A bank that buys one could raise cash from the Eurosystem using the bond as collateral without selling it. That flexibility may be worth a higher bid at the sale.

Historical bond prices offer a clue to the potential impact. A study of 160 changes in Eurosystem collateral eligibility found that yields on newly eligible corporate bonds fell by 4.6 to 20 basis points relative to bonds still waiting to qualify.

Demand to borrow eligible securities also rose, according to the study. A bond fund could earn a fee by lending the security to a bank that wants to pledge it as collateral. Luxembourg’s 1.7 billion euro ($1.86 billion) tokenized bond already qualified through an earlier route.

Banks bought 47% of the October issue, close to their 51% share of Luxembourg’s conventional 10-year sale in March. Those figures show banks were willing buyers in both markets. As eligibility expands, the more revealing figures will be the yields banks accept on newly eligible debt and how much of it they actually pledge.

How Binary Markets Produce a Price

Each market asks whether an Ornn GPU rental-price index will average above a certain threshold in a given month. A trader can buy Yes or No shares on whether, for instance, the H100’s average rental price will stay above $3 per GPU hour.

Thus, the price works as the market’s implied probability that the threshold will be exceeded. For each chip and month Polymarket takes the probabilities from a range of thresholds and combines them into a single projected figure which is the Polymarket-implied rental price (PIRP).

If you then link the PIRPs across the settlement dates you get a curve which tells you whether traders expect rental prices to go up or down through 2028.

Contracts Serve as a Price Reference

The contracts are non-deliverable. Traders are paid out in cash against Ornn index data, do not get any GPUs or cloud computing hours, and have no right to rent capacity at the forecasted price.

However, the contracts allow a cloud provider, AI developer or lender to look at the curve and access their future compute costs before making investment decisions. This puts prediction market pricing into one of the core operating costs of the AI industry.

Whether or not the curve proves to be a useful benchmark will be down to liquidity at each threshold and how well the Ornn indices track what buyers are actually paying in private compute contracts.
