title: Braiins Warns of Widespread Bitcoin Hashrate Hijacking Attacks
summary: Bitcoin mining pool operator Braiins issued a security alert Wednesday, Nov. 25, revealing a series of network hijacking attacks that redirected up to 1.9 exahash per second (EH/s) of computing power by exploiting longstanding security weaknesses in the Stratum V1 mining protocol. Braiins Reveals Bi...
content:
Bitcoin mining pool operator Braiins issued a security alert Wednesday, Nov. 25, revealing a series of network hijacking attacks that redirected up to 1.9 exahash per second (EH/s) of computing power by exploiting longstanding security weaknesses in the Stratum V1 mining protocol.

Key Takeaways

  • Braiins identified four attacks on Nov. 20 affecting between 1,050 and 1,600 mining sites per episode.
  • Attackers exploited internet routing vulnerabilities and unencrypted mining connections without compromising mining pool infrastructure.
  • Braiins recommends migrating to Stratum V2 or authenticated encrypted connections as the threat remains active.

Braiins Reveals Bitcoin Mining Attacks Across Multiple Continents

In an X post and security advisory published Wednesday, Braiins disclosed that an attacker redirected bitcoin miners toward an impersonated mining pool by manipulating internet traffic. The company stressed that neither its mining pool nor the affected mining equipment was directly compromised.

The earliest incidents documented by Braiins occurred between Nov. 7 and Nov. 12, primarily affecting mining operations in Brazil and Argentina. Investigators identified 19 episodes involving between 120 and 400 mining sites per incident, with diverted computational power ranging from 36 to 174 petahash per second (PH/s).

By Nov. 20, the attacks had grown considerably larger and shifted predominantly toward Europe. Braiins identified four episodes lasting between six and 49 minutes, each affecting more than 1,000 mining sites and redirecting between 0.6 and 1.9 EH/s.

“The weakness they used is not newly discovered,” Braiins explained.

Stratum V1, introduced in 2012, facilitates communication between mining equipment and mining pools. Its unencrypted implementation lacks a mechanism for miners to authenticate the server assigning their computational work, leaving mining revenue exposed to malicious network interference.

Braiins traced the European incidents to manipulation of the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), the system responsible for directing internet traffic between independent networks. Fraudulent routing announcements diverted legitimate mining communications toward unauthorized infrastructure.

The investigation found that affected equipment continued operating at full computational capacity while legitimate pool dashboards recorded disappearing hashrate. Consequently, miners could continue consuming electricity without receiving credit for their work.

Stratum V1 Exploit Differs From Recent Luxor Mining Hack

The latest security disclosure follows a separate hashrate hijacking incident involving Luxor Technology earlier this month. On Nov. 15, Luxor confirmed that unauthorized modifications to mining pool configurations through its Commander management platform affected just over a dozen customer accounts.

Estimates suggested approximately 13 EH/s had been redirected to the Ocean mining pool, although the figure remains independently unverified. Luxor CEO Nick Hansen attributed the compromise to a “sophisticated AI-enabled vector,” without publicly disclosing its technical mechanics.

Unlike the Luxor incident, which involved unauthorized configuration changes, the attacks documented by Braiins intercepted communications between mining machines and their intended pools. No changes to mining configurations were necessary, and pool account balances and payout settings remained unaffected.

The underlying vulnerability has persisted for more than a decade. In 2014, Dell Secureworks documented a similar internet routing attack that diverted approximately $83,000 in cryptocurrency mining rewards. Braiins subsequently addressed the threat in 2020 while advocating the adoption of Stratum V2.

The company believes November’s escalating incidents may represent preliminary experimentation by the attacker.

Braiins Calls for Industrywide Migration to Secure Mining Connections

Braiins recommends that mining operators adopt Stratum V2, which encrypts communications and authenticates the identity of mining pools. Operators unable to migrate immediately can use Stratum V1 protected by Transport Layer Security (TLS), provided their firmware properly validates security certificates.

The company released Braiins OS 26.11 on Wednesday, introducing TLS certificate and hostname verification alongside protections against automatic transitions to unencrypted connections. Braiins also introduced a free Stratum V2 proxy for equipment that lacks compatible firmware.

Testing conducted across seven firmware implementations on Nov. 20 and Nov. 23 revealed additional security deficiencies. Two widely used implementations accepted invalid certificates despite offering TLS functionality, potentially exposing operators to impersonation even when communications appeared encrypted.

Braiins also urged mining pools, firmware developers and internet providers to strengthen infrastructure security, while recommending that operators monitor discrepancies between locally reported hashrate and computational power credited by their pools.

Authenticated encryption cannot prevent malicious actors from disrupting internet connectivity, but it can prevent mining equipment from performing work for impersonated pools.

November’s incidents expose an uncomfortable reality for an industry operating increasingly sophisticated industrial infrastructure. Expensive mining fleets remain dependent on communication protocols developed during Bitcoin’s formative years. While computational efficiency has advanced considerably, securing the connection through which that computational power generates revenue remains unfinished business.

title: Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Committee, Heads to Floor
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Committee, Heads to Floor
Rep. Nick Begich's bill to write the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into law, with a 20-year ban on selling its bitcoin, is now eligible for a House floor vote.
This post Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Co...
content:
A bill that would write the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into federal law is now eligible for a vote on the House floor, after the House Financial Services Committee formally reported it on Tuesday.

The American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, H.R. 8957, was filed with amendments as House Report 119-894 and placed on the Union Calendar as Calendar No. 789 on Nov. 24, according to congressional records. The committee had voted 28-21 to advance the bill at a Sept. 16 markup.

Rep. Nick Begich, an Alaska Republican, introduced the bill on May 21. It now lists 23 cosponsors, including Rep. Jared Golden, a Maine Democrat, with Reps. Byron Donalds and Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida added on Nov. 24.

What the amended bill does

The reported text directs the Treasury secretary to set up a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and a separate Digital Asset Stockpile within 180 days of the law taking effect. Bitcoin owned by the federal government would move into the reserve, while other digital assets would go to the stockpile.

The centerpiece is a lock-up. Treasury would have to hold all bitcoin deposited in the reserve for at least 20 years after enactment, and during that period no reserve bitcoin could be “sold, swapped, auctioned, encumbered, or otherwise disposed of for any purpose.”

After the 20 years, the Treasury secretary could recommend selling up to 10% of the reserve in any two-year period. Two years before the holding period ends, Treasury would have to send Congress recommendations on whether to keep holding or begin a gradual release.

Federal agencies would have 60 days after enactment to give Treasury a full accounting of the bitcoin and other digital assets they hold or have seized. Until the reserve is set up, agencies could not sell those coins except for national security, when required by law or a court, or to return assets to crime victims.

The bill also creates a Proof of Reserve system. Treasury would publish an annual report on total holdings, transactions and control of private keys, checked by an independent auditor with expertise in cryptographic attestations, while the Government Accountability Office would provide oversight.

States could choose to store their own bitcoin in segregated accounts inside the federal reserve, keeping title to the coins and the right to withdraw them.

Changes from Begich’s original version

The committee rewrote the bill before reporting it. Begich’s introduced text asked Treasury and Commerce to study funding bitcoin purchases with surplus remittances from Federal Reserve Banks or a revaluation of the Fed’s gold certificates, as well as with tax payments, tariff revenue and gifts.

Those options are gone from the amended study, which now looks at swapping other digital assets in the stockpile, forfeitures and settlements, and partnerships with states or private entities. The amended version also states that nothing in the study authorizes borrowing, pledging government assets as collateral, new taxes or deficit spending to buy bitcoin.

The committee also amended the bill’s title to drop a reference to offsetting costs with Federal Reserve resources, and removed a section that would have required the Exchange Stabilization Fund to report its bitcoin holdings.

Bitcoin Magazine reported on the bill’s bipartisan debut in May and on the full text revealing the 20-year lock-up in June. The reserve itself already exists under Executive Order 14233, signed in March 2025, but an executive order can be reversed by a future president, which is why Begich and his cosponsors want it in statute.

Setting up the reserve has been slow. In July, a report said Treasury and Commerce were competing over who would control it.

Begich’s bill has not received a floor vote. If it passes the House, the Senate would still need to act before it could reach the president’s desk.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Bit Digital Sells Nearly 30,000 ETH to Slash Galaxy Debt by $50 Million
summary: Bit Digital announced Wednesday, Nov. 25, that it sold 29,825 ETH to repay $50 million in secured borrowings from Galaxy Digital, joining a growing roster of publicly traded digital asset treasury (DAT) companies liquidating digital asset reserves to reduce leverage and reposition capital. Bit Digit...
content:
Bit Digital announced Wednesday, Nov. 25, that it sold 29,825 ETH to repay $50 million in secured borrowings from Galaxy Digital, joining a growing roster of publicly traded digital asset treasury (DAT) companies liquidating digital asset reserves to reduce leverage and reposition capital.

Key Takeaways

  • Bit Digital sold 29,825 ETH at an average price of $1,676, cutting its outstanding Galaxy borrowings by 50%.
  • Bit Digital retains 134,532 ETH and ETH-equivalents and expects its Whitefiber bridge loan to be fully repaid in Q2 2027.
  • Corporate digital asset sales have accelerated in 2026 as treasury firms prioritize debt reduction, share buybacks and artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Bit Digital Liquidates $50 Million in ETH to Reduce Secured Leverage

Nasdaq-listed Bit Digital (BTBT) disclosed Wednesday that it sold ethereum (ETH) between Nov. 15 and 23, directing the entire $50 million in net proceeds toward repaying principal under its secured borrowing arrangement with Galaxy Digital. The transaction reduced outstanding borrowings from $100 million to $50 million.

The financing arrangement was originally established to support the DAT firm Bit Digital’s $100 million bridge loan to Whitefiber (Nasdaq: WYFI), its majority-owned artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure business. The capital supported Whitefiber’s NC-1 data center development and other expansion initiatives.

The Whitefiber venture has since secured a $300 million project financing facility for NC-1, including a $100 million delayed-draw tranche contingent upon specified conditions. Bit Digital anticipates full repayment of its bridge loan during the second quarter of 2027.

“We remain confident in ethereum’s long-term role in digital finance and in WhiteFiber’s opportunity in AI infrastructure,” Bit Digital CEO Sam Tabar stated Wednesday.

The Bit Digital executive added:

“We recognize that shareholders expect disciplined execution and tangible results, and our focus remains on making capital allocation decisions that balance long-term opportunity with responsible risk management.”

Following the transactions, Bit Digital retained approximately 134,532 ETH and ETH-equivalents, including 36,811 ETH natively staked on the Ethereum network. Another 69,089 LsETH, a liquid staking token, remains pledged as collateral against the outstanding Galaxy Digital debt.

The pledged assets are included in Bit Digital’s reported treasury balance rather than representing additional reserves. While the company retains substantial digital asset exposure, the repayment reduces its dependence on collateralized financing during a period of pronounced market weakness.

Ethereum Treasury Companies Increasingly Turn to Asset Sales

Bit Digital is hardly alone in trimming its cryptocurrency reserves. Earlier this week, ethereum infrastructure and DAT company BTCS disclosed the sale of approximately 27,300 ETH for $43.8 million, directing the proceeds toward reducing borrowings through Aave, the decentralized finance (DeFi) lending protocol.

Combined, Bit Digital and BTCS have offloaded 57,125 ETH for approximately $93.8 million, with both transactions driven by balance-sheet considerations rather than an outright abandonment of ether.

Other companies have adopted different approaches. Coinshares liquidated its entire corporate ethereum treasury and half its solana (SOL) position, generating $19.3 million to support share repurchases. The investment firm determined that buying its own discounted equity presented a more attractive capital allocation opportunity.

The development illustrates a vulnerability within the digital asset treasury (DAT) model. When cryptocurrency prices decline and corporate shares trade below the value of underlying reserves, management must weigh continued accumulation against debt obligations, operating requirements and shareholder returns.

Corporate Cryptocurrency Selling Becomes a Defining Trend of 2026

Ethereum treasury firms represent only one segment of the broader corporate selling trend. According to an early November estimate from blockchain analytics platform Lookonchain, 14 publicly traded companies collectively sold approximately 108,247 BTC in 2026, valued at roughly $8.08 billion.

Bitcoin miners account for much of the activity. MARA Holdings has disclosed sales totaling approximately 40,581 BTC this year, including 13,597 BTC sold after September. The company directed $750 million from its more recent sales toward repaying bitcoin-backed term loans.

Meanwhile, Riot Platforms sold 20,264 BTC during the first nine months of 2026, with proceeds supporting data center development and the repayment of a $200 million credit facility. Bitcoin miner Bitdeer has similarly depleted its proprietary bitcoin reserves, effectively converting mining production into operating capital.

Other companies, including Sequans Communications and Hyperscale Data, have exited their bitcoin treasury positions entirely. However, the trend is not universal, as Strategy has continued accumulating bitcoin despite the broader market contraction. For Bit Digital, the immediate objective is not to abandon ethereum but to reduce financial exposure while awaiting repayment from its AI infrastructure subsidiary.

Still, the growing volume of corporate digital asset sales reveals a fundamental tension. Assets accumulated as long-term strategic reserves are increasingly becoming sources of immediate liquidity when corporate obligations take precedence.

title: Geo – Protocols Are Not Companies
summary: Yaniv Tal is Founder and CEO of Geo, a network for organizing knowledge people can trust, built on a decentralized knowledge graph. He co-founded The Graph, the indexing protocol that became core web3 infrastructure, after arriving in crypto in 2017 from a background building developer tools, and sp...
content:
Skip to content

Yaniv Tal is Founder and CEO of Geo, a network for organizing knowledge people can trust, built on a decentralized knowledge graph. He co-founded The Graph, the indexing protocol that became core web3 infrastructure, after arriving in crypto in 2017 from a background building developer tools, and spun Geo out as its own company in 2022.

The link will open a new window. Click the menu and down arrow to download the file.

Why you should listen

Yaniv’s central argument is that crypto made a category error. When the industry was overfunded in 2017 and again in 2021, investors rightly demanded to see what their money had built, and the shift to fundamentals was healthy. The mistake, he says, was borrowing the fundamentals of companies. A company sells a product, protects a proprietary advantage and returns margin to shareholders. A protocol like Ethereum is closer to public infrastructure, and its job is to deliver the most benefit to its users, who are often its holders. He welcomes Vitalik Buterin’s recent call to value ETH as a store of value rather than a fee-burning token, and points out that Bitcoin was never valued on fees either.

From there Yaniv makes the case for a small number of crypto stores of value, not just one. He challenges the view that only Bitcoin qualifies, arguing that moving trillions of dollars into a young technology calls for some diversification, and that Ethereum’s ability to upgrade leaves it better placed for risks such as quantum computing. He ties demand for stores of value to the debt loads of fiat governments and sets a 100-year test: listed companies tend to last only a decade or two by his count, so lasting value has to come from networks with real utility and network effects. In his framing, Ethereum is a global system of digital property rights. He also describes the market as a barbell, with fee-maximizing infrastructure for banks at one end and valueless memecoins at the other, and says what’s missing is the middle: networks people hold because they believe they make the world better. Changing that, he argues, is up to VCs, the media and every token holder, because developers build what the market rewards.

The final stretch turns to Geo. Yaniv explains why knowledge needs to be structured as a graph to be composable, revisits the semantic web that the web’s original architects tried and failed to build, and argues that public blockchain infrastructure and cryptographic verification finally make it practical, especially as people want their AI agents to control their own data. He walks through Geo Debates, where users vote on contested questions from geopolitics to health and AI, and previews the second season of Geo’s curator program, in which participants add context, publish knowledge and fact-check claims. He describes the long-term vision as something like Reddit built on a shared knowledge graph, where communities can flag what was taken out of context and hold sources accountable.

title: Ethereum Foundation backs Keccak-256 to counter quantum, AI threats
summary: Ethlabs co-founder Julian Ma told Cointelegraph that AI poses a more immediate threat as Ethereum prepares for one of its biggest security overhauls since the Merge.
content:
The Ethereum Foundation has recommended the Keccak-256 hash function as the basis for Ethereum’s cryptographic defenses against quantum computing and AI-assisted attacks, according to a blog post on Nov. 24. It chose the nearly 20-year-old function over Poseidon, a newer alternative the team had spent years attempting to harden.

Described by Ethlabs co-founder Julian Ma as “one of the largest efforts done in blockchain, not just in Ethereum,” the planned switch to hash-based cryptography acts as a critical move to protect the chain from the future threat of quantum-based attacks.

Keccak-256 is a cryptographic hash function that converts data into a fixed-length, 256-bit digital fingerprint used to verify data integrity, while quantum attacks use quantum computing to exploit weaknesses in existing cryptographic systems.

The chosen hash function would form the backbone of Ethereum’s post-quantum security, meaning that “if it is broken, everything else is broken,” the blog post said. With nearly two decades of resistance to attacks, Keccak was considered the most secure of the candidates evaluated by the Foundation.

While quantum resistance is the long-term goal of the switch, protecting against the rising threat of AI-assisted attacks has become a more immediate priority.

The five hash-function candidates

The initial focus of the Ethereum Foundation’s research on hash functions was balancing the speed and security of the new system. The Foundation passed on SHA-256, despite its use in Bitcoin, citing collision attacks affecting more than half of the hash function’s protection.

Since the research began, the performance of SNARKs, cryptographic proofs that allow statements to be verified without showing the underlying data, has improved. The Foundation noted that security was therefore “the deciding factor.”

Related: Ethereum Foundation doubles protocol security team ahead of overhaul

Poseidon, the hash function the team had previously focused on, was designed in 2019 specifically to handle zero-knowledge proofs. Traditional hashes like SHA-256, used by Bitcoin, made these proofs painfully slow. However, reduced-round versions of Poseidon were still open to attacks, and improvements in SNARK performance reduced its speed advantage.

Two other functions also considered by the foundation were BLAKE2 and BLAKE3, general-purpose hashes used in VPNs and the Linux kernel. While their speed was noted in the blog post, limited research into their resistance to attacks led the Foundation to rule them out as options for the Ethereum network.

Protecting from quantum and AI

Although the move to hash-based cryptography is focused on reducing the threat of quantum computing, AI has become a primary security concern. Increasingly powerful AI systems have raised concerns about the security of cryptographic systems, including those Ethereum relies on.

Ethlabs’ Ma, who proposed an approach to post-quantum and post-AI resistance on Ethereum on Nov. 11, told Cointelegraph that although post-quantum security is important, “AI is here today and it’s breaking everything around us.” He noted that in this environment, “Ethereum has kept 100% uptime, basically because it has a culture of being extremely proactive on these security issues and prioritizing security over everything else.” In the blog post, the Foundation noted that Keccak-256 had so far remained unaffected by AI-assisted attacks.

Ma explained that much of the Ethereum community is aligned on making post-quantum security a priority. He said nearly all core developers are keen to put it first, which he described as “80, 90% of the win,” with the remaining discussions centered on which other upgrades should make way for it.

For the teams that build Ethereum’s software, the Foundation noted that the choice of Keccak would require little new code. Ethereum has used Keccak for its addresses since launch, so client teams can reuse existing code instead of building and testing a new hash from scratch. The Foundation also recommended that the consensus layer, which currently relies on SHA-256, gradually move over to Keccak for certain hashing operations.

Core developers have not approved the Ethlabs proposal, and the Foundation’s published roadmap still targets December 2029 for quantum resistance.

title: SEC Investor Panel to Examine Broker-Free Trading of Tokenised US Stocks
summary:
The US Securities and Exchange Commission’s Investor Advisory Committee will examine a temporary framework that allows retail investors to trade eligible tokenised shares directly on permissioned venues without using a broker-dealer. 
The virtual public meeting is on Dec 3 at 9.30am ET. The first pa...
content:
2026-11-25T20:41:51.441+02:00

Wednesday, 25/11/2026 | 18:41 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Better Markets, OKX, Securitize and former CFTC Chairman Timothy Massad will discuss whether the temporary framework needs further investor protections.
  • The exemption sets shareholder-rights and volume conditions for tokenised shares and is scheduled to expire in September 2031 unless the SEC changes it earlier.

The US Securities and Exchange Commission’s Investor Advisory Committee will examine a temporary framework that allows retail investors to trade eligible tokenised shares directly on permissioned venues without using a broker-dealer.

The virtual public meeting is on Dec 3 at 9.30am ET. The first panel will focus on the SEC's Innovation Exemption (introduced in September), which is designed to facilitate on-chain trading in shares of US-listed companies.

The committee can submit recommendations to the SEC but cannot amend the exemption itself. Any change following the discussion would require separate action by the Commission.

The meeting will be streamed on the SEC’s website.

Market Operators and Investor Advocates Join the Panel

The 90-minute tokenisation panel begins at 10 a.m. ET. Participants include representatives of investor advocacy group Better Markets, crypto exchange OKX and tokenisation platform Securitize, as well as former Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chairman Timothy Massad.

They will discuss the exemption’s risks and benefits for investors and public companies, the different structures used for tokenised equities and whether the current framework should be revised.

Separate panels will cover bankruptcy proceedings and accounting oversight. The committee will also vote on recommendations concerning the proposed removal of the trade-through rule and a possible SEC study of retail investors’ understanding of private-market assets.

How the Innovation Exemption Works

The Innovation Exemption temporarily allows qualifying Tokenised Securities Venues to operate without being treated as exchanges under the Exchange Act.

Certain firms providing capital to their liquidity pools can also operate without being treated as dealers. The relief is subject to a number of conditions.

The tokens must confer the same rights to the holders as the relevant conventional shares. A public company can object to a third party tokenised version of its shares being traded on a venue.

Each venue will be subject to volume limits of 0.25% for companies in the S&P 500 or Russell 1000 and 2.5% for all other companies. In March the committee recommended use of only a limited exemption and the retention of the core investor protections.

The December agenda will be a panel, not a vote on another tokenisation recommendation. The current framework is still in place and will expire in September 2031 unless the SEC chooses to act earlier.

The 90-minute tokenisation panel begins at 10 a.m. ET. Participants include representatives of investor advocacy group Better Markets, crypto exchange OKX and tokenisation platform Securitize, as well as former Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chairman Timothy Massad.

They will discuss the exemption’s risks and benefits for investors and public companies, the different structures used for tokenised equities and whether the current framework should be revised.

Separate panels will cover bankruptcy proceedings and accounting oversight. The committee will also vote on recommendations concerning the proposed removal of the trade-through rule and a possible SEC study of retail investors’ understanding of private-market assets.

How the Innovation Exemption Works

The Innovation Exemption temporarily allows qualifying Tokenised Securities Venues to operate without being treated as exchanges under the Exchange Act.

Certain firms providing capital to their liquidity pools can also operate without being treated as dealers. The relief is subject to a number of conditions.

The tokens must confer the same rights to the holders as the relevant conventional shares. A public company can object to a third party tokenised version of its shares being traded on a venue.

Each venue will be subject to volume limits of 0.25% for companies in the S&P 500 or Russell 1000 and 2.5% for all other companies. In March the committee recommended use of only a limited exemption and the retention of the core investor protections.

The December agenda will be a panel, not a vote on another tokenisation recommendation. The current framework is still in place and will expire in September 2031 unless the SEC chooses to act earlier.

title: Switzerland Picks 57 Countries for Crypto Tax Data Sharing Starting in 2028
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Switzerland Picks 57 Countries for Crypto Tax Data Sharing Starting in 2028
Switzerland approved 57 partner jurisdictions, including all EU states and the UK, for automatic crypto tax data exchanges under the OECD's CARF from 2028.
This post Switzerland Picks 57 Countries for Crypt...
content:
Switzerland’s Federal Council has approved 57 countries and territories with which the country plans to automatically share tax information on crypto users starting in 2028, extending its long-standing bank data exchange to bitcoin and other digital assets.

The list includes all European Union member states, the United Kingdom and various G20 countries, the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) said in a release on Wednesday. The exchange will run under the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, known as CARF.

With the decision, Switzerland intends to implement the crypto exchange at the same time as other global asset management centers, according to the release. The government did not name the 57 jurisdictions beyond those broad groups, and it did not publish the full list alongside the announcement.

Exchanges only with partners that qualify

Data will not flow to every name on the list. An exchange will take place only if a partner jurisdiction wants to swap information with Switzerland and meets the conditions of the OECD standard, in particular its requirements on confidentiality and data security.

Before any financial account or crypto data changes hands, the Federal Council will run a targeted check of whether each partner complies with OECD standards. It will rely on a review mechanism Parliament approved on Sept. 28, 2026, which covers both the older exchange of bank account data and the new crypto exchange.

The domestic legal basis for the crypto exchange took effect on Jan. 1, 2026. Earlier this month, though, the SIF said the framework could not be implemented before Jan. 1, 2027, because the partner list still needed approval and notifications had to go to the OECD. The rules do not apply this year.

The Council also approved Armenia and Rwanda as new partners for the exchange of financial account information, with first exchanges due in 2028, and signed off on two notifications needed to carry out the exchange. Both partner lists were broadly supported during public consultations in 2024 and 2025, the government said.

Down from 74 partners

The final list is shorter than first planned. In June 2025, the Federal Council proposed 74 countries relevant to the crypto market, including all EU states, the UK and most G20 members. That plan left out the United States and Saudi Arabia, and it targeted a 2026 start with first data exchanges in 2027.

Wednesday’s release did not say which countries were dropped or whether the U.S. is now on the list. The U.S. has committed to begin CARF exchanges by 2029, according to the OECD’s Global Forum, which lists Switzerland among 27 jurisdictions aiming for first exchanges by 2028.

That U.S. timeline is already shaping policy elsewhere. South Korea pushed its 22% crypto tax back to 2029 partly because it will not receive American crypto trading data until CARF exchanges with the U.S. begin that year. Officials said taxing earlier could put Korea’s domestic market at a disadvantage.

Switzerland’s decision lands as European governments debate how much they should know about crypto holders. On Tuesday, France’s Senate rejected a rule that would have forced bitcoin holders to declare self-custody wallets, while EU states began collecting crypto transaction data under the bloc’s DAC8 directive this year.

For Switzerland, CARF extends a system it already runs for bank accounts. The country has exchanged financial account information automatically under the OECD’s Common Reporting Standard since 2018, ending much of the secrecy once tied to Swiss banking. Its regulated crypto market keeps growing, with the country’s financial regulator clearing its first bitcoin ETF in October.

Under CARF, crypto service providers in Switzerland will have to collect information on users who are tax residents of activated partner jurisdictions and report it to Swiss tax authorities, which then pass it on to those partners once the exchange begins.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Passports, Bank Accounts and Wallet Addresses
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Passports, Bank Accounts and Wallet Addresses
Bithumb said a follow-up review found its October breach exposed more people and data, including passports and wallet addresses, and lasted about 15 days.
This post Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Pas...
content:
South Korean crypto exchange Bithumb said Wednesday that an October hack of its internal systems exposed more people and far more personal data than it first disclosed, including passport numbers, bank account numbers and crypto wallet addresses.

The exchange also said the intruder had access for about 15 days before being shut out, not the roughly one hour it reported last month.

In an updated notice posted Nov. 25, Bithumb said a follow-up review of the breach of Daou Office, its internal mobile groupware system, turned up additional affected people and additional types of data. The company said the new findings stem from the same incident it disclosed on Oct. 29.

Bithumb breach ran for 15 days

Bithumb now says an unauthorized outside party accessed the groupware system from 1:49 p.m. on Oct. 12 to 3:22 p.m. on Oct. 27, Korea time, and took personal information and files stored there.

That is a sharp change from its first account. Bithumb had said the hack lasted about an hour, from 11:28 a.m. to 12:27 p.m. on Oct. 27, and that it detected the intrusion at 12:14 p.m. that day. The revised timeline means the attacker went unnoticed for more than two weeks.

Bithumb first reported that the data of 6,444 customers and 715 employees, or 7,159 people in total, had been exposed. It did not give an updated count on Wednesday. The notice lists customers, employees of partner companies and current and former staff among those affected.

Passports, bank accounts and wallet addresses

The list of exposed data now runs to 19 items. It includes member numbers, names, mobile numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, resident registration numbers, passport numbers and driver’s license numbers.

It also covers bank account numbers, home addresses, gender, nationality, copies of ID documents, occupations, employer names and work contact details, as well as transaction histories and wallet addresses. Bithumb said not every item applies to every person, and that affected users will be told individually by email and text message what was taken.

For crypto users, the wallet addresses and transaction records stand out. Paired with names and phone numbers, that kind of data can help scammers target people they know hold digital assets.

Bithumb said Daou Office is an internal business system separate from customer exchange accounts and asset data. It said it has found no sign that its exchange service systems or customer database were directly breached, and that it has stepped up real-time monitoring of unusual trades and withdrawals.

Bithumb promises compensation

The exchange said it blocked the attacker’s IP addresses, fixed the vulnerability behind the incident and is running a security review of all of its externally exposed services. It has also set up a dedicated support desk for victims that covers financial and legal counseling as well as compensation reviews.

“We will take responsibility for all harm confirmed to have resulted from this personal information breach and provide all necessary support and compensation to affected customers,” Bithumb said.

Bithumb warned users that it never asks for passwords, verification codes or OTP details by phone, text or messenger. It urged anyone who gets such a request to stop responding, confirm through its official app or customer center and report any financial losses to police.

The disclosure adds to a difficult year for the exchange. Bithumb mistakenly credited users with billions of dollars in bitcoin in February, and regulators fined it $24 million and imposed a six-month partial suspension in March over anti-money laundering violations.

It also comes as South Korea weighs new rules for crypto exchanges, including a 20% cap on ownership stakes. Brokerages including Mirae Asset Securities and Daishin Securities have also suffered a series of cyberattacks.

“We are thoroughly investigating the cause of the incident,” Bithumb said.

Micah Zimmerman

title: DOJ Targets 800 Defendants in Largest-Ever Scam Crackdown, Including Crypto Fraud
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

DOJ Targets 800 Defendants in Largest-Ever Scam Crackdown, Including Crypto Fraud
The Justice Department said its largest-ever scam crackdown has targeted more than 800 defendants since March, with Southeast Asian crypto scam centers among its top targets.
This post DOJ Targets 800...
content:
The U.S. Justice Department said Tuesday that its largest-ever crackdown on scammers has produced actions against more than 800 defendants since March, with cryptocurrency investment fraud run out of Southeast Asian scam centers among its top targets.

The department announced the results of an anti-scam surge that followed President Donald Trump’s Executive Order 14390, signed March 6. Since then, prosecutors have acted in more than 400 cases, bringing new charges, extraditions, guilty verdicts and sentences across 85 federal districts.

U.S. agents also helped police in more than 10 countries raid foreign scam call centers and compounds that targeted Americans. Thirty defendants were extradited to face charges in U.S. courts.

“Predatory scams against the American people will not be tolerated,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said. “The unprecedented results of this surge are just the beginning.”

More than $1 billion in crypto frozen

Crypto sits at the center of much of the effort. The State Department said the U.S. and Southeast Asian law enforcement it funds and trains have helped freeze more than $1 billion in stolen cryptocurrency and take down more than 1.4 million fraudulent websites and accounts.

The Justice Department’s Scam Center Strike Force, formed in 2025 to go after Southeast Asian crypto fraud, says its crypto seizure team has restrained about $1.08 billion in cryptocurrency from these schemes. The team is focused on returning stolen funds to victims.

The FBI’s Operation Blackout has restrained nearly $17 billion in illicit funds, seized more than 14,000 digital devices and helped dismantle more than 29 scam compounds across Asia, Africa and the Middle East, the department said. The FBI also helped free and repatriate more than 2,200 trafficked workers forced to run scams inside those compounds.

“The message to these scam syndicates is clear: if you target Americans, justice will find you,” FBI Director Kash Patel said.

Scam cases tied to fake crypto platforms

In the past month alone, the Criminal Division filed or unsealed charges against more than 30 scam defendants, including those tied to Southeast Asian scam centers running crypto investment fraud schemes. Other cases involved inheritance fraud, jury duty imposters working from Georgia prisons and sweepstakes schemes aimed at elderly Americans.

The Secret Service said it has restrained more than $200 million in illicit funds during the surge. One of its cases identified a crypto investment conspiracy run from scam centers in Cambodia that targeted at least 174 U.S. victims. In October, a Chinese national was extradited from the Netherlands and arraigned in California over his alleged role.

In Moldova, State Department-backed raids in October shut down five call centers and led to the detention of eight suspected coordinators who allegedly ran fake crypto trading platforms. The SEC said that in the last year it charged three purported crypto asset trading platforms and four investment clubs with defrauding retail investors of more than $14 million.

Homeland Security Investigations said its fraud cases have led to the seizure or freezing of more than $120 million, including funds held in bank and cryptocurrency accounts.

The crackdown builds on months of pressure on overseas fraud rings. Trump planned to highlight the push against overseas crypto scams in October, and the U.S. government seized more than $580 million in crypto linked to Southeast Asian scam networks in February. In October 2025, prosecutors moved to seize 127,271 bitcoin tied to a Southeast Asian scam operation.

The stakes are large. Citing Gallup, the department said 10% of U.S. adults experienced a scam last year, directly or through someone in their household, and Americans lost an estimated $68 billion to scams in 2025, including crypto investment scams.

The department noted that an indictment is merely an allegation and that all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty.

Micah Zimmerman

title: HRF Announces Funding of Seven Bitcoin Projects for People Living Under Authoritarian Regimes
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

HRF Announces Funding of Seven Bitcoin Projects for People Living Under Authoritarian Regimes
HRF's Bitcoin Development Fund backed seven projects for self-custody, privacy and education under repression, from phone wallets to solar mining in Nigeria.
This post HRF Announces Fundin...
content:
The Human Rights Foundation (HRF) is pleased to announce grants from its Bitcoin Development Fund for seven projects advancing bitcoin self-custody, financial privacy, and education for people living under authoritarian regimes.

One project translates bitcoin terminology into 21 African languages. Another mines bitcoin with surplus solar power in rural Nigerian homes, paying it directly to the households that generate it. Others build tools for people facing repression anywhere — activists who need to find and fix the privacy leaks in their bitcoin use, communities who need self-custody devices built from parts found in any electronics store, observers who need election evidence preserved before it disappears, and people who need to turn an ordinary phone into an offline Bitcoin wallet.

Together, these efforts help human rights defenders, journalists, nonprofits, and individuals hold, send, and verify their money freely under repression.

HRF’s grantees for Round III of 2026 are:

  • CryoBrick

Many people want to self-custody bitcoin, but in much of the world, buying a hardware wallet is too expensive. CryoBrick transforms feature phones into offline Bitcoin signing devices. Because it looks and works like an ordinary phone, activists living under authoritarian regimes can self-custody bitcoin while maintaining plausible deniability. Technical Director Apalok will use HRF’s support to conduct comprehensive security hardening and peer review, integrate Bitchat for offline messaging, and publish how-to guides, expanding access to bitcoin and the property rights it protects to a far larger global user base.

  • Exonumia Africa: Bitcoin Glossary

Bitcoin’s benefits remain out of reach for many African communities because high-quality education resources do not exist in their local languages. Exonumia, an open-source project that translates Bitcoin educational content, is building a Bitcoin Glossary in 21 African languages. The project will coordinate a continent-wide community of translators through three in-person and 12 virtual translation sprints, where native speakers review and validate more than 250 terms. Because every term is validated by native speakers rather than machines, the approved terms give wallet developers a trustworthy foundation for localizing bitcoin software into African languages, extending access to bitcoin education and the financial freedom it offers. HRF’s support will see the glossary published as a free public resource. 

  • Pawavox

In much of Africa, democratic elections remain a struggle and most countries are not fully free. Exacerbating this, evidence of fraud documented by citizens is often lost because paper forms go missing and photos and messages cannot be verified. Pawavox, created by Nigerian civic-tech founder Jason Omu, is a platform that gives election observers and human rights defenders a new way to record irregularities. Using Pawavox, observers capture short video or voice reports, each GPS-tagged and timestamped. This evidence is then published to Nostr, a decentralized communications protocol, as a record that is much harder for anyone to tamper with. HRF’s grant will help fund the completion of the Nostr integration and expansion across Africa, helping protect the integrity of the evidence on which democratic accountability depends.

  • SeedSigner

Branded hardware wallets are a common way to self-custody bitcoin, but under repressive regimes, they can be expensive and attract unwanted attention. SeedSigner is an open-source signing device that users assemble themselves from inexpensive, widely available parts, so there is no finished-device supply chain for an attacker to compromise. It currently runs on a small computer, called a Raspberry Pi Zero, which can be unavailable in regions that need self-custody most. Lead maintainer Keith Mukai will use HRF’s support to migrate the SeedSigner code to more widely available hardware, ending dependence on any single manufacturer. Then, more individuals under repressive regimes will be able to hold their own bitcoin without trusting anyone else.

  • Stealth

Many users assume they gain financial privacy by using bitcoin, but bitcoin is a public network, and the ways they compromise their privacy are often invisible. Stealth is an open-source auditing tool that runs directly on a user’s node (a computer that verifies the Bitcoin network). It analyzes a bitcoin wallet using the same techniques that blockchain analytics firms employ, then produces a report with severity levels, confidence scores, and concrete fixes for users. The HRF grant supports lead maintainer LORDBABUINO in adding support for the main Bitcoin network and building packages for standard node kits. With this tool, activists will be able to better spot the privacy leaks they leave behind when using Bitcoin, before an adversary does.

  • Strandedwatt

Nigeria is one of the world’s most active digital asset markets, but the legal path to acquiring bitcoin runs through exchanges that collect troves of identity and transactional data. At the same time, many rural Nigerian homes are receiving solar electricity for the first time, but much of that power goes unused in the daytime. Strandedwatt, a bitcoin mining initiative, installs small open-source Bitcoin miners in homes, converting surplus solar power into bitcoin, which is paid privately and directly to host households. The next step, backed by HRF, will see Bitnob CEO and project lead Bernard Parah deploy 100 Jua Kali miners in these homes and publish an open-source playbook other communities can replicate. Meanwhile, households excluded by the Nigerian financial system gain a permissionless path to freedom money.

  • Specter DIY

A commercial Bitcoin hardware wallet has software and hardware the user cannot inspect, and carrying one can signal to outsiders that someone owns bitcoin. Specter DIY is a fully open-source, air-gapped Bitcoin hardware wallet that anyone can build from off-the-shelf components and verify line by line. There is no purchase record, and the finished device does not look like a Bitcoin wallet at all. For activists in Belarus, dissidents in Venezuela, and journalists in Burma, it is a path to financial self-sovereignty. HRF’s grant to the Specter Association, the nonprofit that maintains the project, helps fund hardware costs, AI tooling, and vulnerability bounties, ensuring the developers behind a self-custody tool dissidents can inspect and verify remain supported.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Ukraine Approves Crypto Rules After Disagreements Between Regulators
summary:
Ukraine’s parliament
has approved legislation establishing a regulatory framework for
cryptocurrencies, introducing authorization requirements for service providers
and setting rules for taxation and consumer protection.
The Verkhovna Rada
passed the Virtual Assets Bill on November 25, with 271 lawm...
content:
2026-11-25T18:43:00.000+02:00

Wednesday, 25/11/2026 | 16:43 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • Parliament passes crypto law aligning Ukraine’s framework with EU MiCA rules, effective July 2027.
  • The country introduces 5% tax rates on cryptocurrency profits under a transitional regime.

Ukraine’s parliament has approved legislation establishing a regulatory framework for cryptocurrencies, introducing authorization requirements for service providers and setting rules for taxation and consumer protection.

The Verkhovna Rada passed the Virtual Assets Bill on November 25, with 271 lawmakers voting in favour and eight against.

The legislation establishes the legal status of virtual assets and aims to align Ukraine’s regulatory framework with the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation.

Ukraine Sets Licensing Rules for Crypto Providers

Cryptocurrency exchanges, custodians and other virtual asset service providers will need authorization or registration and will be subject to annual reporting requirements.

The National Securities and Stock Market Commission and the National Bank of Ukraine will oversee the sector. The NBU will retain responsibility for electronic money and currency-related matters, according to lawmaker Yaroslav Zheleznyak.

The legislation also introduces requirements for safeguarding customer assets, handling complaints and protecting users. Service providers will face stricter financial monitoring obligations , including checks on the origins of funds.

🇺🇦 BREAKING: UKRAINE'S PARLIAMENT PASSES ITS CRYPTO LAW WITH 271 VOTES - BRINGING IN LICENSING FOR EXCHANGES AND TAXES ON CRYPTO PROFITS THE LAW TAKES EFFECT JULY 1, 2027, WITH A REDUCED 5% TAX RATE THROUGH 2028, THEN 18% A 5% MILITARY LEVY APPLIES ON TOP https://t.co/EB4wRLbt3y

— DEGEN NEWS (@DegenerateNews) November 25, 2026

Cryptocurrency Taxation

The new framework will tax profits from cryptocurrency sales based on the difference between purchase and selling prices, using an approach similar to securities taxation.

Crypto-to-crypto exchanges will be exempt, as will profits below one minimum wage. Cryptocurrency transactions will also not attract value-added tax.

A preferential tax rate will apply until 2028, with personal income tax and the military levy both set at 5%. After that, personal income tax will increase to 18%, while the military levy will remain at 5%.

The law is scheduled to take effect in July 2027, subject to presidential approval.

Earlier Regulatory Disagreements

The legislation faced objections from the NBU, which raised concerns about regulatory gaps involving foreign tokens, potential market concentration and the authorization process for trading platforms.

The disagreements were addressed during subsequent revisions. Zheleznyak said both the NBU and NSSMC had agreed on the final provisions before parliament approved the bill.

Ukraine first passed a Virtual Assets law in 2022, but it never took effect because the necessary tax legislation was not completed.

title: SBI Solana Global Goes Live, Bringing $2.3T Financial Giants into Onchain Finance
summary:
Key Takeaways: SBI Solana Global officially lifted the roof on Solana’s operations. SBI Holdings and SMFG have combined assets of $2.3T and 80M+ customers. The venture will target payments with
The post SBI Solana Global Goes Live, Bringing $2.3T Financial Giants into Onchain Finance appeared first ...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • SBI Solana Global officially lifted the roof on Solana’s operations.
  • SBI Holdings and SMFG have combined assets of $2.3T and 80M+ customers.
  • The venture will target payments with stablecoins, tokenization, and onchain asset management.

Japan continues to make another move into financial sector blockchain infrastructure. SBI Holdings, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG), and the Solana Foundation have completed their agreements for a new joint venture structure, with SBI R3 Japan now operating as SBI Solana Global.

BREAKING: SBI Solana Global is live.

SBI Holdings and SMFG bring $2.3T in combined assets and 80M+ customers to Japan’s onchain financial market, built on Solana. https://t.co/BxDxknE4ja

— Solana (@solana) November 25, 2026

The plan is to bring the existing Japanese financial systems into connectivity with Solana’s blockchain system, and then to Korea and other foreign markets.

  • SBI Solana Global Begins Full-Scale Operations
  • Four Business Lines Target Onchain Finance
    • Stablecoin Payments and Remittances
    • Japan First, Then Expansion Across Asia

SBI Solana Global Begins Full-Scale Operations

SBI Holdings announced the completion of the transition of SBI R3 Japan Co., Ltd. to SBI Solana Global Co., Ltd. on November 25 through a series of agreements among the three parties.

Solana Foundation will partner with the newly formed company to help with its business development and expansion. The partnership is a collaboration of the financial expertise and reach of SBI and SMFG and the full UX of the Solana blockchain’s high-speed, low-cost solution.

SBI Holdings and SMFG have combined assets of over $2.3 trillion and a headcount of more than 80 million customers, Solana said. The most significant data does not reflect the value of assets already on the Solana network, but rather the significance of the financial groups.

Financial products and transactions will be executed on chain, but the venture will function as a bridge between traditional financial markets and on-chain services.

Read More: Solana Tokenized Equities Hit $1.22B, Nearly Doubling While Stock Offerings Expand

Four Business Lines Target Onchain Finance

SBI Solana Global has laid out four key growth segments, comprising payments, asset issuing, investment distribution, and management.

Stablecoin Payments and Remittances

The first is related to the establishment of cross-border and domestic payment infrastructure based on stablecoins. The company will also investigate smaller transactions powered by AI agents, a novel application of blockchain payments.

The second business line is used for the tokenization of financial assets such as bonds, investment funds and loan receivables. They could provide more financing avenues and widen the investors’ access onchain.

Real-world asset (RWA) tokenization is what is covered in the third area. SBI Solana Global plans to digitize commodities, various rights, and various physical or non-financial assets. They also might secure asset authenticity and traceability by using blockchain records.

Finally, the company will venture on chain assets management services by using stablecoins and tokenized assets. Its longer-term goal is to integrate payments, issuance, distribution and investment management into a single financial payments system.

Japan First, Then Expansion Across Asia

The three in Japan hope to create feasible applications and a sustainable business prior to expanding into other Asian marketplaces.

SBI Solana Global plans to bridge the gap between Japanese digital financial activities and the international ecosystem of Solana. This may offer opportunities for cross-border payments, investment, financing and asset distribution.

However, the November 25 announcement did not provide individual product launch dates, financial targets, or a detailed ownership breakdown.

title: Swiss National Bank Explores DLT Ledger for Tokenized Money and Securities Settlement
summary:
Key Takeaways: The SNB’s research regarding tokenized money and securities is based on a common DLT platform. The project involves several Swiss banks, with UBS, SIX, Sygnum to participate. This
The post Swiss National Bank Explores DLT Ledger for Tokenized Money and Securities Settlement appeared f...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The SNB’s research regarding tokenized money and securities is based on a common DLT platform.
  • The project involves several Swiss banks, with UBS, SIX, Sygnum to participate.
  • This initiative follows Project Helvetia, as well as BIS-led Project Agorá.

The Swiss National Bank is trying to determine if central bank money can coexist and work together with commercial bank money and securities on a common distributed ledger.

The project aims to connect key Swiss financial actors to experiment with the technical, governance and operational parameters of a tokenized settlement platform for domestic and cross-border transactions.

  • SNB Starts Swiss Financial Ledger Study
  • Tokenized Central Bank Money Is Not Yet Confirmed
    • Project Builds on Helvetia and Agorá
    • Tokenization Moves Deeper Into Regulated Finance

SNB Starts Swiss Financial Ledger Study

The SNB announced the exploratory project on November 24 alongside UBS, SIX, Zürcher Kantonalbank, PostFinance, Banque Cantonale Vaudoise, Basler Kantonalbank, Sygnum Bank and settlement platform Seturion.

The Swiss Financial Ledger will look at whether different money and tokenized securities are compatible to be used together on the same DLT-based infrastructure.

Participants will learn about a number of areas such as platform architecture, technical design, governance and operating models. The SNB has also established a Strategic Board with participation by the institutions involved and an observer role for the Swiss Bankers Association.

Read More: Singapore Issues S$100M Tokenized MAS Bills, Testing Wholesale CBDC Settlement at Scale

Tokenized Central Bank Money Is Not Yet Confirmed

The central bank has been careful to state the boundaries of expectations of the project. The research is not an indicator of Switzerland’s choice to launch the ledger. It also does not declare SNB’s intention to provide financial institutions with central bank money in the form of tokens.

The work is, rather, the continuation of studies the central bank has conducted on the evolution of the current financial infrastructure through tokenization, it says.

This is significant for the cryptocurrency industry. The initiative focuses on regulated financial settlement infrastructure, not public cryptocurrencies or permissionless blockchain networks.

Project Builds on Helvetia and Agorá

The Swiss Financial Ledger project is a component of Project Helvetia, which has been researching ways to settle tokenized asset transactions with central bank money.

It also leverages project Agorá, an initiative initiated by the Bank for International Settlements and the Institute of International Finance, which is a public-private initiative.

Agorá explores the potential for tokenizing central bank reserves and commercial bank deposits while connecting them to a programmable settlement.

The BIS highlighted the advantages of its prototype for using commercial bank deposits and central bank reserves as tokens to enable atomic settlement between multiple currencies and jurisdiction.

Tokenization Moves Deeper Into Regulated Finance

The Swiss project comes amidst a growing movement among central banks and financial institutions to investigate blockchain-type infrastructure for financial assets.

The model to be tested does not put crypto networks at the heart of settlement, but instead leaves the central bank and regulated commercial bank to manage it.

In general, the development is another indication that the tokenization technology is progressing toward its mainstream incorporation into the financial infrastructure in securities settlement and wholesale payments.

The next phase is to determine if such a common platform is efficient, secure and offers sufficient real-world utility to warrant exiting the exploratory stage.

title: Pepperstone Names Cross-Asset Lead to Link CFD and Spot Crypto Businesses
summary:
Pepperstone has appointed Laurence Willows, a former digital-assets executive at IG, as Head of Cross-Asset. He will develop products and commercial models for both the broker’s CFD business and the spot-crypto platform launched in Australia this year. 
Willows left the London-listed broker in June,...
content:
2026-11-25T16:41:06.610+02:00

Wednesday, 25/11/2026 | 14:41 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • A former IG digital-assets executive Laurence Willows is appointed as Head of Cross-Asset at Pepperstone.
  • As Finance Magnates previously reported, Pepperstone’s brief for the role covered new commercial models and potential expansion into new markets.

Pepperstone has appointed Laurence Willows, a former digital-assets executive at IG, as Head of Cross-Asset. He will develop products and commercial models for both the broker’s CFD business and the spot-crypto platform launched in Australia this year.

Willows left the London-listed broker in June, where he held the position of Head of Business Development for its digital-assets offering. His remit also covered IG’s US crypto operations, including the tastycrypto self-custody wallet.

According to Willows’ LinkedIn profile, he left IG in June 2026, announcing a new chapter in his career. He joined Pepperstone in November 2026. Pepperstone has not published an updated description of the role.

Spot Crypto Adds a Second Product Model

Pepperstone started its crypto business in February, launching a spot trading platform under the Pepperstone Crypto brand. The model differs from the group’s CFD business as clients buy and hold the cryptoassets themselves instead of trading contracts that track prices.

The platform currently serves Australian clients and offers spot trading in major cryptocurrencies along with a limited range of tokenised US stocks and ETFs, which give price exposure to the referenced securities without ownership of the underlying shares.

Pepperstone Crypto is operated by Pepperstone Digital Pty Ltd, which is registered with AUSTRAC as a digital currency exchange provider. It operates separately from Pepperstone Group Limited’s ASIC-regulated CFD business.

Cross-Asset Role Goes Beyond Crypto

In an interview with Finance Magnates, Pepperstone described the cross-asset position as a link between its CFD, crypto and futures business lines.

The executive would report to Chief Operating Officer Tom Williams and develop a global product roadmap covering client demand, commercial models and potential expansion into new markets.

The mandate is to look at how the group can serve its existing client base across all asset classes and to look at the development of products in the context of longer trading hours, with a particular focus on the growth of 24/7 markets.

Willows' appointment gives that strategy a dedicated executive. The company has not yet said which products, markets or customer segments it will be focusing on.

title: US Futures Watchdog Posts Record $22.5 Million Surplus as It Halves Trading Fee
summary:
The National Futures Association (NFA), the self-regulatory body of the US futures industry, ended its last fiscal year with a record $22.5 million surplus. It got there with fewer member firms than in any year of the past decade, FM Intelligence analysis published today (Wednesday) shows.
Most of t...
content:
2026-11-25T16:40:00.000+02:00

Wednesday, 25/11/2026 | 14:40 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The self-regulator lives mostly off a per-contract charge customers pay, and contract volume kept growing.
  • The cut returns the charge to its pre-2018 level until mid-2027, while swap dealers face higher annual dues.

The National Futures Association (NFA), the self-regulatory body of the US futures industry, ended its last fiscal year with a record $22.5 million surplus. It got there with fewer member firms than in any year of the past decade, FM Intelligence analysis published today (Wednesday) shows.

Most of that money comes from a fee charged on every futures trade, which brokers pass on to customers as a separate line on their statements. Contract volume kept rising, and fee income grew for a fifth straight year in fiscal 2026.

In May, NFA's Board voted to cut the fee from 2 cents to 1 cent per side for 12 months from July 1, 2026, FM Intelligence's analysis of the association's fiscal 2026 accounts shows.

That takes the fee back to where it stood before NFA doubled it in January 2018, citing the need to fund its operations and keep adequate reserves. It was only the fourth increase in the association's history.

Who Pays the Fee

For a customer trading through a US broker, the charge on a round turn, the opening and closing of one contract, falls from 4 cents to 2 cents until June 30, 2027. Options on futures are charged per trade, and that rate also halves to 1 cent.

The fee covers more than traditional futures. Event contracts listed as futures and carried by a futures commission merchant (FCM) are assessable, which brings part of the prediction-market business into NFA's funding base.

That business is moving inside the NFA perimeter. Prediction-market apps have been registering as introducing brokers under existing FCMs, and Polymarket's affiliate received NFA approval to operate as an FCM in November.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC ), which oversees NFA, is writing a framework for event contracts, the product line behind several of NFA's newest registrations.

Swap Dealers Pay More

Not every member shares in the cut. Swap dealers, whose part of NFA's budget sits below the floor of the association's own reserve policy, face higher annual dues from July 2026 and again from July 2027.

The increase is not spread evenly. The lowest-paying of the three swap dealer tiers rises the most, by FM Intelligence's calculation.

NFA also budgets for a cash deficit in fiscal 2027, according to its May filing with the CFTC. How far fee income falls in the year of the cut depends on contract volume, which the association does not set.

The full FM Intelligence analysis puts a range on fiscal 2027 fee income, sets NFA's cushion against its reserve target and shows what each swap dealer tier pays through 2028.

The fee is scheduled to return to 2 cents per side on July 1, 2027.

title: CleanSpark May Sell More Bitcoin Than It Mines to Cut Treasury Risk After $987M Loss
summary:
Key Takeaways: The sale of some Bitcoin may be more than what CleanSpark mines due to minimizing treasure risk. The miner ended fiscal 2026 with 13,530 BTC worth about $1.1
The post CleanSpark May Sell More Bitcoin Than It Mines to Cut Treasury Risk After $987M Loss appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The sale of some Bitcoin may be more than what CleanSpark mines due to minimizing treasure risk.
  • The miner ended fiscal 2026 with 13,530 BTC worth about $1.1 billion.
  • Meanwhile, CleanSpark incurred a $987.1 million annual loss, despite Bitcoin’s drop in value.

Following a rough fiscal year with a drop in mining revenue, and a severe price volatility in the value of its BTC holdings, CleanSpark is adopting a more flexible strategy in management of its Bitcoin treasury.

It could sell as much Bitcoin as it produces in some quarters and use the proceeds to fuel operations and growth without being reliant upon new equity or debt, he says.

  • CleanSpark Signals More Active Bitcoin Selling
    • Bitcoin Becomes a Source of Non-Dilutive Capital
  • CleanSpark Ends FY2026 With 13,530 BTC
    • Bitcoin Price Swings Hit CleanSpark’s Results

CleanSpark Signals More Active Bitcoin Selling

On the part of the earnings call, CEO Gary Vecchiarelli said that the firm will be selling almost all the bitcoins produced monthly or in any given quarter to fund day-to-day operations.

He further noted that it may be necessary to sell a small portion of its production outside the quarterly period in order to limit treasury exposure as market conditions warrant. Unlike fixed formulas, CleanSpark makes decisions on selling bitcoins based on the liquidity needs, market conditions and risk management.

The strategy is more dynamic in pursuing Bitcoin as working capital, as opposed to holding it as a reserve asset.

Bitcoin Becomes a Source of Non-Dilutive Capital

CleanSpark said it had already sold additional Bitcoin after the September fiscal year-end to strengthen its cash position ahead of potential acquisitions.

Management has decided that selling BTCs and pledging BTCs as loans are options other than new equity sales. The company also generated $30.6 million in derivative-related proceeds during fiscal 2026 through its digital asset management program.

Read More: MSCI Cuts Strategy From Global Indexes, Putting Bitcoin Treasury Model Under Pressure

CleanSpark Ends FY2026 With 13,530 BTC

At the end of September, CleanSpark had 13,530 BTC, including 6299 BTC collateral, in its vault. Those holdings were valued at roughly $1.1 billion at the fiscal year-end price.

During fiscal 2026, the company’s total output was 7,253 BTC, which was a decline from 7,637 BTC it had produced during fiscal 2025. The average hashrate dropped 21% to 36 EH/s, and miner efficiency increased to 14.8 joules per terahash, up from 16.7 joules per terahash one year ago.

CleanSpark also slashed its own operating unit to approximately 200,000 machines for the year. Mining will proceed until profitable economics lists otherwise, said management.

Bitcoin Price Swings Hit CleanSpark’s Results

Full year revenue slipped 25% to $576.5 million, while CleanSpark enjoyed a net loss of $987.1 million, compared with a net income of $364 million in fiscal 2025. Adjusted EBITDA turned in a loss of $304.2 million.

The year-over-year earnings shift was driven by a mix of non-cash Bitcoin mark-to-market adjustments that accounted for about two-thirds of the earnings change, Management said. Bitcoin was valued at about $83,600 at the end of fiscal 2026, compared with roughly $114,000 a year earlier.

CleanSpark also posted a non-cash item of $177 million driven by the utility’s decision to shift its Sandersville facility from Bitcoin mining to AI data center operations.

title: Finery Markets Adds 20+ African and Latin American Currencies for Stablecoin Trading
summary:
Finery Markets added pricing in more than 20 African and Latin American currencies today (Wednesday) through a partnership with LINK. The Limassol-based company runs a trading network for institutional crypto firms.
LINK will stream stablecoin quotes in currencies including the Nigerian naira, Kenya...
content:
2026-11-25T16:05:08.840+02:00

Wednesday, 25/11/2026 | 14:05 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • LINK will stream naira, shilling and real quotes to the network's institutions and handle local payouts.
  • Sending money to Sub-Saharan Africa costs 8.46% on average, the most of any region, World Bank data show.

Finery Markets added pricing in more than 20 African and Latin American currencies today (Wednesday) through a partnership with LINK. The Limassol-based company runs a trading network for institutional crypto firms.

LINK will stream stablecoin quotes in currencies including the Nigerian naira, Kenyan shilling, Brazilian real and Mexican peso. Much of that trading still runs manually over chat, Finery Markets said.

The quotes reach the costliest region to send money to. Transfers to Sub-Saharan Africa cost 8.46% of the amount sent on average, the highest of any region, according to World Bank data cited by the company.

Stablecoins carried 83% of trades on its network in the first nine months of 2026, the company said. Its annual report had put their share of institutional OTC volume at 78% in 2025, up from 23% in 2023.

Africa's Cash-Out Spreads Run Above Latin America's

Sergey Klinkov, managing director at Finery Markets, described the regions as markets "where stablecoins thrive the most, yet they're still the hardest markets to reach."

The last step, turning stablecoins into local money, is where the two regions differ most.

A January review of 66 African stablecoin routes by payments firm Borderless.xyz put Africa's median conversion spread at 299 basis points, or about 3%, against roughly 1.3% in Latin America, as FinanceMagnates.com reported in February.

The naira, shilling and Ghanaian cedi all clustered near 300 basis points in that review. By FinanceMagnates.com's calculation, the African median was more than twice the Latin American one.

LINK Handles the Local Payout

Institutions on the network, which the company puts at more than 150 firms, reach LINK's pairs through their existing connection. LINK then converts the stablecoins and pays out through regulated partners, under tightening local rules.

Nigeria's central bank requires foreign dollar-stablecoin issuers to hold NGN15 billion (about $11.1 million) in a local company, and approves remittances separately, while Kenya's draft rules propose KES 500 million ($3.86 million) for stablecoin issuers, FM Intelligence data show.

LINK sells an API that lets fintechs and payment firms convert and settle FX and stablecoin transactions, including through mobile money.

Emmanuel Evarist, co-founder and CEO of LINK, said Finery Markets' technology "lets us scale our pricing across a global network of institutional counterparties instantly."

Finery Markets, founded in 2019, reports more than $75 billion in cumulative trading volume and 150 institutional clients in 40 countries, including brokers, OTC desks and hedge funds.
