title: Coinbase Joins Dublin Crackdown on North Korean Crypto Heists and Fake IT Workers
summary:
Key Takeaways: Coinbase partnered with U.S. and Irish authorities to combat North Korean cyber crime. Discussions were centred around crypto theft and fake IT from stolen identities of all. According
The post Coinbase Joins Dublin Crackdown on North Korean Crypto Heists and Fake IT Workers appeared ...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Coinbase partnered with U.S. and Irish authorities to combat North Korean cyber crime.
  • Discussions were centred around crypto theft and fake IT from stolen identities of all.
  • According to TRM Labs, North Korean hackers have stolen approximately $7.4 billion in crypto in 2026.

Coinbase has joined law enforcement, government agencies and security specialists in Dublin for a two-day meeting focused on disrupting North Korean cyber operations targeting the crypto industry.

Attendees included investigators from the FBI, FinCEN, and Irish cybercrime police, as well as private-sector security teams aiming to enhance the detection, reporting and tracking of attacks.

  • Coinbase and Law Enforcement Target DPRK Crypto Crime
    • Fake Jobs Remain a Major Entry Point
  • North Korea’s Crypto Theft Hits Record Scale
    • Exchanges Help Trace and Freeze Stolen Crypto

Coinbase and Law Enforcement Target DPRK Crypto Crime

Coinbase co-sponsored the Dublin symposium with the U.S. Department of State’s Office of Cooperative Threat Reduction. The program was also facilitated with the support of Global Affairs Canada, Google and Payward.

The two primary risks were Pyongyang-backed cryptocurrency theft and actors impersonating tech job offers on the Internet.

According to Coinbase some of the attacks involve legitimate recruitment emails, interview invitations or requests to download software at first. If an employee does so, attackers can gain entry to a company’s systems or credentials.

There’s one other strategy operating in reverse. North Korean IT workers register for remote positions with fake profiles so they can work and may be given access to critical company systems.

Read More: Coinbase Launches Crypto Options Globally, Bringing Deribit Liquidity to Retail Traders

Fake Jobs Remain a Major Entry Point

The Dublin meeting considered ways to identify slick applications and bogus recruitment drives before they become a security incident.

Which is particularly relevant for a crypto company, as its staff might have access to wallets, infrastructure or in-house security tools. Generally, they also spoke about what evidence should be saved after an attack and the speed of notifying authorities.

North Korea’s Crypto Theft Hits Record Scale

It is a meeting given its unusual level of expense for the crypto industry throughout the last year. TRM Labs estimates North Korean-affiliated thieves taking around USD 7.4B worth of cryptocurrency in 2026 via to October 29 makes up about 85% of hack losses of cryptocurrencies in the TRM Labs dataset. With the lack of the scandalous Binance hack, it would drop to 45%.

TRM estimates North Korean groups have robbed about $12.8 billion of crypto since 2017.

As losses are in huge numbers, the need to trace them back to the blockchain has grown more and more urgent. Public ledgers can identify where stolen money goes and exchanges and other analytics companies as well as stablecoin issuers can intervene at various points in the laundering process before assets are completely removed.

Exchanges Help Trace and Freeze Stolen Crypto

Coinbase stated that they cooperate with blockchain analytics companies and law enforcement to trace stolen assets, blacklist threatening addresses and assist the freezes if legally and technically feasible. That’s the kind of speed coordination can make a difference, as evidenced at recent enforcement activity.

The U.S. Justice Department on Nov. 23 sought the forfeiture of over $1.1 billion in USDC allegedly stolen by North Korea-related actors from Binance. U.S. officials reported that they had successfully helped to freeze, seize or recover over $2.9 billion in crypto assets linked to the heist.

title: Crypto News Today: Bitcoin’s $58K Battle Intensifies as Ethereum Risks $1,237 and XRP Longs Slip Underwater
summary: Bitcoin is struggling near $58,000 as options-market positioning leaves little cushion, while Ethereum and XRP face renewed pressure around key on-chain cost-basis levels.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC ETH XRP

Bitcoin is struggling near $58,000 as options-market positioning leaves little cushion, while Ethereum and XRP face renewed pressure around key on-chain cost-basis levels.

The latest market signals point to growing stress across major cryptocurrencies, with Glassnode highlighting increased downside volatility, weakening US demand, and significant investor losses.

Bitcoin Price Today: $58K–$64K Gamma Zone Raises Volatility Risks

Bitcoin traded around $58,500–$59,000 on November 25, returning to levels last seen during its summer decline. The move has also pushed BTC below the lowest Fire Sale band on the Rainbow Chart version highlighted in recent market discussions. The chart uses logarithmic regression to compare Bitcoin’s historical closing prices with a long-term growth curve, dividing the results into colored bands that represent different market valuations.

Based on historical daily closes, the chart shows the price is now outside its full model range. Source: @Cryptoze/X

The unusual deviation raises questions about the model’s usefulness during the 2026 correction. However, the Rainbow Chart is a historical valuation reference rather than a predictive indicator. Its calculations also vary across providers, with different regression periods and band settings producing different classifications for the same Bitcoin price. Consequently, moving outside one chart’s modeled range does not necessarily invalidate the broader framework. Previous periods of deep undervaluation have preceded recoveries, but they have not reliably identified market bottoms.

Options positioning presents a more immediate concern. Glassnode’s November 24 Week The on-chain report identified a short gamma zone between $58,000 and $64,000, where dealer hedging could amplify Bitcoin’s price movements.

Bitcoin is trading in a $58K–$64K short-gamma zone, where options dealers’ hedging now amplifies price swings by selling dips and buying rallies. Source: Glassnode via X

When options dealers are short gamma, they generally need to sell Bitcoin as prices decline and buy as prices recover to maintain their hedges. This behavior can reinforce existing price movements rather than reduce volatility. Glassnode noted that the current trading range offers little support from dealer hedging, warning that a move starting within the zone could pick up speed.

The report also identified long gamma positioning between $56,000 and $58,000 and between $64,000 and $66,000. In those ranges, dealer hedging could help moderate price swings. However, Bitcoin’s recent decline has already weakened its nearby support structure. Glassnode reported that the $62,000–$66,000 support zone broke on November 19, followed by an intraday decline to approximately $55,300 on November 21.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Glassnode also highlighted weakening institutional demand from the United States. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $4.3 billion in net outflows over 20 trading days, while Coinbase spot traders remained net sellers over the previous 30 days. Meanwhile, Binance activity showed a more balanced relationship between buying and selling.

The report identified Bitcoin’s realized price near $53,200 as another important reference point. This metric represents the average price at which existing coins last moved on-chain. Glassnode noted that previous bear markets eventually pushed BTC below this level, although Bitcoin has not yet recorded a sustained move beneath it during the current downturn.

Ethereum Price Risks $1,237 as Cost-Basis Support Weakens

Ethereum faces a separate challenge as its price falls below a significant historical acquisition zone. On-chain analyst Ali Martinez highlighted a Glassnode cost-basis distribution chart showing approximately 1.14 million ETH acquired around $1,680.

Ethereum has fallen below the $1,680 cost-basis level, putting approximately 1.14 million ETH holders at risk of further losses and increasing downside pressure. Source: Ali Martinez via X

With ETH trading near $1,640 on November 25, the price has moved below that concentration. The development leaves a substantial group of holders facing unrealized losses and raises concerns about whether buyers will defend the lower price levels.

The distribution chart identifies relatively thinner supply concentration below $1,584, with the next notable clusters appearing around $1,237 and $1,089. Approximately 1.37 million ETH were acquired around $1,237, while another 968,000 ETH have a recorded acquisition level near $1,089.

These concentrations offer potential reference zones if selling pressure continues. However, cost-basis distribution does not measure available buy orders or guarantee that investors will defend a particular price. It reflects where existing holdings were acquired or last recorded at an average acquisition price, making it useful for understanding potential areas of investor reaction.

Ethereum (ETH) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

A decline toward $1,237 would represent a substantial extension of Ethereum’s current correction. Whether ETH reaches that level will depend on market demand, broader cryptocurrency sentiment, and the ability of buyers to stabilize prices above the nearer support areas.

Martinez included Ethereum in his broader “prepare for the worst” analysis covering Bitcoin and XRP. The assessment highlights how weakening market conditions are affecting the cost-basis positions of holders across multiple large-cap cryptocurrencies.

XRP Price Faces $0.84 Support as Long Positions Slip Underwater

XRP is also approaching an important on-chain support level as the broader cryptocurrency market remains under pressure. The token traded around $0.91–$0.92 on November 25, remaining above the $0.84 cost-basis zone highlighted by Martinez.

XRP faces immediate cost-basis support at $0.84, with potential downside targets at $0.62 and $0.36 if selling pressure intensifies. Source: Ali Martinez via X

According to the analyst’s Glassnode-based chart, approximately 833 million XRP were acquired around $0.84. A sustained move below this level could expose lower historical acquisition clusters around $0.62 and $0.36.

The chart identifies approximately 1.11 billion XRP around $0.62, followed by a substantially larger concentration of 6.57 billion XRP around $0.36. These levels could become relevant in a deeper correction, although the size of a cost-basis cluster does not establish that buyers will return at those prices.

Derivatives positioning adds another source of pressure. Coinbase Markets published a Glassnode chart on November 24 showing XRP’s net open positioning by average entry price. The largest concentration of net long positions was recorded around $0.982, while XRP’s spot price stood near $0.923.

XRP is trading 6% below the $0.982 entry level of its largest net-long cluster, leaving nearly all leveraged long positions underwater. Source: Coinbase Markets via X

The difference places the largest group of these positions approximately 6% below their average entry price. The distribution also indicates that nearly all the recorded net long notional sits above the prevailing spot price, leaving much of the positioning underwater.

This creates a difficult situation for traders holding bullish positions. Some may decide to maintain their exposure in anticipation of a recovery, while others could reduce positions to limit further losses. Additional selling or forced position closures could increase pressure if XRP loses nearby support.

XRP price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The distinction between spot cost-basis levels and derivatives positioning is important. The $0.84 zone reflects an on-chain acquisition concentration, whereas the $0.982 level represents the average entry price of a significant group of outstanding net long positions. Together, they show pressure emerging across both spot holdings and speculative trading activity.

Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP Face Mounting Market Pressure

The latest indicators reveal different but interconnected risks across the three cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin is contending with negative dealer gamma, weak US buying activity, and a breakdown of its previous support range. Ethereum is trading below a significant acquisition cluster, while XRP faces pressure from both underwater derivatives positions and declining on-chain support levels.

Glassnode’s November 24 report also identified elevated options-market bearishness, with puts changing hands at approximately 1.7 times the number of calls on a seven-day average. That represented the highest reading since June 2022. The report further noted that realized losses had climbed to their highest levels since the FTX collapse in November 2022.

These readings point to widespread investor stress, although they do not establish that the current correction has reached its final stage. Bitcoin’s ability to regain the $60,000 level, Ethereum’s response to its lower acquisition zones, and XRP’s defense of $0.84 remain important areas to monitor.

For now, the three assets are showing signs of weakening market confidence. A sustained recovery in demand could ease the pressure, but continued selling would leave their respective support structures exposed to further tests.

title: BossaFX's Owner Builds a New Brand for People Who Never Open a Trading App
summary:
Poland's DM BOŚ launched a managed investment service on Friday aimed at savers who keep their money in bank accounts. Sold under a new brand, Investia, it puts clients into exchange-traded funds (ETFs) picked by licensed advisers.
The brokerage arm of Bank Ochrony Środowiska is chasing the same ret...
content:
2026-11-25T14:35:00.000+02:00

Wednesday, 25/11/2026 | 12:35 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • Investia, run by DM BOŚ, puts savers into adviser-picked ETF portfolios from PLN 1,000 for 1.2% a year.
  • XTB, which opened 33 times as many Polish accounts in a year, already sells ready-made plans without commission.

Poland's DM BOŚ launched a managed investment service on Friday aimed at savers who keep their money in bank accounts. Sold under a new brand, Investia, it puts clients into exchange-traded funds (ETFs) picked by licensed advisers.

The brokerage arm of Bank Ochrony Środowiska is chasing the same retail money that made XTB the largest player in Polish brokerage. At the end of October it ran 200,836 accounts, or about 6.4% of the market, while XTB held 42%, according to the Central Securities Depository of Poland (KDPW).

DM BOŚ said more than PLN 1 trillion (about $250 billion) of Polish household savings sits in accounts that pay no interest. Investia takes deposits from PLN 1,000 and charges 0.1% a month including VAT, or 1.2% a year.

A Separate Brand From Bossa

DM BOŚ has traded for more than 30 years as Bossa, which sells Warsaw-listed and foreign stocks and ETFs, investment funds through Bossafund and contracts for difference through its BossaFX platform.

It chose a new name for Investia because, it said, savers often see the stock market as too risky.

"The Bossa brand is strongly associated with the stock exchange and active investors," Bogdan Koczorowski, a management board member at DM BOŚ, told Bankier.pl.

After a short suitability questionnaire, Investia assigns one of four base strategies matched to the client's risk profile.

At least 80% of the money stays in that base portfolio, and clients can steer up to 20% into themes such as commodities, sectors, regions or bonds, which the managers then fill with ETFs.

Early clients pay no fee for a year. The waiver covers anyone who opens and funds an account by the end of February 2027.

DM BOŚ plans to connect Investia to IKE and IKZE retirement accounts and to the new OKI personal investment accounts in early 2027. Retirement wrappers have been the entry point for many Polish investors, with 170,000 IKE accounts opened in 2024, the most in 18 years, FM Intelligence data show.

The Distance to XTB

On account openings, the gap between the two firms keeps widening. XTB added 620,262 Polish accounts in the 12 months to October, about 33 times the 18,784 DM BOŚ added, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation from KDPW data.

DM BOŚ still crossed 200,000 accounts in October, ranking fifth behind XTB and the brokerage arms of mBank, Bank Pekao and ING Bank Śląski.

XTB also targets passive savers, but leaves the choices to the client. Its Investment Plans let Polish users build portfolios of stocks and ETFs or pick a ready-made plan by risk profile, from PLN 50, its website shows.

The ready-made plans arrived with a redesign XTB began rolling out across Europe in July, and purchases inside a plan carry no commission up to a monthly turnover cap.

XTB was tested this week. Some clients reported that its app slowed or would not log them in after the US open on Monday, when Nvidia shares rallied. XTB said yesterday (Tuesday) that platform traffic in that window ran 90% above a typical November US open, in a statement sent to Money.pl.

XTB said its platform stayed available, apologized for what it called temporary difficulties and pointed affected clients to its complaints procedure. In August, XTB's web platform failed to load around the US open, a day before its shares set a record.

Commissions Under Pressure

Fees have been the main battleground since Trade Republic entered Poland in September 2025, when DM BOŚ matched mBank's zero-commission ETF trading in IKE and IKZE accounts.

"Revenue from brokerage commissions depends heavily on the stock market cycle," Koczorowski said, adding that market rates tend to fall.

DM BOŚ adopted a strategy in March to build asset management into a second source of revenue alongside brokerage. Under Investia, it charges a 0.5% fee on money withdrawn within 12 months of being paid in.

title: HyroTrader Adds Hyro Core From $9 and No-Evaluation Hyro Instant to Rebuilt Crypto Prop Platform
summary: The new accounts follow an October overhaul that brought the firm’s own trading terminal, AI-agent trading, BloFin and static loss limits on every challenge   DUBAI, UAE, November 2026: HyroTrader, a crypto proprietary trading firm, has launched two new ways to get a funded trading account. Hyro Cor...
content:
The new accounts follow an October overhaul that brought the firm’s own trading terminal, AI-agent trading, BloFin and static loss limits on every challenge

DUBAI, UAE, November 2026: HyroTrader, a crypto proprietary trading firm, has launched two new ways to get a funded trading account. Hyro Core is a one-phase challenge from $9, and Hyro Instant skips the challenge altogether. Both went on sale on 4 November 2026.

They are the second step of a rebuild that began in October. That month HyroTrader launched its own trading terminal with stock and index contracts and opened accounts on it to AI trading agents. It also added BloFin as a second exchange, made every loss limit static and made its payouts easier to verify on a public dashboard.

Firms like HyroTrader give traders a funded account and pay them a share of the profit made on it. Traders usually earn that account by passing a paid trading test, known as a challenge.

At HyroTrader, every account, funded or not, is a simulated (demo) account running on live market data. The payouts are real money, paid as a share of the simulated profit.

Hyro Instant is the bigger change for a firm that until now funded only traders who passed a challenge.

“Without an evaluation, a firm cannot establish whether a trader has a consistent track record or simply had a few successful trades,” HyroTrader said in announcing Hyro Instant. “Nevertheless, the demand for a faster route is clear.”

Hyro Core is the firm’s lowest-priced challenge. A $2,500 account costs $9, and the largest, $100,000, costs $349. Against One-Step, the firm’s other one-phase challenge, it pairs the lower price with tighter loss limits.

To pass, a trader needs a 10% profit over at least four trading days, with no single day counting for more than 40% of it. The challenge ends if the account loses more than 3% of its starting balance in a day, or 5% in total. Both limits are static, which means they stay fixed to the starting balance and do not rise as the account gains.

Funded Hyro Core traders receive a fixed 80% of the profit as payouts. The fee is not refunded once the challenge is activated.

“A trader’s budget does not necessarily reflect their motivation or skill,” HyroTrader said in announcing Hyro Core.

Hyro Instant, a funded account with no evaluation. Image: HyroTrader

Hyro Instant has no test at all. After identity verification and account setup, the trader receives a funded account with no profit target to reach. It costs from $169 for a $5,000 account to $2,799 for $100,000.

It keeps Hyro Core’s daily and total loss limits and adds a per-trade limit. No single trade may lose more than 2% of the starting balance. A first breach of that trade limit brings a warning, and a second closes the account.

The first payout opens after three qualifying trading days (days on which the trader closes at least one trade above set size and price-move thresholds), with the account in profit. The profit split starts at 80% and can rise to 90% at the firm’s discretion. The fee is refunded only if identity verification is not approved.

Both new accounts run on what HyroTrader built in October. At the centre is the Hyro platform, the firm’s own trading terminal, which needs no exchange account. It offers more than 700 perpetual futures markets (contracts with no expiry date) on live prices. Besides crypto, they include contracts on stocks such as Apple, Nvidia and Tesla, on the S&P 500, and on gold and silver.

Traders who prefer an exchange can instead run any programme on their own demo account at Bybit or, since October, at BloFin. HyroTrader says that in 2023 it became the first crypto prop firm to let traders run a challenge on their own exchange demo account.

On the Hyro platform, Hyro Instant accounts included, traders can also connect their own AI agent through MCP, the Model Context Protocol (an open standard for linking AI tools to other software). The agent places trades for the trader’s own strategy under the account’s usual rules, and the trader can revoke its access at any time.

The October rebuild also made payouts easier to check. HyroTrader lists the payouts it sends on the Solana blockchain on a public transparency page, each with a link to its blockchain record unless the trader has chosen to hide it. In November the minimum payout fell from $100 to $25.

The firm also eased its existing challenges in the same week. One-Step challenges bought from 5 November need at least three trading days instead of five and allow an 8% total loss limit instead of 6%. Two-Step challenges bought from 4 November need four trading days in each phase instead of five.

About HyroTrader

HyroTrader is a crypto prop firm launched in 2023 and operating from Dubai, UAE. Traders take a challenge or start funded with Hyro Instant, receive 80% of their profits as payouts, up to 90% on some programmes, and are usually paid in stablecoins within 24 hours.

According to HyroTrader’s public payout transparency page, the firm has paid more than $9.5 million in profit splits to traders since 2023, as of November 2026. More than $1.6 million of that went out on the Solana blockchain. HyroTrader says it has funded more than 1,700 traders.

HyroTrader is not a broker and does not provide investment services or advice. All trading takes place on simulated accounts.

title: Ethereum (ETH) Price Prediction: $1,500 Make-or-Break Support Could Decide Between $2,000 Rally and Sub $1,000-Crash
summary: Ethereum (ETH) is approaching a critical $1,500 support zone as BlackRock selling and BitMine accumulation raise questions over a potential bottom or deeper breakdown.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ETH

Ethereum (ETH) is approaching a critical $1,500 support zone as BlackRock selling and BitMine accumulation raise questions over a potential bottom or deeper breakdown.

Ethereum (ETH) recently traded near $1,675, with technical analysts identifying the $1,500-$1,600 region as the next major support zone. While a successful defense of this area could support a recovery toward $2,000, longer-term chart analysis identifies $1,383 as a critical structural support, below which the risk of a deeper correction toward $1,000 increases.

Ethereum Price Breakdown Puts $1,500 Back in Focus

Ethereum’s weekly structure has weakened considerably after losing the support that held through much of the second half of 2026. Crypto Patel highlights a confirmed break of structure, with ETH now trading around $1,690 and moving back toward the horizontal support near $1,504.

That level matters because it sits near the lows formed earlier this year. A successful defense would give Ethereum another chance to establish a larger double-bottom structure, but a clean weekly breakdown below $1,500 would leave far less support underneath.

ETH has already lost the recovery trend, and bulls now need the $1,500 region to hold before the market can start discussing another meaningful higher-timeframe rebound.

Ethereum is approaching the $1,500 support region after a confirmed weekly structure breakdown. Source: Crypto Patel via X.

Analyst Warns $1,383 As Key Support

The bearish case becomes more serious on Peter Brandt’s long-term weekly chart. Ethereum is still trading above the rising support line that has guided the larger structure since the 2022 lows, but price is now moving much closer to the area where that structure would begin to fail.

Ethereum remains above its long-term rising support, but Peter Brandt sees approximately $1,383 as the critical level bulls need to defend. Source: Peter Brandt via X.

Brandt identifies approximately $1,383 as the critical level beneath the market. If ETH cannot remain above that region, the higher-timeframe structure would weaken considerably, and the risk of a move below $1,000 would increase.

That gives the current $1,500-$1,600 region even more importance. Bulls still have some room to defend the broader trend, but another sharp move lower would bring Ethereum uncomfortably close to Brandt’s larger breakdown level.

BlackRock Sells as BitMine Keeps Buying the ETH Dip

Large investors are taking opposite sides of Ethereum’s latest decline. Whale Insider reports that BlackRock ETF clients sold approximately $90.54 million worth of ETH, keeping institutional flow pressure elevated while price moves deeper into the correction.

Meanwhile, BitMine is doing the opposite. In a post on X Cointelegraph reports that Tom Lee’s company purchased another 7,819 ETH, taking its total holdings to approximately 6.09 million ETH, or around 4.98% of Ethereum’s total supply. The company is continuing to add while ETH trades near some of its weakest levels of the year.

That split makes the current range more interesting. ETF clients appear to be reducing exposure as price falls, while BitMine is using the same weakness to increase an already enormous position. Neither side confirms where Ethereum will bottom, but the contrast shows that the selloff is not being treated the same way by every large market participant.

Contrary View: Recovery Opening Toward $2,000

Not every higher-timeframe view expects the decline to keep extending. PILTR’s roadmap treats the $1,500-$1,600 region as a potential base rather than the beginning of a much deeper breakdown, although the chart still allows for more volatility before buyers regain control.

For the broader Ethereum Price Prediction, a successful reaction from this zone could first bring $2,000 back into focus. If buyers continue rebuilding from there, the recovery path extends toward $2,500-$2,800, turning the current selloff into a potential accumulation phase rather than a complete structural failure.

That makes the reaction around $1,500-$1,600 particularly important. A strong defense would support PILTR’s recovery scenario, while another sustained breakdown would shift the balance back toward the deeper bearish levels highlighted by Brandt.

PILTR’s roadmap sees $1,500-$1,600 as a potential higher-timeframe base before a recovery toward $2,000 and eventually $2,500-$2,800. Source: PILTR via X.

Where Can ETH Price Finally Stabilize?

ETH price is reaching a stage of the correction where the behavior around the lows matters more than another single red candle. Several higher-timeframe views are now pointing toward the same broad $1,500-$1,600 region, making this the area where buyers have the best opportunity to slow the decline.

A bottom does not need to begin with an explosive recovery. What bulls first want to see is selling pressure losing momentum, repeated defense of the lows, and price gradually reclaiming territory instead of immediately making another lower low. That would suggest the market is starting to absorb the supply hitting it.

If that process develops, $1,800-$1,900 could become the first meaningful recovery area before attention moves back toward $2,000 and above. Until then, Ethereum is still searching for stability rather than showing a confirmed bottom.

Q4 2026: Capitulation or Bottom?

Brave New Coin’s price chart shows that ETH has surrendered almost its entire recovery from the June lows, falling from approximately $2,750 in September to $1,644. The formation of successive lower highs and lower lows throughout Q4 reflects persistent selling pressure, with the market now approaching the same $1,500–$1,600 region that supported its previous multi-month recovery.

Ethereum price is trading at around $1,653, down 3.18% in the last 24 hours. Source: Brave New Coin

For the broader Ethereum Price Prediction, the final weeks of Q4 could determine whether ETH establishes a larger double bottom or extends its bearish trend into 2027. A sustained defense of $1,500, followed by a recovery above $1,900–$2,000, would provide early evidence of structural improvement. However, losing the June lows would expose the critical $1,383 support, below which the risk of a deeper correction toward $1,000 increases considerably.

title: Gold Price Analysis as $3,500 Support Shapes the Next Market Move
summary: Gold's latest correction lower has opened the door for $3,500 again now that sellers have taken out the key retracement level.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XAG

Gold's latest correction lower has opened the door for $3,500 again now that sellers have taken out the key retracement level.

Gold has seen its second day of losses in the past week. While the metal is trading above $3,558, last week’s November pattern continues to lose energy and erodes the much broader recovery formation. James Stanley had identified $3,608 as support, though the latest trading data from TradingView shows it was not defended.

Gold Breaks $3,608 as Sellers Target $3,500

James Stanley’s X analysis yields $3,608 as the 50% retracement of the 2022-2026 gold rally. The chart features an uptrend line that had held with prior higher lows until the latest correction finally pushed through the line. Gold then moved back toward the horizontal support zone near $3,608, which Stanley viewed as a level to form a new higher low.

TradingView update: The daily candle had an opening value of $3,634.77, a high of $3,678.33, and a low of $3,552.90. Source: Stanley Via X

The market shows at the time of writing, XAU/USD was trading at $3,557.96, losing 2.11%. The other downside target that is highlighted is $3,500, which is the next major target. Stanley says this is the line in the sand.

As such, we need the buyer to recapture $3,608 to shift the near-term structure. Otherwise, we start to risk another flush towards $3,500. A firm breakdown below here would further erode the multi-month bull recovery setup.

Oversold Momentum And Additional Risk To The Downside

On the other hand, the daily TradingView chart for gold shows a persistent downtrend the entire time. Gold prices have been sliding lower since August from about $4,650, setting lower highs and lower lows along the way. Gold’s descent picked up steam in November by losing the $4,000 and $3,800 levels and falling through $3,608.

RVI is currently at 25.53 versus the 36.83 reading for its signal average. Both readings are below the 50 midpoint of the indicator, while the main line sits closer to the lower 20 range, suggesting a lack of momentum and strong downside pressure. The RVI is not a volume indicator; it is a relative volatility index.

Gold’s near-term resistance currently lies near 3,600-3,680, which includes the fractured support zone and the open/high of the current candle. Source: TradingView

A break above this zone could lead to a test of the $3,800 level, followed by $4,000. Near-term support is now seen near the 3,550-3,500 range. If that region gives way, the yellow metal could extend its decline, although the provided charts do not show the next clear support level.

What Traders Should Be Looking At Next

If the gold price trades below $3,608, traders will need to see if it can hold the key support zone of 3,550-3,500. To the downside, momentum will be considered to be improving if the yellow metal can hold a break below $3,500, with signs of a lift above $3,608 revealing the first evidence of improving momentum. Resistance is seen at $3,680 and then $3,800. The Relative Volatility Index has to get back above its 36.83 signal average.

For the time being, the daily structure has continued to favor sellers. Buyers have to take back $3,608 and form higher lows before the recovery scenario will have more convincingly confirmed technical support.

title: Crypto Bought the Gold Story. Mines Are a Different Business.
summary:
Tether, the company behind USDT, issues the gold-backed token Tether Gold. In a November filing, it disclosed a 14.6% stake in Metalla Royalty & Streaming. That's on top of its purchase of a 32% stake in gold royalty company Elemental Altus last year.

content:
2026-11-25T13:42:44.453+02:00

Wednesday, 25/11/2026 | 11:42 GMT by FM

Disclaimer

  • Tether’s move into gold royalties brings crypto capital closer to mining. Anyone following it there needs to judge mines as businesses, not as stand-ins for bullion.

Tether, the company behind USDT, issues the gold-backed token Tether Gold. In a November filing, it disclosed a 14.6% stake in Metalla Royalty & Streaming. That's on top of its purchase of a 32% stake in gold royalty company Elemental Altus last year.

These companies give miners upfront capital in exchange for mine revenue or the right to buy a share of future production. In my view, that gives Tether some of the most direct exposure to mining revenue within the crypto industry.

Investors have long debated whether Bitcoin is digital gold and whether tokenized gold offers the best of both worlds. Far less attention has gone to the businesses that find, build and operate gold mines, and how they’re financed.

The industry has changed

Mining has a history of overspending, poorly timed acquisitions and disappointing returns, so it’s not a business to jump into without first doing your homework and understanding the stakes. A 2019 McKinsey analysis found that large gold miners wrote down the value of their assets by about $129 billion after gold peaked in 2011.

As dollars have flocked to gold in the past few years, stronger balance sheets and capital discipline have put these companies back in order. Sprott Asset Management notes that net debt across the gold miners index is at a 20-year low. That gives investors a reason to look again at what those businesses earn and how they spend it.

The World Gold Council reports that average all-in sustaining costs rose 22% year over year to about $1,930 an ounce in the second quarter of this year. Gold averaged about $4,500 over the same period, leaving a gap of more than $2,500 an ounce above sustaining costs. That is before financing costs, taxes and the cost of building new mines.

How new mines get financed

Strong margins at existing mines don’t always finance the next round of projects. Developers have to pay for construction and equipment before the mine begins to sell. A production-linked financing deal can cover those costs in exchange for a claim on the gold the project is expected to deliver.

S&P Global found that mines across a range of metals that started production between 2020 and 2024 took almost 18 years to go from discovery to production. Exploration, permitting and financing all extend that timeline. Additional capital can help when funding is the obstacle.

I have worked in mining for more than 25 years. As CFO of Lake Shore Gold during the financial crisis, I helped raise more than $500 million to develop gold mines. That taught me that a valuable deposit can’t do anything without the financing and management to build it.

Royalty companies are one way investors get exposure to that financing. Developers can also raise money through streaming deals or prepayments for future gold deliveries. That gives miners cash in exchange for a commitment tied to future production. Some of those rights could be tokenized. A token holder would need the same answers as any streaming investor, and one more: who holds the contract if the mine misses a delivery.

Rio2’s 2024 financing for its Fenix Gold project in Chile is a recent example of how that arrangement works. The terms were a $100 million prepayment commitment from Wheaton Precious Metals, a streaming company, in exchange for 95,000 ounces of gold, with deliveries scheduled to begin this year and run until 2032, plus payments to Rio2 equal to 20% of the spot gold price on delivery. Alongside equity financing, that commitment formed part of the package that completed its construction funding.

For investors, the return depends on the value of that future gold exceeding the upfront capital and later payments. They have to wait several years and accept the risk that production can fall short.

Gold in the ground isn’t gold in a vault

Investors who want exposure to the gold price may reasonably prefer bullion. Mining shares don’t simply track the price of gold, as a higher price can widen a producer’s margin, while a falling price can squeeze it just as quickly, more so if costs are rising.

Explorers and developers carry even more risk; early-stage exploration is akin to high risk investments like biotech research. Investors fund drilling to find out whether a deposit exists and can be mined. A discovery can create substantial value, but many projects never become mines.

A deposit’s value isn’t simply the ounces in the ground multiplied by the gold price. You have to work out how much gold can be recovered, what it will cost to build and operate the mine, and how long it will take to sell the first ounce. If a token gives you a claim on future production, its value depends on whether the mine gets built and delivers.

Anyone putting capital into mines should start with a few questions: Does the deposit have the grade, size and location to support economic mine operations? Is there a path to permits and financing? Has a team raised capital and worked on projects before, and can its funding plan withstand delays?

Bitcoin’s supply is set by code. Gold’s is set by geology, capital and the people who know how to turn a deposit into a mine. Crypto investors already own some of the metal. Anyone looking further down the supply chain should know that a mine is a business first, and judge it that way.

Mario Stifano is CEO of Galantas Gold Corporation (TSX-V & AIM: GAL), a gold and copper company with projects in Chile.

title: Cardano Price Prediction: $0.15 Support Faces Critical Test as Analysts Eye $0.25 Recovery
summary: Cardano (ADA) holds near critical $0.15 support as Bitfinex longs accumulate and CME liquidity expands, with traders watching for a potential recovery toward $0.25.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ADA

Cardano (ADA) holds near critical $0.15 support as Bitfinex longs accumulate and CME liquidity expands, with traders watching for a potential recovery toward $0.25.

Cardano (ADA) recently traded near $0.15, according to Brave New Coin, with technical analysts identifying the $0.14-$0.15 region as a critical support zone following an extended decline.

Despite holding above support, ADA remains under pressure, with traders watching liquidity below $0.14 as a potential downside target. Longer-term chart projections identify $0.25 and $0.41 as potential recovery levels, although the current price structure has yet to confirm a broader bullish reversal.

ADA Holds $0.15 Support as Liquidity Remains Below

Cardano has managed to hold the same support region that has attracted buyers several times during the recent decline. Analysts place that area around $0.15, with ADA stabilizing just above it after another sharp move lower.

There is one issue bulls still need to deal with. AllCryptoGem’s ADA chart shows an unswept low sitting beneath the current price around the lower-$0.14 region, leaving a pocket of liquidity that could still be tested before a cleaner recovery develops. A brief move below support followed by a quick reclaim would therefore look very different from a sustained breakdown.

Cardano continues to defend support near $0.15. Source: AllCryptoGems via X.

For now, the support remains intact, but the stronger bullish signal would come after ADA deals with that lower liquidity and begins reclaiming the recent breakdown levels. Until then, the market is holding rather than reversing.

Cardano Price Prediction Targets $0.41 and Higher

The broader structure remains corrective, but Cardano price is approaching an area where previous channel moves have started to change direction. Famous crypto analyst Lana Valentis highlights ADA moving toward the midline of a larger descending channel, an area that could become the next important reaction point if buyers remain active around current prices.

The chart maps a much wider recovery path if that reaction develops. $0.25 stands out as the first larger target, followed by $0.41 and $0.78, while $1.18 and $3.00 sit much further out in the cycle. Those levels should be viewed as stages of a recovery rather than immediate targets from $0.15.

The setup therefore starts much closer to current price. ADA first needs to stop making new lows and turn the channel midline into a base. If that happens, the market can begin looking toward $0.25 as the first level capable of changing the tone of the larger structure.

Cardano is approaching the midline of its descending channel, with $0.25 becoming the first larger recovery level. Source: Lana Valentis via X.

Bitfinex ADA Longs Show Multi-Year Accumulation

While ADA price remains weak, positioning on Bitfinex has been considerably more stable. Jesse Peralta highlights ADA long exposure that has largely remained inside a broad accumulation range since mid-2022, with current positioning sitting around 7.02 million ADA.

That is notable because the long buildup has survived several large swings in Cardano’s price. After the extreme positioning seen during earlier cycles, longs have spent the past few years consolidating between roughly 5.8 million and 8.4 million rather than collapsing alongside ADA.

It gives the current support test another layer of context. Price is back near depressed levels, but long positioning suggests a section of the market has continued building exposure through the decline. A recovery from $0.15 would make that long-term accumulation much more relevant than it appears while price is still falling.

Bitfinex ADA longs remain around 7 million. Source: Jesse Peralta via X.

CME Liquidity Adds an Institutional Layer to Cardano

Cardano is also beginning to develop a stronger market-infrastructure story. GSR is providing continuous two-sided liquidity in CME Group’s Cardano spot ADA and Micro Cardano futures markets, improving the depth available to participants trading ADA through regulated venues.

That matters differently from a simple price catalyst. Better two-sided liquidity can make it easier for larger market participants to enter, exit, and hedge positions without relying entirely on offshore crypto exchanges. Over time, that can make ADA more accessible to professional and institutional traders who require deeper and more reliable markets.

From $0.15 to $0.25: What Bulls Need to Prove

Cardano does not need an immediate vertical rally for the outlook to improve. The first job is much simpler: absorb the liquidity around the recent lows, keep the broader $0.14-$0.15 region intact, and begin producing higher lows instead of another continuation leg lower.

That would gradually shift the focus away from defending support and toward recovering lost ground. Once ADA starts reclaiming the upper-$0.10s, $0.20 becomes the first psychological hurdle, while $0.25 carries greater importance because it sits near the first larger target highlighted by the descending-channel setup.

Cardano price is trading around $0.15, down 0.64% in the last 24 hours. Source: Brave New Coin

The move toward $0.25 would therefore be less about one breakout candle and more about Cardano rebuilding structure step by step. If long positioning remains firm and broader market conditions improve at the same time, the recovery would have more behind it than a simple oversold bounce.

Final Outlook: Is Cardano Price Quietly Building a Q4 Base?

Cardano price still looks weak, but the market underneath it is not entirely bearish. Support around $0.15 continues to attract attention, Bitfinex longs have been accumulating for years, and the addition of continuous CME liquidity gives ADA a more developed institutional trading backdrop while price searches for a floor.

For the broader Cardano Price Prediction, the interesting part of Q4 may be whether this period near the lows becomes accumulation rather than another breakdown. If ADA can absorb the remaining liquidity beneath support and begin rebuilding above $0.20, the path toward $0.25 becomes much easier to argue. From there, the larger $0.41 and $0.78 levels would only become relevant if Cardano develops a genuine higher-timeframe trend change.

title: Anthropic’s Claude Ship AI Agent Reviews PRs, Fixes Bugs and Approves Code
summary: Anthropic has launched Claude Ship in beta, extending Claude Code beyond code generation into GitHub pull request reviews, automated fixes, and policy-based approvals.
content:
Skip to content

Anthropic has launched Claude Ship in beta, extending Claude Code beyond code generation into GitHub pull request reviews, automated fixes, and policy-based approvals.

The new workflow combines AI-powered code analysis with agents that address developer feedback, resolve failing checks, and determine whether changes meet a team’s approval requirements. 

Claude Ship (beta) automates PR reviews, fixes issues, and approves changes under team policies to accelerate code delivery. Source: @ClaudeDevs/X

The release targets a growing bottleneck in software development as AI coding tools generate code faster than engineering teams can manually review and approve it.

How Claude Ship Handles GitHub Pull Requests

Claude Ship brings together three components: Code Review, PR Steward, and Claude Approvals. The system is designed to handle different stages of the pull request (PR) process, from identifying potential bugs to resolving issues and determining which changes are eligible for approval.

The Claude Ship workflow combines automated fixes, policy-based approvals, risk checks, and gradual enforcement to protect the main branch. Source: @0xShoopy/X

Code Review, which is already generally available, examines proposed changes against the wider codebase. It uses multiple AI agents to identify potential problems, verify findings, and categorize issues before posting them to GitHub. Teams can select Quick, Standard or Deep review levels depending on the complexity of their projects and the level of scrutiny required.

PR Steward takes over when a pull request receives feedback or encounters problems. The agent works in the cloud to address comments from developers, resolve merge conflicts, and fix failing continuous integration (CI) checks. It can also respond to findings from Code Review and other review tools. After each push, PR Steward explains what it changed and provides instructions for reversing those changes if necessary.

Anthropic has separated these responsibilities from the approval process. PR Steward is designed to fix problems without approving or merging pull requests. Claude Approvals handles that decision through policies established by the development team.

Developers can also direct the agent through GitHub comments. For example, they can use @claude to provide additional instructions or @claude stop to pause its activity.

Team Policies Determine Which Changes Claude Can Approve

Claude Approvals introduces an automated sign-off process based on rules maintained inside a repository. Anthropic describes the approach as similar to a more advanced CODEOWNERS file, allowing engineering teams to define approval requirements beyond basic file ownership.

The policy can determine which changes qualify for automated approval and which require human involvement. Teams can use custom classifiers written in natural language, consider Code Review findings, and specify how many people must approve particular changes. Sensitive code can remain subject to mandatory human sign-off, even when routine updates qualify for automated approval.

Anthropic recommends initially running Claude Approvals in observe-only mode. During this phase, the agent evaluates pull requests and reports its decisions without granting approvals. Teams can compare those decisions with their existing review process before enabling enforcement.

GitHub branch protection and required checks remain part of the process. Repository permissions and established rules continue to govern what can be merged, helping organizations introduce AI-assisted approvals without removing their existing controls.

Anthropic Reports Faster Code Reviews and More Merged PRs

Claude Ship builds on Anthropic’s internal experience using AI agents to review code written by both developers and other AI systems. The company has increasingly relied on Claude for its own software development, creating a need to handle code reviews at a similar pace.

Now available for GitHub repositories on Claude Team and Enterprise, with admin-controlled repo-wide automation. Source: @ClaudeDevs/X

In an October engineering blog post, Anthropic said merged pull requests for the Claude Code codebase more than doubled between June and September 2026. The company also reported that the share of merged changes that required reverts fell by more than 40% during that period.

The figures reflect Claude’s role in a wider internal review process rather than the performance of Claude Ship as an independently tested product. Anthropic also previously reported an increase in the share of internal pull requests receiving substantive review comments, from 16% to 54%, following the introduction of its Code Review system.

These results indicate how automated analysis can increase review coverage while reducing some of the work required from engineering teams. However, the figures are based on Anthropic’s own development environment and should not be interpreted as independently verified performance benchmarks for other organizations.

Human Oversight Remains Part of the Workflow

Anthropic’s engineering team has described a layered approach to reviewing AI-generated code. The internal process includes testing changes before a pull request opens, automated code and security reviews, CI checks, risk-based human approvals, merge queues, and mechanisms for detecting and reversing faulty releases.

The company distinguishes between routine updates and changes that could create wider technical or security problems. Documentation changes and low-risk updates may require fewer human approvals, while sensitive areas such as billing systems, software update mechanisms and CI workflows receive additional scrutiny. Anthropic also uses monitoring and rollback procedures because automated reviews cannot eliminate every potential error.

Customer feedback highlighted the intended division of responsibilities. Vatsal Bhatt, Director of Engineering at TELUS Digital, said: “We keep a human in the loop, and the human’s time now goes to the changes that need it.”

The approach reflects Anthropic’s position that AI should take on repetitive review and correction tasks while developers retain responsibility for decisions that require deeper technical judgment. The company also acknowledges that Claude Ship may miss bugs, security vulnerabilities, or other problems.

Availability and How Developers Can Use Claude Ship

Claude Ship is available in beta to customers on Claude Team and Enterprise plans using GitHub repositories. Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals remain in beta.

Individual developers can access the workflow through Claude Code by updating the application and running the /ship command on a prepared change. Claude then pushes the change, opens a pull request, reviews it, and works through feedback and failing checks. The command is rolling out through the Claude Code CLI and desktop application.

Engineering administrators can enable the system across individual repositories without requiring developers to invoke /ship manually. They can choose review levels, determine when automated reviews run, and establish monthly spending limits. Organizations can also introduce the components separately rather than activating the entire workflow immediately.

Claude Ship uses token-based billing, with costs depending on pull request volume, code size, review depth, and the amount of work performed by PR Steward. Anthropic also lists restrictions for organizations using Zero Data Retention, HIPAA configurations, or customer-managed encryption keys.

With Claude Ship, Anthropic is extending AI-assisted software development into the review and approval stages that traditionally depend on engineering teams. Its approach gives organizations more options for handling routine changes automatically while preserving human oversight for decisions that require additional scrutiny.

title: Cardano Adds Brale Stablecoin Issuance With Programmable Controls Across 30 Chains
summary:
Key Takeaways: Cardano is now home to Brale, a live version of regulated USD stablecoins. Stablecoins can be used to pay for businesses for treasury and settlement. CIP-113 adds programmable
The post Cardano Adds Brale Stablecoin Issuance With Programmable Controls Across 30 Chains appeared first on...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Cardano is now home to Brale, a live version of regulated USD stablecoins.
  • Stablecoins can be used to pay for businesses for treasury and settlement.
  • CIP-113 adds programmable compliance controls directly to Cardano-native tokens.

To improve its infrastructure in the stablecoin space, Cardano now introduces Brale, a new platform that will enable payments and treasury applications using stablecoins and new fiat-backed USD tokens to be created by businesses.

The integration also connects Cardano to Brale’s broader infrastructure spanning more than 30 blockchain networks.

Cardano is now live on @Brale_xyz.

Businesses can issue their own USD stablecoin on Cardano, or use stablecoins for settlement, payouts and treasury, and move them across 30 chains.

The integration is built on CIP-113, Cardano’s standard for programmable tokens. https://t.co/DSRBYG0fsB

— Cardano Foundation (@Cardano_CF) November 24, 2026

  • Brale Brings Regulated Stablecoin Issuance to Cardano
  • CIP-113 Adds Rules Directly to the Token
    • Cardano Expands Its Stablecoin Infrastructure
    • Stablecoin Competition on Cardano Is Growing

Brale Brings Regulated Stablecoin Issuance to Cardano

With Brale, businesses can now launch their own dollar-backed stablecoin right on Cardano.

Brale provides netting and redemption, custody, reserve management, compliance and banking integration for the regulatory apparatus of the asset. The company operating the service determines the name of the stablecoin and the stablecoin they’re building.

Companies can also transfer funds from bank accounts to the Cardano ledger and then stake them as settlement tokens or pay out, payroll or cross border as stablecoins.

Businesses already having Brale can integrate Cardano instead by using a prior built integration.

Read More: Cardano and Injective Unlock First Live IBC Link, Bringing ADA and INJ Across Two Ecosystems

CIP-113 Adds Rules Directly to the Token

The rollout is based on CIP-113, Cardano’s standard of programmable tokens. While a simple crypto asset may be transferable once a valid transaction is signed, a CIP-113 token could contain other rules that need to be fulfilled for the move to be accepted.

Those controls can help with functions regulated issuers may want to perform, such as the ability to freeze or seize funds in accordance with the policy of the token. These compliance conditions are instead represented as elements of the token’s onchain logic and not just an element of an external system.

For stablecoin issuers, that opens up the door to layer native assets with transfer programmability and retain blockchain settlement.

Cardano Expands Its Stablecoin Infrastructure

Brale welcomes Cardano on mainnet and testnet, and companies can use the network via its app or API.

A typical flow begins when a customer transfers money in U.S. dollars into their bank account and then transfers the funds to Brale. After this Brale mints the stablecoin to Cardano and transfers that to the target wallet, where this transaction is captured for reconciliation.

Additionally, stablecoins based on its infrastructure can be transacted between over 30 supported blockchain networks, Brale also reports.

Stablecoin Competition on Cardano Is Growing

Over the last 2 years there have been several dollar dominated assets and payment pathways added to Cardano, but Brale brings its own twist: business infrastructure to launch stablecoins.

title: Global Digital Asset and Structured Finance Platform OpenVault Completes $2 Million Seed Round at $20 Million Post-Money Valuation
summary: Round led by HorizonArc Ventures; proceeds to fund AI technology, product expansion, compliance and global growth Global digital asset and structured finance platform OpenVault today announced the completion of a $2 million seed round led by HorizonArc Ventures, with a post-money valuation of $20 mi...
content:
Round led by HorizonArc Ventures; proceeds to fund AI technology, product expansion, compliance and global growth

Global digital asset and structured finance platform OpenVault today announced the completion of a $2 million seed round led by HorizonArc Ventures, with a post-money valuation of $20 million.

The proceeds will be primarily used for AI technology development, product portfolio expansion, compliance infrastructure, and global market growth.

A One-Stop Gateway for Digital Asset Yield

OpenVault is an innovative financial platform focused on digital asset yield management, RWA (real-world assets), and structured financial products. Through its standardized Vault architecture, the platform integrates stablecoin yield, quantitative investment strategies, and diversified asset allocation, providing global users with a transparent, efficient, one-stop digital asset investment gateway.

AI-Powered, Lower Barriers to Entry

Powered by its proprietary AI engine, OpenVault significantly lowers the barrier to participation:

  • AI Smart Recommendation and Auto-Subscription: Based on users’ risk preferences, asset profiles, and market conditions, the system automatically matches and subscribes to suitable products. Users can enable a “stable yield” mode with one click, achieving true set-and-forget management.
  • Stable Yield Product Suite: Includes high-yield stablecoin Vaults, market-neutral quantitative strategies, RWA yield products, and more, with a strong focus on risk control and return stability, designed for users seeking steady capital appreciation.
  • BTC FCN and Other Structured Products: Offers Bitcoin-linked Fixed Coupon Notes (FCN) and other structured financial products, allowing users to capture potential BTC upside while benefiting from downside protection and fixed coupon features, balancing return potential and risk.
  • End-to-End AI-Assisted Management: From product selection and automatic reinvestment to risk monitoring and yield rebalancing, AI is involved throughout the process, greatly improving operational convenience and decision-making efficiency.

Making Structured Finance Accessible

With “standardized Vault + AI-driven” as its core, OpenVault aims to turn complex digital asset and structured finance products into user-friendly tools accessible to ordinary investors. The platform emphasizes asset transparency, strategy traceability, and quantifiable risk control, striving to deliver a more robust and intelligent wealth management experience in the digital asset space.

The crypto trading platform combines the best features of centralized and decentralized exchanges to offer users fast transactions, low trading fees, advanced trading features, and a smooth interface, all without an intermediary, as in centralized exchanges.

The Hyperliquid platform specializes in perpetual futures trading, allowing users to trade crypto derivatives without owning the underlying assets. For developers, Hyperliquid is an Ethereum-compatible smart contract platform (HyperEVM), which enables them to build DeFi applications within its ecosystem.

Additionally, the Hyperliquid protocol has a native cryptocurrency, HYPE. The HYPE token serves as the backbone of the Hyperliquid ecosystem. It plays a key role in governance, staking, and enabling advanced transactions within the HyperEVM.

The table below provides an overview of the Hyperliquid crypto exchange, including its features, founders, and additional details.

About Hyperliquid Crypto Project and Team

Hyperliquid is a DEX designed to combine the speed and user experience of CEXs with the transparency and security of DeFi. The project was co-founded by Jeff Yan and Iliensinc, both Harvard alumni with strong backgrounds in finance and blockchain technology. Jeff Yan has expertise in quantitative trading, while Iliensinc, though pseudonymous, is highly respected for his skills in blockchain infrastructure.

The team also includes members from prestigious institutions, such as Caltech and MIT, as well as professionals from top firms like Citadel and Hudson River Trading. The project prioritizes community, which is reflected in their rejection of venture capital funding, allocating 70% of its tokens to users, and the redistribution of all revenue back to the community.

Start trading on Hyperliquid today and receive a $100 welcome reward to boost your trading capital.

Key Features of Hyperliquid Crypto Exchange

The key features of Hyperliquid crypto exchange are an on-chain order book, gas-free transactions, high leverage trading, liquidity vaults, cross-chain compatibility, and pro-level trading tools.

On-Chain Order Book

Most decentralized exchanges use off-chain order books or automated market makers due to the high throughput required by on-chain order books. However, the platform runs its order book on-chain, providing transparency, security, and speed-optimized transactions through its custom consensus mechanism, HyperBFT, which can confirm up to 200,000 transactions per second using Byzantine Fault Tolerance.

Gas-Free Transactions

Since Hyperliquid operates on its own Layer 1 chain, it controls the entire infrastructure and does not require users to pay gas fees for transactions, unlike Ethereum or other public blockchains. Instead, the platform covers the underlying transaction costs internally and charges users only minimal fees.

High Leverage Trading

Hyperliquid offers up to 40x leverage on perpetual futures contracts, allowing traders to amplify their positions beyond what their actual trading capital can carry. Due to the high risk associated with leverage trading, this feature is particularly tailored to experienced traders who are familiar with the strategy and want to increase their profit potential from rapid market movements.

Liquidity Vaults

Liquidity vaults on Hyperliquid are created by individuals or entities who want to share their trading strategies with others. Users can deposit funds into these vaults and earn a share of the profits or losses based on the vault leader’s trading performance. Aside from user-owned vaults, the Hyperliquid platform features protocol vaults, such as the Hyperliquidity Provider (HLP) Vault, which acts as a market maker and liquidation mechanism, earning a portion of the trading fees.

Cross-Chain Compatibility

Previously, users had to bridge into Arbitrum before accessing Hyperliquid. With the recent Router Nitro Integration, Hyperliquid now supports single‑step deposits from over 30 blockchains, including major EVM chains (Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, Polygon, etc.) and non‑EVM networks like Solana, Sui, Tron. This integration eliminates the previous process that required traders to bridge funds through Arbitrum before accessing Hyperliquid.

Pro-level Trading Tools

Another standout feature of Hyperliquid is the advanced trading tools available to traders, which are similar to those used by professional traders on traditional exchanges. This includes features such as the on-chain order book, real-time charts, customizable order types (including limit, market, and stop orders), in-depth market data, and responsive user interfaces, catering to both retail and institutional traders.

What Are the Pros and Cons of Hyperliquid?

The pros of Hyperliquid are listed below:

  • Advanced Trading Features: Hyperliquid offers a wide range of trading options, including spot trading, perpetual trading, pre-launch futures contracts, margin trading, and up to 40x leverage. Additionally, it supports multiple order types, including market, limit, stop market, stop limit, scale, and TWAP orders, providing traders with advanced tools to execute various strategies.
  • Community-Owned Liquidity Pools (Vaults): The Hyperliquid platform features an advanced vault system, where users can open their own vaults or contribute deposits to existing ones, sharing in the profits (about 10%).
  • Fast Transactions on a Custom Layer 1 Blockchain: Hyperliquid operates on its own Layer 1 blockchain, utilizing a proprietary HyperBFT proof-of-stake consensus that enables up to 200,000 transactions per second, with near-instant finality and very low latency.
  • Low Fees and No Gas Charges on Trades: Thanks to its PoS consensus and efficient design, Hyperliquid charges very low maker (0.045%) and taker (0.015%) fees and eliminates gas fees for trading transactions, significantly reducing trading costs compared to most other decentralized exchanges.
  • Broad Asset Support and Cross-Chain Bridging: The platform supports over 100 assets, including major cryptocurrencies like BTC, ETH, AVAX, SOL, and SUI. It also offers multiple bridges (Arbitrum Bridge, Synapse, HyBridge) to facilitate cross-chain transfers, enhancing liquidity and user flexibility.
  • User-Friendly Experience with One-Click Trading: The Hyperliquid decentralized perpetual exchange simplifies trading with one-click order execution and wallet connection. This helps to avoid repeated confirmations and streamlines the trading experience, similar to centralized platforms.
  • Governance and Community Focus: The native HYPE token enables governance participation and incentivizes trading activity. The platform is community-oriented, rejecting venture capital funding and reinvesting profits in users, which solidifies a more user-focused ecosystem.

The cons of Hyperliquid are listed below:

  • Limited Withdrawal Options: Currently, USDC is the primary cryptocurrency supported for withdrawals. If you wish to withdraw another cryptocurrency or stablecoin from Hyperliquid, you will first need to convert it to USDC. 
  • Centralization: Although Hyperliquid claims to be fully decentralized, some have criticized Hyperliquid for its relatively centralized structure. Critics argue that the protocol is not truly decentralized in comparison to other Layer-1 blockchain networks like Ethereum. 
  • Systemic Risk and Operational Concerns: The platform has faced criticism over incidents such as the JELLY token controversy, where a large trader’s actions resulted in substantial losses for liquidity providers. Critics argue that mixed vaults expose users to systemic risk and that unrestricted position sizes allow potential manipulation.

What are Hyperliquid Supported and Restricted Countries?

Hyperliquid is accessible in major global markets, including the United Kingdom, Singapore, South Africa, Hong Kong, France, Nigeria, Australia, Vietnam, and many others, spanning over 180 countries. Users in these supported countries can trade over 100 crypto assets on the platform without requiring Know Your Customer (KYC) verification.

Aside from these supported countries, Hyperliquid explicitly restricts users in the following countries and regions from using Hyperliquid’s app:

  • United States, including all US states and territories.
  • Ontario, Canada
  • Sanctioned Territories, including jurisdictions subject to economic sanctions or export control laws not named in the Terms, such as Russia, North Korea, Iran, Cuba, and Syria.

These restrictions apply regardless of citizenship or physical presence, meaning individuals or entities residing, incorporated, or operating in these regions are barred from accessing Hyperliquid’s platform interface.

What Are Hyperliquid Trading Fees?

Hyperliquid trading fees are based on your rolling 14-day cumulative trading volume and are assessed at the end of each day in UTC. All sub-account volume on Hyperliquid contributes to the master account’s total, and all accounts share the same fee tier. Vault volume is calculated separately. Referral discounts and rewards apply only to your first $25 million in trading volume.

Having said that, Hyperliquid trading fees include perps fee tiers, spot fee tiers, staking tiers, and maker rebates. Here’s a breakdown of these trading fees:

Perps Fee Tiers

Perps fee tiers are variable trading fees applied to perpetual futures contracts based on your 14-day trading volume. Depending on your category and total trading volume, you can expect your taker and maker fees to decrease. The categories include Base rate, Diamond, Platinum, Gold, Silver, Bronze, and Wood. Start trading with low fees on Hyperliquid. Get fee discounts and a 30% cashback on all your trading fees.

By staking Hyperliquid’s native token (HYPE), you qualify for trading fee discounts. The more you stake, the higher your discount tier, up to a maximum discount of 40%.
