title: Microsoft’s ‘Code Red’ Exposes Crypto’s Own Cloud Problem
summary: Key takeaways Microsoft has reportedly declared a “Code Red” to overhaul its engineering and crisis response after a global outage on November 12-13 that lasted about 24 hours. Coinbase’s May outage was traced to a cooling failure in an AWS data center: all five matching engine nodes were in the sam...
content:
Key takeaways

  • Microsoft has reportedly declared a “Code Red” to overhaul its engineering and crisis response after a global outage on November 12-13 that lasted about 24 hours.
  • Coinbase’s May outage was traced to a cooling failure in an AWS data center: all five matching engine nodes were in the same building, and three went offline, disrupting trading, deposits and withdrawals for about eight hours.
  • Moving assets off exchanges does not remove the reliance on centralized infrastructure, because wallets often depend on third-party RPC providers rather than the user’s own node.
  • The issue is not that crypto firms use the cloud but whether they have credible alternatives when it fails, as more assets move onto blockchains.

Microsoft has reportedly declared a “Code Red” initiative to overhaul its engineering and crisis response following a global service outage that lasted approximately 24 hours. For an industry built around the idea of decentralization, crypto has good reason to pay attention.

According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters, the technology giant is reconsidering how it prevents and responds to major infrastructure failures after its November 12-13 outage disrupted businesses, government operations and financial firms.

Crypto likes to position itself as an alternative to centralized infrastructure. Yet some of its largest businesses depend on the same handful of cloud computing companies, and the consequences of that reliance have already been felt by traders.

How A Cooling Failure Brought Coinbase Trading To A Halt

In May, Coinbase experienced an infrastructure failure that demonstrated how surprisingly fragile access to cryptocurrency markets can be.

The exchange’s official incident report, published on June 1, traced the disruption to a cooling equipment failure inside an Amazon Web Services (AWS) data center.

Coinbase had five matching engine nodes located within the same building. Three went offline during the incident, leaving the system without enough functioning nodes to operate normally.

The exchange had not implemented an automated mechanism to switch its matching engine to another availability zone.

A separate failure involving AWS’s managed event-streaming infrastructure complicated the recovery further.

For approximately eight hours, customers experienced severe disruptions affecting trading, deposits and withdrawals. Restoring the remaining systems took roughly another 12 hours.

“

“The duration of the outage is unacceptable to us,” Coinbase acknowledged in its subsequent investigation.

Coinbase · June 1 incident report

This was not the first time the exchange had encountered such problems. An AWS outage in October 2025 resulted in three hours and 17 minutes of degraded performance for Coinbase customers.

Despite these incidents, the relationship between cryptocurrency businesses and cloud providers continues to deepen. More recently, Coinbase and AWS partnered to bring x402 payments to CloudFront publishers, bringing blockchain-based payments into existing web infrastructure.

The uncomfortable part is that the blockchains themselves did not need to fail for customers to lose access to exchange services.

A decentralized settlement network is of limited immediate use to someone whose assets are sitting inside an exchange they cannot access.

Your Crypto Wallet May Be Less Decentralized Than You Think

Moving assets away from centralized exchanges does reduce some of these risks. However, it does not necessarily eliminate reliance on centralized infrastructure.

Consider an Ethereum wallet.

When a user opens the application to check their balance or send a transaction, the wallet generally communicates with an Ethereum node through a remote procedure call, commonly known as an RPC.

That connection allows the application to retrieve blockchain information and submit signed transactions.

How a wallet app connects to Ethereum through an RPC connection.

Many users rely on infrastructure operated by third-party providers rather than running their own nodes. If the provider becomes unavailable, the wallet may struggle to display balances or broadcast transactions, even while Ethereum continues producing blocks.

In an RPC service outage, the assets can remain intact on the blockchain even when the wallet’s usual connection to the network stops working.

Ethereum’s own node documentation acknowledges that widespread reliance on cloud hosting could introduce a common point of failure.

Distribution of Ethereum nodes.

The distribution of Ethereum nodes also raises questions about infrastructure concentration. Having thousands of independently operated nodes does not necessarily eliminate shared dependencies if many rely on the same hosting providers.

Hosting of Ethereum nodes across providers.

Shared infrastructure can create security risks as well as availability problems. NewsBTC previously covered the debate over verifier and RPC security following the KelpDAO exploit. That incident was an exploit, not a routine cloud outage.

There are alternatives. Users can connect compatible wallets to another RPC provider or operate their own Ethereum nodes. Developers can also design applications to switch between independently operated infrastructure providers when one becomes unavailable.

But these options are not always obvious to the average person opening a wallet on their phone.

The industry has spent years making crypto easier to use, often by hiding much of its technical complexity. In doing so, it has sometimes reintroduced the dependencies that blockchain technology was intended to reduce.

Centralization Is Sometimes A Deliberate Engineering Choice

It would be easy to criticize every cryptocurrency company that uses Amazon, Google or Microsoft infrastructure. The reality is more complicated.

Coinbase explained that keeping its matching engine nodes physically close together was a deliberate decision intended to meet the speed and capacity requirements of its markets.

Separating those systems introduces communication delays. Running redundant infrastructure also costs money, particularly when companies must synchronize large amounts of financial information across multiple locations.

Cloud computing providers offer considerable engineering resources and operational capabilities that smaller crypto companies would struggle to reproduce independently.

The problem is not simply that crypto businesses use centralized services. It is whether they have credible alternatives when those services fail.

Coinbase subsequently outlined plans to improve recovery across availability zones and conduct regular failover exercises in production environments.

Those are useful commitments, although publishing a recovery plan and successfully executing one during an unexpected outage are two different things.

What Microsoft’s Code Red Means For Crypto

There is no established evidence that Microsoft’s latest initiative was prompted by a failure of cryptocurrency networks. The relevance lies elsewhere.

As financial institutions bring more assets onto blockchains, the reliability of the infrastructure connecting investors to those networks becomes increasingly important.

A tokenized investment fund may exist on a distributed ledger, but investors can still depend on centralized custody providers, banking services, identity verification systems and applications to manage their holdings.

A decentralized exchange may execute trades through smart contracts, but its website and the infrastructure connecting users to those contracts can introduce separate vulnerabilities.

Crypto companies should be demonstrating how their products behave when their preferred infrastructure provider goes offline. Can users still submit transactions? Can traders cancel orders? Can another operator take over without waiting for an engineering team to intervene?

Microsoft’s reported response to its November outage is a reminder that even companies with enormous technical resources can discover weaknesses in systems they previously considered reliable.

Crypto does not need to abandon cloud computing. It needs to stop treating decentralization at the blockchain level as proof that everything built around it is equally resilient.

title: BlackRock Launches Hong Kong Tokenized Fund With A HK$10 Entry Point
summary: Key takeaways BlackRock has launched its first tokenized money market fund in Asia-Pacific, the HKD Digital Liquidity Fund, for investors in Hong Kong. The tokenized D OnChain class lists a minimum investment of HK$10, against HK$10 million for the conventional I class, but access through stablecoin...
content:
Key takeaways

  • BlackRock has launched its first tokenized money market fund in Asia-Pacific, the HKD Digital Liquidity Fund, for investors in Hong Kong.
  • The tokenized D OnChain class lists a minimum investment of HK$10, against HK$10 million for the conventional I class, but access through stablecoins is reportedly limited to professional investors.
  • The fund gives HKDAP, the Hong Kong dollar stablecoin issued by Anchorpoint Financial, a use beyond payments, while the returns still come from the underlying short-term instruments.
  • Tokenization does not remove dealing deadlines or redemption limits, and the disclosures reviewed did not yet give total fund assets or current yields.

BlackRock has launched its first tokenized money market fund in Asia-Pacific, giving investors in Hong Kong a new way to move money between traditional investments and blockchain-based financial products.

The BlackRock tokenized fund, known formally as the HKD Digital Liquidity Fund, supports both conventional and tokenized investment units. It also introduces a use case for HKDAP, the Hong Kong dollar stablecoin issued by Standard Chartered-led Anchorpoint Financial.

The development follows Anchorpoint’s plans to expand HKDAP to Solana, announced in late October.

However, there is an interesting detail in BlackRock’s product disclosures. One of the fund’s tokenized classes requires a minimum investment of just HK$10, while access through stablecoins is reportedly limited to professional investors.

The technology may be making financial products more accessible, but the institutions behind them still decide who gets through the door.

What BlackRock’s New Tokenized Fund Actually Offers

BlackRock announced regulatory authorization for the fund on September 10, with its product listings identifying November 16 as the inception date. The commercial launch was reported on Tuesday, November 24.

Unlike many of the investment products available across decentralized finance, BlackRock’s fund does not depend on cryptocurrency lending, liquidity pools or token incentives to generate returns.

Its investment strategy revolves around short-term financial instruments, including government-backed securities and bank deposits.

Investors gain exposure to those assets through fund units. With tokenized units, blockchain technology is used to maintain ownership records.

BlackRock’s official product disclosure lists a minimum initial investment of HK$10 for its D OnChain class, alongside a management fee of 0.31% and daily income distributions.

BlackRock product disclosure for the HKD Digital Liquidity Fund. Source: BlackRock.

For comparison, the fund’s conventional I class requires a minimum initial investment of HK$10 million.

The difference is substantial, although a lower investment minimum should not be confused with unrestricted access. Different share classes and distribution channels come with their own conditions.

A Stablecoin That Can Finally Do More Than Move Money

Perhaps the most interesting part of BlackRock’s launch is what it means for HKDAP.

Anchorpoint Financial, a joint venture between Standard Chartered, Animoca Brands and HKT, received its stablecoin issuer licence from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in April.

Until now, much of the discussion surrounding regulated Hong Kong dollar stablecoins has focused on payments, transfers and their potential role in financial infrastructure.

BlackRock’s fund introduces another practical application. Eligible investors can use digital money denominated in Hong Kong dollars to access investments denominated in the same currency.

In its September announcement, BlackRock stated:

“

“Investors will be able to use HKDAP” to subscribe to and redeem investments from the fund.

Imagine a company that already holds HKDAP for operational payments. Instead of leaving all its surplus liquidity in stablecoins, it could potentially move some of that balance into a money market fund and earn investment income while the money is not needed.

The important distinction is that the stablecoin itself is not generating the fund’s returns. The underlying financial instruments are.

Conceptual illustration based on BlackRock’s stated fund structure and digital-cash subscription arrangements. Not a technical settlement architecture or guarantee of immediate redemption.

For stablecoin issuers, this kind of integration could ultimately prove more valuable than simply securing another exchange listing. It gives businesses a reason to hold and use digital cash beyond cryptocurrency trading.

The Blockchain Is Always Open. The Fund Isn’t.

There is still a noticeable difference between what blockchain infrastructure can do and what BlackRock’s product currently offers.

The D OnChain class lists a daily dealing schedule with an 11 AM Hong Kong time trading deadline and settlement on the trade date.

Anyone familiar with decentralized finance will recognize the contrast. A blockchain does not stop processing transactions because a bank has closed or a fund has passed its dealing deadline.

But tokenizing an investment does not automatically change the operating hours, liquidity arrangements or legal obligations of the underlying fund.

BlackRock also warns that technology failures, compromised wallets and disruptions involving blockchain service providers could interfere with investors’ ability to access or redeem their holdings.

Restrictions on redemptions are possible under stressed market conditions, while investors remain exposed to potential capital losses.

These limitations are not necessarily a failure of tokenization. Institutional investors have regulatory, custody and accounting obligations that cannot simply be removed by deploying a smart contract.

Still, if investors ultimately have to work around many of the same deadlines and intermediaries they encounter in traditional finance, the immediate advantages of tokenization become narrower.

Hong Kong Is Building The Infrastructure Around Tokenized Finance

Earlier this month, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority expanded its EnsembleTX settlement initiative to support continuous settlement using tokenized central bank money.

The initiative involves several major financial institutions, including BlackRock, and supports applications involving tokenized deposits and investment funds.

These developments are gradually connecting different parts of the financial system that previously operated separately.

There are now regulated digital currencies, tokenized investment products and settlement infrastructure being developed to move value between them.

However, BlackRock’s latest launch also shows why the size of the tokenization market should not be measured solely by the number of financial products being brought onto blockchains.

The more interesting figures will be how much money actually enters these funds through digital cash, how frequently investors move between the two products and whether those transactions become cheaper or faster.

BlackRock’s product disclosures reviewed for this article did not yet provide usable figures for total fund assets or current yields.

Nor does the launch establish unrestricted access through decentralized exchanges or lending protocols.

Those are the developments worth watching before declaring that tokenized finance has moved beyond institutional adoption and into the hands of ordinary crypto users.

Hong Kong now has another piece of the infrastructure. The next challenge is getting people to use it.

title: Bitcoin Loses $60,000 And Gold Offers No Protection During Its Worst Selloff Since 1982
summary: Key takeaways Bitcoin fell back below $60,000 on Tuesday after a Monday recovery above $64,000, while gold is in its own severe correction. Gold fell 24.6% over the 60 days to November 23, its steepest loss over such a period since 1982. Neither asset pays income while interest-bearing investments l...
content:
Key takeaways

  • Bitcoin fell back below $60,000 on Tuesday after a Monday recovery above $64,000, while gold is in its own severe correction.
  • Gold fell 24.6% over the 60 days to November 23, its steepest loss over such a period since 1982.
  • Neither asset pays income while interest-bearing investments look more attractive, and selling gold does not automatically send money into Bitcoin.
  • The October PCE report on November 25 is the next test: the previous reading showed headline inflation of 3.6% and core inflation of 3.1%.

The Bitcoin price fell back below $60,000 on Tuesday, cutting short a recovery that had taken the cryptocurrency above $64,000 a day earlier. But perhaps the more troubling development for investors is happening outside the crypto market.

Gold is going through a severe correction of its own, leaving investors in two assets often associated with wealth preservation facing substantial losses.

This is not the first time Bitcoin and gold have struggled simultaneously. What makes the current environment particularly difficult is that neither asset generates income at a time when interest-bearing investments offer an increasingly attractive alternative.

The question is no longer simply whether Bitcoin is digital gold. It is whether investors have enough reason to own either asset under current monetary conditions.

Gold’s Selloff Exposes A Bigger Problem For Bitcoin

The selling extended well beyond Bitcoin. Figures from the World Gold Council show that Bitcoin lost 13.7%, gold fell 8.3% and the Nasdaq dropped 10%, while the US Dollar Index gained 0.4%. The numbers point to a broader reduction in risk exposure rather than a selloff specific to crypto.

Weekly performance through November 20, 2026. Source: Bloomberg / World Gold Council, Weekly Markets Monitor, November 23, 2026.

Gold declined 24.6% over the 60 days ending November 23, its steepest loss over such a period since 1982.

The World Gold Council’s latest market assessment, published on Monday, identified several risks facing the precious metal, including pressure on leveraged equity and credit positions, restrictive monetary policy and the possibility of another disappointing US inflation report.

The organization also identified the lack of a clear reduction in speculative positioning as a concern.

This matters for Bitcoin because the argument for buying BTC during a gold correction often assumes that capital leaving one scarce asset will eventually find its way into the other.

There is little reason to assume that happens automatically.

An investor selling gold to reduce leverage or meet a margin requirement is unlikely to replace that exposure immediately with Bitcoin. The priority is raising cash, not finding another store of value.

There is also a difference between selling an asset because its investment thesis has deteriorated and selling because the cost of maintaining a position has become too expensive. The latter can create opportunities for patient buyers, but it rarely provides a reliable indication of when a market will bottom.

Bitcoin’s Recovery Is Still Missing Conviction

Monday’s trading session offered Bitcoin investors some encouragement. The cryptocurrency recovered above $64,000 following the previous week’s decline to its lowest levels in roughly two years.

The move did not hold.

Bitcoin (BTC) price, September 1 to November 21. Source: Coinglass.

The broader picture is hardly encouraging. Bitcoin has lost nearly 24% over the past three months, falling from a period high of $86,578 to a low of $58,178. Although BTC has since recovered above $60,000, the bounce has done little to change the broader downward trend.

Tuesday’s return below $60,000 raises questions about the strength of the recovery, particularly given the improvement in technology stocks during Monday’s session.

If Bitcoin struggles to sustain gains when conditions improve elsewhere, investors should be careful about assuming that another equity market rally will necessarily pull BTC higher.

There is also an important distinction between a recovery driven by fresh buyers and one driven by traders closing profitable short positions. Both can produce impressive green candles. Only the former demonstrates that investors are willing to commit new capital at higher prices.

Spot trading activity, ETF subscriptions and derivatives positioning will offer a better indication of which type of recovery the market is experiencing.

For now, the failure to retain Monday’s gains makes the rebound less convincing than its initial size suggested.

Does This Undermine Bitcoin’s Digital Gold Thesis?

Bitcoin’s recent performance will inevitably revive criticism of its role as a store of value. However, gold’s own losses make that argument considerably less straightforward.

The metal has been used to preserve wealth for centuries, yet it remains vulnerable to changes in interest rates, investor positioning and the strength of the US dollar.

Bitcoin shares some of those vulnerabilities while carrying considerably different market risks, including its dependence on speculative demand and the availability of leverage across cryptocurrency exchanges.

That does not invalidate Bitcoin’s scarcity argument. Its supply characteristics have not changed because its market price has fallen.

What the current correction does challenge is the assumption that scarcity alone guarantees protection during financial stress.

An asset can have a credible long-term investment case and still be a poor short-term hedge. Bitcoin investors would benefit from separating those two propositions rather than defending both every time the market declines.

The Next Test Comes From The Federal Reserve’s Preferred Inflation Measure

The immediate focus now turns to Wednesday’s US inflation release.

The Bureau of Economic Analysis is scheduled to publish its October personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report on November 25. The previous release showed annual headline PCE inflation of 3.6%, with core inflation at 3.1%.

US personal income and outlays data. Source: Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA).

Another stronger-than-expected reading could reinforce expectations of restrictive monetary policy, making conditions more difficult for assets that rely heavily on capital appreciation.

A softer reading, particularly if accompanied by falling Treasury yields, could offer some relief to both Bitcoin and gold.

For Bitcoin, however, recovering $60,000 should be treated as a starting point rather than confirmation of a broader reversal. Monday’s trading high above $64,000 represents a more demanding test of whether buyers are prepared to return.

Until that happens, the market has demonstrated that it can bounce. It has yet to demonstrate that it can sustain a recovery.

What is BingX?

BingX is a cryptocurrency exchange that offers multiple trading services and employs robust security measures, allowing traders to buy, sell, and trade digital assets with peace of mind.

The platform is most popular for offering copy trading services and social trading features that allow users to earn passive income. This is especially beneficial for traders who are unsure of their trading skills and would rather earn passive income with the assets.

Let’s look at BingX from a glance: here is a detailed summary of the trading platform, covering its founder, year of establishment, geographic restrictions, features, and more.  

Exchange BingX
Founded2018
Founder Josh Lu
Features
  • Spot Trading
  • Copy Trading
  • Grid trading bots
  • BingX Wealth, and 
  • P2P marketplace
Margin Trading Yes
Leverage Up to 150X
Trading Fees0.1% maker/taker for spot, 0.02% maker, and 0.05% taker for futures trading.

  • Two-factor authentication (2FA)

Supported Cryptocurrencies and Available Trading Pairs900+ cryptocurrencies and over 1000 trading pairs.
Accepted Payment MethodsCredit cards, Apple and Google Pay, bank transfers, and direct crypto deposits.
Device Compatibility Mobile and desktop.
Restricted Countries Saudi Arabia, United States, Netherlands, Iceland, New Zealand, China, Japan, Luxembourg, Bosnia, and Norway.

What Are the Pros of BingX?

BingX pros are:

  • Passive Income: BingX offers opportunities for users to earn passive income through the social trading service.
  • Simple Interface: The platform is simple and easy to use for beginners, and users can explore their trading account which has a standard TradingView.
  • Reliable in Terms of Compliance: BingX is available in over 100 countries, including Australia, Germany, and Russia.
  • Demo Trading: BingX offers a pre-funded trading simulator that allows you to practice trading without putting your money on the line. 
  • Copy Trading Feature: On BingX, you can choose to copy the trading strategies of experienced traders to maximize your profits. The platform has about 17,000 elite traders with detailed profile overviews to help you make the right choice.
  • Know Your Customer Verification: The KYC verification process is optional on BingX. In fact, there’s little difference between what verified and unverified users can do on the platform. The main difference is the withdrawal limits and discounts on trading fees.
  • BingX customer support is available 24/7.
  • Mandatory Test: To start trading derivatives on BingX, users must pass a specific test to ensure they don’t blow up their funds.
  • Supports 900+ Crypto and over 1000 Trading Pairs: BingX currently has a large selection of 925 cryptocurrencies and over 1204 trading pairs.

What Are the Cons of BingX?

BingX cons are:

  • No Leverage for Spot Trading: BingX does not offer leverage for spot trading, so you cannot amplify your trades to get better earnings. This is because using higher leverage can lead to higher rewards, though with higher associated risks.
  • High Withdrawal Fees: Withdrawal fees on BingX are relatively high compared to the market average. For instance, the cost of withdrawing USDT through ERC20 is higher than that of most exchanges. So, we do not recommend trading with small amounts on BingX to avoid giving up a chunk of your money to withdrawal fees.
  • No Fiat Money: BingX does not allow traders to directly exchange crypto for fiat or vice versa. However, you can use stablecoins, like USDT, which is tied to the US dollar.

What Are the Best Features of BingX?

The Best Features of BingX include Futures and Spot trading, Copy trading, Grid Trading Bots, Crypto Staking, and a P2P marketplace to help users complete transactions with one another. Now, let’s walk through the details of these features and how you can use them to maximize your crypto investment.

Spot and Futures Trading

In Spot markets, users can buy and sell cryptocurrencies for immediate delivery while enjoying profits or incurring losses directly from changes in the cryptocurrency value. On BingX, spot trading supports two types of orders: Market orders and Limit orders.

The first is a type of order in which you execute a buy or sell order immediately at the best price in the current market for fast trading. Meanwhile, Limit orders are a type of order where you can set the amount and the highest buy price or lowest sell price you can take.

When the market price matches your expectations, the system will automatically execute the order at the best price within the limit price range you set.

Here’s an example of how the two order types on BingX’s Spot Market work:

If you place a market order to buy ETH at the current market price, 3700 USDT. You can simply set the amount you want (e.g 100 USDT). The order will then be filled immediately when you initiate the transaction.

On the other hand, if you want to buy ETH at a lower price of 3500 USDT and the last price was 3700, you can choose the limit order and set the buy price at 3500 USDT. The limit order will be filled when the price of the coin drops to 3500 USDT. The same goes for selling crypto at a higher price than the current market price.

BingX also provides a Futures Trading Interface, which allows users to trade against the future price of a particular token while amplifying earnings through leverage.

For futures on BingX, you can either go long (buy) or short (sell) a trading pair to capitalize on the market price volatility. The trading platform provides two types of futures trading: Standard Futures and Perpetual Futures (USDT-M and Coin-M).

  1. Standard Futures Contracts

These contracts have a set expiration date on which a trader can agree to buy or sell a specific digital asset at a predetermined price. It is ideal for inexperienced traders; the trading interface is straightforward, intuitive, and easy to navigate.

Also, transactions on the Standard Futures Market are concluded quickly, making it perfect for investors who are currently on a tight budget.

  1. Perpetual Futures Contracts

Perpetual futures contracts do not have expiration dates, and you can hold them as long as you want to maximize your profits. BingX offers two margin modes in their perpetual futures market: USDT-margined (USDT-M) and Coin-margined (Coin-M). USDT-M.

That being said, the next question is, which one is best for you? Well, it depends on your experience and requirements, but here’s a guide on how to select between the Standard and Perpetual Futures trading on BingX.

Choose standard futures:

  • If you are new to futures.
  • If you need fast order execution.
  • If you prefer a more straightforward and faster trading process.
  • If you are interested in trading foreign currencies, international indices, and commodities.
  • If you would like to experiment with standard Coin-M futures.

Choose perpetual futures:

  • If you already have experience in trading futures.
  • If you invest large amounts of money in crypto.
  • If you need to trade without slippage when opening/closing positions.
  • If you need a more functional and sophisticated trading interface.
  • If you need greater market depth and higher liquidity.

Whichever one you decide on, BingX has an advanced slippage mechanism that initiates accurate stop losses to prevent you from losing a significant amount of money on trades.

Copy Trading

BingX has one of the best copy trading platforms where users can copy the strategies of more experienced traders to avoid losing your hard earned money. BingX copy trading has over 17,000 professional elite traders divided into categories, like trending traders and conservative traders.

Unlike other crypto exchanges that display minimal information on their Master Traders, BingX’s copy trading feature shows Copiers in-depth information to help them make suitable choices. Copiers can see the traders’ earnings, the number of open positions, the type of account they are using, and their risk ratings.

In addition, you can expand your search to a 6-month range to see the trader’s track record. BingX also provides a comprehensive filter option so you can set your requirements and decide which trader to copy.

Once you select an elite trader you want to copy, any trade they make is automatically replicated in your account. You also don’t have to worry about losses because BingX offers a Copy Trading Subsidy Voucher to safeguard your trades. If you incur any losses from Copy Trading, they will be offset based on the amount specified in the voucher.

Grid Trading Bots

BingX’s Grid Trading Bots can automatically buy crypto low and sell high 24/7, according to previously set instructions. These bots are designed to yield returns from market volatility, and they can operate 24/7, eliminating the need for you to constantly monitor your trades.

BingX offers three Grid Trading Bots for different markets, and they include the Futures Grid (amplifying margins and profits), Spots Grid (quick buy and sell), and the Spot Infinity Grid (advanced spot grid).

The Spot Infinity Grid is also known as “Never-Exit-Trades-Early Grid.” Unlike Spot Grid, the Spot Infinity Grid does not require you to set an upper price limit. This helps avoid a common issue in Spot Grid when the price exceeds the upper limit, resulting in missed opportunities.

Spot Infinity Grid, on the other hand, allows users to hold onto their digital assets in a rising market. So, whether you are active or not, and as long as the market fluctuates up or down, you will make more profit than you probably would using the regular Spot Grid.

BingX Wealth

BingX Wealth is an all-in-one asset management service where users earn interest and achieve stable returns on their funds or crypto they are not using at that moment. This feature supports mainstream cryptocurrencies such as USDT, BTC, ETH, XRP, and more.

BingX Wealth offers two main modes of earnings to cater to different users: Flexible Term and Fixed-term. Whether you decide to use the flexible or fixed-term option, here are the benefits of opting for the BingX Wealth program:

  • Capital Preservation: BingX Wealth offers conservative earning options with various product durations that provide stable interest returns.
  • Zero Fees: No fees are charged for subscription and redemption.

  • VIP Exclusive Wealth: VIP users enjoy higher returns and a broader selection of products on BingX Wealth.

P2P Marketplace

Another standout feature that makes BingX popular among users is the social trading interface, which allows inexperienced traders to replicate the trades of seasoned traders.

In addition, the app supports spot trading, futures, and derivatives trading, backed by a TradingView with advanced charting tools and real-time data. BingX also offers various bonuses to users, including daily check-in, first registration, first trade, first deposit immediately after registration, and major promotions.

Many users appreciate the app’s responsiveness, demo accounts, and ease of use, but there have also been concerns regarding high withdrawal fees and delays in fulfilling limit orders. So, consider the limitations regarding fiat-crypto pairs and withdrawal fees before committing to the platform.

What are BingX Fees?

Bingx fees are charged for Spot Trading, Futures Trading, Deposits, and Withdrawals, and they also charge separate fees depending on your VIP level. The platform follows the traditional makers and takers fees, where

  • Maker Fee: You pay this fee when you add liquidity to the market by placing a limit order. These fees are usually lower and apply to limit orders that are not filled immediately.
  • Taker Fee: You pay this fee when you remove liquidity by placing an order that matches an existing order. These fees are higher and are filled immediately.

Here is a breakdown of maker and taker fees for spot and futures trading. We also cover deposit and withdrawal fees, plus discounts for various VIPs:

Spot Trading

The spot trading fee on BingX is 0.10% for both makers and takers. This flat rate applies to most trading pairs available on BingX, including popular ones like BTC/USDT, XRP/USDT, and ETH/USDT.

Futures Trading

Remember that BingX offers two types of contracts in its futures market, so here are the different fees for each of them.

  1. Perpetual

BingX charges 0.02% for makers and 0.05% for takers. The platform charges fees for opening and closing positions. Additionally, they offer a “One Way Trading Mode,” giving users one aggravated position for each digital asset.

For instance, if you open two short positions on XRP, it will add the second to the first, and their opening prices will be added, as well as the lot price. So, if you then open a long position for XRP, it will sell from your shorts instead of opening a separate long position.

Only charges a fee on closing transactions, which is 0.045%. Unlike Perpetual Contracts, which have a one-way trading mode, the Standard Contracts have a Hedge trading mode. This means that no matter how many positions you open and size, all positions will be held separately.

Is BingX Safe and Legit for Trading?

BingX has robust security measures in place, like 2FA, proof of reserve, a fund password for withdrawals, address whitelisting, an encrypted connection, and anti-phishing code to protect users’ digital assets. Here is a breakdown of how the platform’s security features protect users’ funds from fraud attacks or breaches.

  1. 2FA and Multi-factor Authentication

Enabling 2FA on BingX ensures that even if someone gains access to your password, they would need a secondary verification method, usually a unique code sent to your email, to access your account.

Also, the platform offers multiple authentication methods besides 2FA, such as individual fund passwords, account passwords, fingerprint verification (biometrics), and other supporting verification means, including Google authentication.

  1. Proof of Reserve

BingX safeguards user funds, which are 100% backed by reserve funds. Authoritative auditors like Mazars have verified their financial data, and they publish their Merkle Tree on the 1st and 15th of every month.

  1. Address Whitelisting

BingX has a withdrawal whitelist feature that allows cryptocurrency traders to only make withdrawals to the listed wallet address. This prevents authorized withdrawals.

  1. Encrypted Connection

BingX uses secure sockets layer encryption. This means that the platform scrambles the information you send between your browser and its servers to avoid single points of failure.

  1. Anti-phishing Code

The platform offers old and new traders a personal anti-phishing code that appears in all their real emails. This code helps you tell the difference between real emails from BingX and fake ones from fraudsters.

title: MEXC Releases September–October Security Report: Guardian Fund Adds 1,000 BTC, Reserve Ratios Exceed 100%
summary: Mutsamudu, Comoros, November 24, 2026 – MEXC, a pioneer in 0-fee digital asset trading, has released its September–October 2026 security report. The report shows that the MEXC Guardian Fund increased its BTC holdings to 2,000 BTC, while reserve ratios for four major assets—BTC, ETH, USDT, and USDC—r...
content:
Mutsamudu, Comoros, November 24, 2026 – MEXC, a pioneer in 0-fee digital asset trading, has released its September–October 2026 security report. The report shows that the MEXC Guardian Fund increased its BTC holdings to 2,000 BTC, while reserve ratios for four major assets—BTC, ETH, USDT, and USDC—remained above 100%.

The crypto industry faces security challenges across multiple points of exposure. The report recorded 196 security incidents in September–October, with total asset losses exceeding $7.3 billion. Several large-scale incidents involved breaches of exchange wallets and transaction signing systems that enabled unauthorized asset transfers. Attackers used fake recruitment campaigns to persuade employees to download malware, exploited vulnerabilities in third-party tools to steal internal credentials, and distributed phishing links through compromised official accounts. These incidents have drawn greater attention to platforms’ access controls and reserve transparency.

Guardian Fund Adds 1,000 BTC

In September 2026, MEXC allocated an additional 1,000 BTC to the Guardian Fund, marking its second addition of the year. By the end of September, the fund held 2,000 BTC and more than 100 million USDT, maintaining reserves in both BTC and USDT.

The Guardian Fund is designed to support user protection in serious security incidents, including major exploits, targeted attacks, and unforeseen system vulnerabilities. The latest addition follows MEXC’s plan, announced in May 2026, to expand the fund to $500 million within two years. MEXC has published the fund’s holding addresses so users can review on-chain balances and transaction records:

USDT Reserve Address (Ethereum):

  • 0x469AfE803C54A36674C55231489Cf4b61da8c1bC

First BTC Reserve Address:

  • 1MDVjZdX8QD212pT8Z8EMP7DuFQHKqN3mx

Second BTC Reserve Address:

  • 19KYQDpyssRUtpfa4pfAWiNQLeysThd1us

Reserve Ratios Exceed 100% for All Four Assets

MEXC’s October 9, 2026 reserve snapshot showed reserve ratios above 100% for all four major assets disclosed. The BTC reserve ratio stood at 293.86%, with wallet assets of 12,402.93 BTC against user assets of 4,220.56 BTC. The ETH reserve ratio was 110.90%, with wallet assets of 59,691.16 ETH against user assets of 53,820.65 ETH. USDT and USDC reserve ratios were 122.38% and 115.42%, respectively.

Users can review platform wallet and user asset data on the MEXC Proof of Reserves and Asset Protection page and use Merkle tree verification to check whether their account balances are included in that reserve snapshot.

Futures Insurance Fund Reaches 830 Million USDT to Help Cover Liquidation Deficits

As of November 5, 2026, the MEXC Futures Insurance Fund held 830,411,315 USDT. This was an increase of 38,714,893 USDT, or 4.89%, from the September 1 balance disclosed in the previous report.

The Futures Insurance Fund covers deficits caused by insufficient margin during forced liquidation. It provides a financial buffer during sharp market swings and helps reduce the risk of triggering auto-deleveraging (ADL). Users can view the fund balance and historical changes on the MEXC Trust page.

MEXC Returns More Than 1 Million USDT in Erroneous Deposits

MEXC helps users recover assets deposited in error. In September–October, its customer service team manually completed 1,354 returns of erroneous deposits, returning assets worth 1,002,660 USDT. Compared with July–August, the number of completed returns increased 65.5%, while the value of assets returned rose 66.5%.

MEXC CEO Vugar Usi said, “In the AI era, attackers can find vulnerabilities and develop attacks faster. Exchanges must also upgrade their technical defenses, strengthen internal controls, and improve their incident response capabilities. MEXC will continue to invest in security, build up its protection reserves, and regularly report on progress in user protection. Through sustained security investment and transparent disclosure, we aim to build lasting trust with our users.”

About MEXC

Founded in 2018, MEXC is a leading global multi-asset trading platform built as your 0-fee gateway to infinite opportunities. Serving users across 170+ markets, MEXC provides simple and efficient access to crypto, stocks, tokenized assets, derivatives, and a growing range of TradFi-linked opportunities through one account and one gateway.

With 0 trading fees, deep liquidity, broad asset coverage, and a high-performance trading experience, MEXC is designed for retail users who want to discover earlier, act faster, and trade with fewer barriers. As crypto and traditional finance continue to converge, MEXC is committed to making global opportunities more accessible, helping users trade freely and MEXCmize every opportunity.

title: Could Bitcoin’s Price Decline Increase Demand for Stablecoins?
summary:

The post Could Bitcoin’s Price Decline Increase Demand for Stablecoins?  appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
One of the most attractive aspects of cryptocurrency investments has always been associated with the relative liquidity of this marketplace. However, this silver lining can often be obscured by a cloud of volatility. The fact that Bitcoin has tested its lowest levels since April 2026 clearly signals that a readjustment may be in order. Investors are also worried, as the recent dip below $74,000 might indicate that another round of bearish sentiment is soon to take hold.

Should traders liquidate their current positions? Might it be better to short all cryptocurrencies for the moment? Although there can be arguments made for both of these strategies, we need to remember that hedging is still a very real possibility. Stablecoins pegged to the United States dollar could represent the safest port in this storm, and it pays to take a closer look at why some astute traders are adopting this rather conservative mindset. 

  • How Dollar-Pegged Stablecoins Maintain Their Value 
  • Why Stablecoin Demand May Change During Market Volatility 
  • Stablecoin Use Cases Beyond Cryptocurrency Trading 
  • Risks and Limitations of Stablecoins
  • Conclusion: What Bitcoin Volatility Could Mean for Stablecoin Demand 

How Dollar-Pegged Stablecoins Maintain Their Value 

As the name already suggests, stablecoins are often capable of superseding (at least to an extent) some of the volatility that can be attributed to open-market crypto volatility. This arises from how they function. Unlike other tokens, stablecoins are directly pegged to the dollar at roughly $1 per coin. Note that they may also be linked to other US assets, such as short-term treasuries. So what happens if the price begins to dip?

Assuming that the value of a stablecoin, such as USDC, dramatically falls below its $1 value, arbitrageurs will often choose to purchase these tokens at a lower value. This serves two primary purposes:

  • It enables them to become involved on a dip (securing potentially higher profit margins)
  • Large-scale purchases help to boost prices back to a relative 1:1 parity. 

However, there is another reason why stablecoins represent attractive assets during times of uncertainty. 

Why Stablecoin Demand May Change During Market Volatility 

One of the misconceptions that has been attributed to cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin is the belief that the sheer value of this asset makes it somewhat immune to short-term price swings. The recent performance of Bitcoin should clearly illustrate otherwise. The fact of the matter is that the vast majority of crypto tokens, and meme coins, are affected by several variables. These include market sentiment, supply, demand, speculation, and sudden cascading liquidations.

Stablecoins function in a slightly different manner. Thanks to their inherent relationship with the dollar, they can be used as a more “stable” medium of exchange when other tokens may begin to exhibit pear-shaped movements. 

Stablecoin Use Cases Beyond Cryptocurrency Trading 

Another potent argument which stablecoin pundits will often make involves the utilitarian nature of these tokens. For instance, some readers may not be aware that they can often serve as a substitute for fiat when playing online blockchain-based games may offer. Well-known examples include Tether and USD Coin; two options that a growing number of iGaming providers work with.

This is pivotal when it comes to real-world applications. Unlike meme coins, and even a handful of major cryptocurrencies, the fact that stablecoins can now double as viable transfer options has helped to increase demand, and if chart values fall, they are not likely to suffer from a lack of liquidity. 

Risks and Limitations of Stablecoins

Any article discussing the merits of specific cryptocurrencies must seek to adopt a fair, and balanced approach. This is why it is just as logical to highlight some pitfalls that could impact a stablecoin investment. 

Perhaps the most obvious concern involves what would happen if a stablecoin were suddenly de-pegged from its underlying currency. While this is unlikely, another problem has already been illustrated in the past. Some readers may recall the devaluation of USDC once it was discovered that this stablecoin was linked to the failing Silicon Valley Bank. Confidence essentially collapsed, and the value of USDC plummeted. 

A final stumbling block is directly tied to inflation. Cryptocurrencies have been traditionally associated with hedges against inflationary rates. This is not the case with stablecoins due to their relationship with fiat. In other words, the value of tokens can be directly impacted by rising, or falling, inflationary data. If interest rates begin to rise, borrowing costs will follow suit. This makes it more expensive to purchase crypto, and investors are more likely to turn to low-risk positions (such as high-yield savings accounts). 

Conclusion: What Bitcoin Volatility Could Mean for Stablecoin Demand 

We can now see why some astute traders have been turning to stablecoins as a means to offset recent market jitters. However, this does not signify that such assets represent a win-win situation. Risks should always be balanced with potential rewards, and investors should allocate more funds than they are prepared to lose. 

Might Bitcoin continue to fall? Will we soon reach a stable level of support before the end of 2026? This question is on everyone’s mind, and time will tell.
